          "excerpt": "# isolated-attempts — Decisions\n\nClass: architectural (bead coding-harness-s9r; it changes how every writing verb of the runner runs a model and amends the doctrine sentence in `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3). The interview ran in the conversation on 2026-11-22; the answers are recorded below with the options as they were put. Earlier decisions it builds on: the shared design of 2026-10-16 (beads coding-harness-6ie and coding-harness-s9r), the design of 2026-11-12 that folded coding-harness-c99h, -t3s3, -znc and -6ie into this bead, and the retention answer of 2026-11-03 (coding-harness-c99h Q-1).\n\n## Q-1 · Direction: own worktree per attempt, or the three-way comparison\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — open the lane now on the 2026-11-12 design, without the three-way comparison of 2026-10-23; the orchestrator re-checks it against the alternatives.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: how a writing attempt is isolated.\n  Intention: a failed attempt leaves its changes in the lane worktree and the next step trips over them; on 2026-11-22 this happened three times (u1ha, ttic, i76l).\n  Today: every attempt writes in the lane worktree.\n  Repository change: Options: A open now on the 2026-11-12 design (own git worktree per attempt from the fixed base, failed attempt saved as a side ref, fallback builds on it); B after Monday in a block with the maintainer; C first compare worktree, container (Podman/Docker) and k3s/OpenShift.\n  Architecture change: a new attempt lifecycle for all writing verbs.\n\nIn the context of writing attempts that damage the next one, facing a cheap per-attempt worktree or a heavier container or cluster, we decided to build the per-attempt worktree now, to achieve an end to the hand clean-up at the lowest cost, accepting that network access and foreign file reads are not covered by this change. — 2026-11-22\n\nThe orchestrator's re-check: the worktree covers the damage class (lane and runner inputs) at seconds per attempt; a container adds a network lock and blocks foreign reads but needs a Linux VM on macOS and stalled on 2026-10-15 (branch explore/isolated-attempts); k3s/OpenShift is heavier still. A container can later sit on top of the worktree (bead coding-harness-yw2p).\n\n## Q-2 · Threat model\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — an attempt may damage its own worktree in any way (delete, edit, symlink, replace inputs); the lane and every file the runner reads its next prompt from stay untouched; network access and reading foreign files are out of scope, with their own bead (coding-harness-yw2p).\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: which model behaviour the runner must withstand.\n  Intention: the spec states the threat model (bead).\n  Today: no stated mod",

          "excerpt": "## The workflow in one screen\n\n| # | Phase | Artifact | Gate |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Explore | `plans/changes/<name>/research.md` | — |\n| 1a | Interview | `decisions.md` | the class minimums met — feature ≥ 3 · ADR change ≥ 5 (feature with ADR: 5 total) · spike 3 topics or reasoned skip · bounded 1 or reasoned skip — gate `interview-minimums` |\n| 2 | Spec | `spec.md` | validator green, no open `[DECISION]` |\n| 2a | Spec-Review *(optional)* | lines for `findings.md`, dimension SPEC | no open `[AMBIGUITY]` |\n| 2b | Design *(by class)* | `design.md` | validator green; an ADR draft when `architectural` |\n| 3 | Plan | `plan.md` | validator green |\n| 4 | Implement | code + tests | `make verify` green |\n| 4b | Review loop *(stage 2)* | loop rows, into `findings.md` after the phase-6 verdict | rounds until a clean round — the free swarm, the Flash swarm, then the paid ladder (ADR 0021); a targeted check after each runner repair and each orchestrator hand repair, the full `make verify` before phase 6 |\n| 5 | Verify | test output as evidence | stop-hook blocks on a red tree |\n| 6 | Review | `findings.md` | no open BLOCKER — `[DIVERGENT]` counts as BLOCKER |\n| 7 | Commit | pull request | CI green |\n\n**Stage 2** (framework content, ADR 0007 as amended by ADR 0011 and ADR 0016): a foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py`, which runs the leak check before every call. Codex drafts spec, design and plan (`draft <change>`; GLM 5.3 after two failed attempts) and reviews 6; Opus 5.5 reviews 2a (`spec-review <change>`); the review loop (4b) runs on OpenCode Go through Pi until a clean round (ADR 0021): round 1 is the free swarm, the models the `free_stage` rule selects from a forced live catalog refresh, on the implementation diff alone with no tools; round 2 is the Flash swarm, up to three cheapest reachable admitted paid models in parallel; then one id of the `opencode-go` entry's `modelle` set per round, cheapest first: the runner orders it by the declared `anfragen_5h` (requests per 5 hours, more is cheaper); a failed Flash member is replaced by the cheapest unconsumed one. GLM 5.3 Flash explores a `bounded` change or a `spike` (a `feature` or `architectural` change goes to the research swarm, ADR 0020) and implements, and Codex repairs the findings the orchestrator takes (`repair <change>`, ADR 0017: a fresh Codex attempt after a failed post-run check, then Sonnet 5.5; phase 6 re-checks in a fresh read-only Codex session — a reviewer's own session never repairs); `explore <change>`, `draft <change>`, `implement <change>` and `repair <change>` are live;\n`--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5 and records why when Stage 2 is off or Z.ai unavailable.           "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Worktrees — one per change",
          "end_line": 911,
          "excerpt": "### Worktrees — one per change\n\nWritten 2026-09-29 from D-5 (worktrees in the repository, through the tool's own\nmechanism), ADR 0006 (parallel work, one worktree per session) and the\nmeasurement of 2026-09-23 (`docs/research/2026-09-23-worktree-tracker-writes.md`).\nThe same rule holds in `lakeswitch-ai`, with the differences its\n`docs/workflow.md` §9 lists.\n\n1. **One change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.** Two sessions\n   never share a worktree, and nobody switches the branch of the main checkout\n   while another session runs.\n2. **In the repository, under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`.** That directory is in\n   `.gitignore` already, and it is where Claude Code puts its own worktrees\n   (`claude --worktree <name>`, and a sub-agent's `isolation: worktree`). By\n   hand: `git fetch origin && git worktree add -b <branch>\n   .claude/worktrees/<name> origin/main`. `bd worktree create` works as well but\n   writes the worktree's path into the tracked `.gitignore`, which is one more\n   change in the diff. Sibling directories beside the repository are retired\n   (D-5); worktrees that still sit there are finished and removed, not moved.\n3. **Always from a freshly fetched `origin/main`.** A worktree on a stale base\n   produces a pull request that is behind before it opens.\n4. **The tracker needs nothing.** `tools/bd` in a worktree finds the main\n   checkout's tracker through the shared git directory — no variable, no\n   redirect file, no copy. Concurrent writers lose nothing and a contested\n   claim has exactly one winner (measured 2026-09-23 with bd 1.3.0).           "excerpt": "# ADR 0025 — A runner repair passes a targeted check; one full make verify precedes phase 6\n\n* Status: accepted by the merge of the pull request that carries this file.\n  Until that merge, open is proposed and closed is rejected. Amends ADR 0021\n  decision 6; supersedes no ADR. Amends no D- or O-number.\n* Review: the maintainer decided on 2026-11-08, in the conversation, that\n  ADR 0021 decision 6 changes together with the runner change that makes a\n  repair pass on a targeted check (pull request #343, bead\n  coding-harness-gxwg), and that the amendment travels in a decision pull\n  request of its own (answer \"Fertig machen + ADR-PR\"), and answered its\n  interview the same day (`plans/changes/adr-repair-check/decisions.md`,\n  Q-1 to Q-5). Decider: maintainer ·\n  prepared by Claude Code. Acceptance is the merge commit; the review header\n  remains pending.\n* Date: 2026-11-08 · takes effect on merge.\n\n## Context\n\nADR 0021 decision 6 ends \"requiring `make verify` green after repair as\ntoday\". Every runner repair therefore paid for a full `make verify`, even for\na narrow edit. Full checks run one at a time under the machine-wide verify\nadmission (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`, \"One admission per user and machine\"), so a\nrepair cycle waits for the lock and then for the whole suite. The workflow\nrecords a full run at 12 to 13 minutes (measured 2026-10-30); the lane times\nthis decision should shorten are not measured.\n\nThe maintainer had already let a targeted check stand in for a full one after\na hand repair by the orchestrator (2026-10-30, bead coding-harness-24ag). The\nchange `repair-targeted-check` extends that rule to runner repairs and adds an\nenforced full check before phase 6 (`plans/changes/repair-targeted-check/`,\non the branch of #343). Without this amendment the ADR would contradict the\ngate the runner enforces (review-loop row L8-3 of that change; bead\ncoding-harness-firy).\n\n## Decision\n\nADR 0021 decision 6's last sentence is replaced by:\n\n1. After a runner repair the runner runs a targeted check: the tests linked\n   to the touched files, the prior retry selections, ruff on the touched\n   Python files, and the gates the touched file kinds feed.\n2. When that selection is not safe, the full `make verify` runs instead, as\n   the fallback for that repair.\n3. One fresh green full `make verify` on the head under review is required\n   before phase 6. A red, unstartable or timed-out run stops the review;\n   runner audit lines in `findings.md` do not count as a new head.\n4. The orchestrator measures repair duration, verify-lock wait and every\n   failure the full check before phase 6 finds that a targeted check missed,\n   over five changes or two weeks, whichever comes first, and reports the\n   result to the maintainer.\n5. This rule holds from the merge. The testing-strategy spike (bead\n   coding-harness-1ga5) may amend or replace it with an ADR of its own; the\n   measurement of point 4 enters that spike as a finding.\n\nThe rest of ADR 0021 decision 6 stands unchanged.\n\n## Consequences\n\n* A repair cycle no longer waits for a full run unless its selection is\n  unsafe; the effect on cycle and lane times is not yet measured.\n* A targeted check can miss a test the touch map does not link to a touched\n  file.           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen: option (1), with the inference removed, the reverse direction held,\nand the whole gate carried by the kit with a day per repository — because an\nattribution per edit needs the claim where the edit is made, one rule is\neasier to hold than an explicit rule beside a guess, and a workflow rule that\nholds in one repository alone is not a rule of the workflow (Q-1 to Q-5).\n\n**What is decided**, in five points:\n\n1. A change claims, in the header of its own spec, every file under\n   `docs/adr/` it creates, changes or removes. A later change that amends an\n   ADR claims that amendment itself.\n2. An ADR edit belongs to the change of the measured work that claims it. A\n   change that does not claim the file is no owner of it, whatever else the\n   work touches. The owner owes five interview answers of the maintainer,\n   whatever its class and its date.\n3. An ADR edit that no change of the work claims is a finding that names the\n   remedy. Nothing infers an owner from the paths a diff touches or from an\n   ADR's text.\n4. For a feature begun after its repository adopted the gate, the answer \"yes\"\n   comes with at least one claimed ADR file, and the answer \"no\" with none.\n5. The interview gate travels with the kit as mechanism.           "excerpt": "# isolated-attempts — Decisions\n\nClass: architectural (bead coding-harness-s9r; it changes how every writing verb of the runner runs a model and amends the doctrine sentence in `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3). The interview ran in the conversation on 2026-11-22; the answers are recorded below with the options as they were put. Earlier decisions it builds on: the shared design of 2026-10-16 (beads coding-harness-6ie and coding-harness-s9r), the design of 2026-11-12 that folded coding-harness-c99h, -t3s3, -znc and -6ie into this bead, and the retention answer of 2026-11-03 (coding-harness-c99h Q-1).\n\n## Q-1 · Direction: own worktree per attempt, or the three-way comparison\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — open the lane now on the 2026-11-12 design, without the three-way comparison of 2026-10-23; the orchestrator re-checks it against the alternatives.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: how a writing attempt is isolated.\n  Intention: a failed attempt leaves its changes in the lane worktree and the next step trips over them; on 2026-11-22 this happened three times (u1ha, ttic, i76l).\n  Today: every attempt writes in the lane worktree.\n  Repository change: Options: A open now on the 2026-11-12 design (own git worktree per attempt from the fixed base, failed attempt saved as a side ref, fallback builds on it); B after Monday in a block with the maintainer; C first compare worktree, container (Podman/Docker) and k3s/OpenShift.\n  Architecture change: a new attempt lifecycle for all writing verbs.\n\nIn the context of writing attempts that damage the next one, facing a cheap per-attempt worktree or a heavier container or cluster, we decided to build the per-attempt worktree now, to achieve an end to the hand clean-up at the lowest cost, accepting that network access and foreign file reads are not covered by this change. — 2026-11-22\n\nThe orchestrator's re-check: the worktree covers the damage class (lane and runner inputs) at seconds per attempt; a container adds a network lock and blocks foreign reads but needs a Linux VM on macOS and stalled on 2026-10-15 (branch explore/isolated-attempts); k3s/OpenShift is heavier still. A container can later sit on top of the worktree (bead coding-harness-yw2p).\n\n## Q-2 · Threat model\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — an attempt may damage its own worktree in any way (delete, edit, symlink, replace inputs); the lane and every file the runner reads its next prompt from stay untouched; network access and reading foreign files are out of scope, with their own bead (coding-harness-yw2p).\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: which model behaviour the runner must withstand.\n  Intention: the spec states the threat model (bead).\n  Today: no stated model; each repair closed one case (codex-repairs F-8, F-10..F-14).\n  Repository change: Options: A lane and runner inputs only; B also block foreign file reads without a container; C container from the start.\n  Architecture change: none beyond Q-1.\n\nIn the context of the threat model, facing a narrow or a wide scope, we decided to protect the lane and the runner's inputs only, to achieve a small change that can be built and checked in days, accepting that network and foreign reads wait for the container bead. — 2026-11-22\n\n## Q-3 · Environment in the attempt worktree\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — the attempt worktree links the lane's .venv and installed Pi; a lane without them is refused before the model call with the remedy (make venv, tools/pi/install.sh); the runner checksums the shared environment before and after each attempt and rejects the attempt on a difference.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: where an attempt worktree gets its Python environment and Pi.\n  Intention: without the pinned Pi about 110 tests fail and an attempt goes red for an environment reason (0zhf attempts 2 and 3, 2026-11-22).\n  Today: the lane worktree carries both.\n  Repository change: Options: A link the lane's environme",

          "excerpt": "## Sessions across checkouts\n\n- **Another session in the same checkout:** say so before changing a file,\n  committing or switching the branch, and offer a worktree. House rule 4 holds\n  for the tracker meanwhile.\n- **Worktrees: one change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.**\n  A worktree lives under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`, is branched from a freshly fetched `origin/main`,\n  and is removed after the merge; tracker access, claims and sibling directories: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3.\n  Each new checkout or worktree runs `make venv` and `bash tools/pi/install.sh` once before `make verify`\n  (`PYTHON=` picks a 3.12+ interpreter; one that does not match the lock fails the suite, bead\n  coding-harness-ei0; the Pi tests and the swarms need the pinned Pi, bead coding-harness-hs0o).\n- **A text-only change (Markdown outside `scripts/`, `tests/`, `prompts/`,\n  `decisions/`) skips the local `make verify`;** CI is its gate.\n- **Omnigent starts inside the worktree** (ADR 0006). Its default policy (`tools/omnigent/`) is a second layer;\n  nothing depends on it alone. Which tools are denied or asked, and why: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3, \"Worktrees\".\n- **What could not be read is \"not read\", never \"none\"** — an unopened file\n  and an empty query say different things.\n- **A standing rule belongs in the repository's `AGENTS.md`** — every harness\n  reads it; chat, memory and a user file do not reach the next one. Where an\n  agent may not write it (lakeswitch: `human-decided`), propose the text.\n- **Research about this repository lives in `docs/research/`.** A vault note,\n  chat or rendered page is a view of it: it names the source path and commit,\n  and a finding is never first written there. Personal reasons to care stay\n  outside the repository.\n- **The maintainer's Claude Code display** (status line, session entry, handover safety net, `/handover`) lives\n  in `tools/claude-code/`; change it there and reinstall with `tools/claude-code/install.sh`, never only in `~/.claude`.\n- **Sub-agents survive a budget pause** (maintainer, 2026-10-06). Each commits\n  and pushes after every green step and ends its report with a `Resume:` line;\n  the orchestrator keeps a list (agent id, branch, last pushed commit, next\n  step) and resumes or restarts there. One change at a time, with few agents\n  and a visible queue. A long runner job starts in the harness's background mode, one job per call — never with `&` or `nohup` inside a command, which ends without a notice and leaves a lane idle unseen (maintainer, 2026-11-04). Every night run arms a recurring 30-minute wake, keeps the machine awake, and checks and logs its lanes as described in `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, ‘Night runs’.\n- **Pull requests stay mergeable:** synced daily, asked about after five working\n  days, three per hot file, sliced over ~800 lines, merged through the merge queue at their exact head (without it: one at a time against the new head once every check completed); questions in one 15:00 block (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n- **Findings returned as text** (when the harness refuses a reviewer's write)\n  are committed unchanged by the orchestrator, which says so in the commit.\n  MINOR rows on tests, security or false statements are repaired without asking; style rows\n  are accepted limits named in the PR. A second finding of one mechanism ends case repair; a mechanism no choke point closes gets a `Boundary` in its spec; a hand repair marks the loop row `fixed`, regenerates the index after a header edit and stamps after local midnight (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4).\n- **An exhausted review ladder goes to phase 6** (maintainer, 2026-11-20): when\n  `review-loop` refuses because every stage of its run is consumed and the last\n  round was not clean, and every taken row of that round is repaired, the lane\n  goes to the phase-6 review instead of a new loop run; phase 6 checks that last\n  repair. Reason: a run's history cannot be reset, and asking each time stopped\n  lanes overnight.\n\n",

          "end_line": 1535,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",

`decisions.md` is read by the early statement check below, which refuses an unreadable file\n    # with the remedy; the preflight does not read it a second time with a bare message.\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, CODEX, bead_file=\"research.md\")\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    refuse_unreadable_statements(root, change)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    # The derived leftovers the run started with: put back with the rest, but never blamed on the model.\n    started_with = {path for path in changed_paths(root) if derived_leftover(root, path)}\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    tools = tool_state(root)  # before any model runs (R-21)\n    routes = [\n        (CODEX, \"codex\", None),\n        (CODEX, \"codex-repair\", \"the first draft attempt failed\"),\n        (GLM, \"glm\", \"two Codex draft attempts failed\"),\n    ]\n    diagnostics: list[str] = []\n    for attempt, (endpoint, route, reason) in enumerate(routes, 1):\n        key = None\n        if endpoint == GLM:\n            # The key is read only when the GLM attempt is due (spec, criteria 23 and 24).\n            key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n            if key is None:\n                raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        prior_plan = ctx.plan.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.plan.exists() else \"\"\n        prior_time = prior_plan if TIME_HEADING.search(prior_plan) else \"## Time used\\n\"\n        started_wall, started_mono = utc_now(), monotonic_now()\n        prompt = draft_prompt(ctx, diagnostics)\n        begin_work_call(ctx, \"draft\", endpoint, prompt, attempt, route, ctx.findings, reason)\n        unmeasured: str | None = None\n        try:\n            before = worktree_tree(root)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            before, unmeasured = \"\", str(error)\n        call_error: CallFailed | None = None\n        try:\n            if endpoint == CODEX:\n                run_codex(ctx, prompt, writable=True, verb=\"draft\")\n            else:\n                run_work_model(ctx, prompt, endpoint, writable=True, key=key)\n        except CallFailed as error:\n            call_error = error\n        if key is not None:\n            #           "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone.           "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Worktrees — one per change",
          "end_line": 911,
          "excerpt": "### Worktrees — one per change\n\nWritten 2026-09-29 from D-5 (worktrees in the repository, through the tool's own\nmechanism), ADR 0006 (parallel work, one worktree per session) and the\nmeasurement of 2026-09-23 (`docs/research/2026-09-23-worktree-tracker-writes.md`).\nThe same rule holds in `lakeswitch-ai`, with the differences its\n`docs/workflow.md` §9 lists.\n\n1. **One change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.** Two sessions\n   never share a worktree, and nobody switches the branch of the main checkout\n   while another session runs.\n2. **In the repository, under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`.** That directory is in\n   `.gitignore` already, and it is where Claude Code puts its own worktrees\n   (`claude --worktree <name>`, and a sub-agent's `isolation: worktree`). By\n   hand: `git fetch origin && git worktree add -b <branch>\n   .claude/worktrees/<name> origin/main`. `bd worktree create` works as well but\n   writes the worktree's path into the tracked `.gitignore`, which is one more\n   change in the diff. Sibling directories beside the repository are retired\n   (D-5); worktrees that still sit there are finished and removed, not moved.\n3. **Always from a freshly fetched `origin/main`.** A worktree on a stale base\n   produces a pull request that is behind before it opens.\n4. **The tracker needs nothing.** `tools/bd` in a worktree finds the main\n   checkout's tracker through the shared git directory — no variable, no\n   redirect file, no copy. Concurrent writers lose nothing and a contested\n   claim has exactly one winner (measured 2026-09-23 with bd 1.3.0). Who may\n   write is house rule 4: the first writing session writes the tracker; every\n   other session claims its one bead with `tools/bd update <id> --claim\n   --actor <session>` and leaves its handover comment on that bead, nothing\n   more. After tracker writes: `tools/bd dolt push` first, `git push` second.\n5. **Omnigent starts inside the worktree.** Omnigent runs Claude Code as its\n   authors intend (`omnigent claude --use-native-config`, ADR 0006); the session\n   is started from the worktree's directory, so its hooks, its\n   `.claude/settings.json` and `tools/bd` all resolve there. Omnigent's own\n   tools reach the session as `mcp__omnigent__<tool>`, and neither Claude\n   Code's path rules, the hooks on its file tools nor Omnigent's own Claude Code\n   hook see what they do. Each one that writes, runs, spawns or changes state is\n   therefore denied by name in `.claude/settings.json`; the read-only ones stay\n   usable, except one that may send the task text to a routing judge\n   (`sys_advise_models`), which the user is asked about each time\n   (`permissions.ask`; decision of 2026-09-29). The one list, with a reason per\n   tool, is `scripts/omnigent_policy.py`. Read-only tools stay usable.\n   The default policy in `tools/omnigent/` is the second layer, rendered from\n   that same list. It refuses the denied ones and asks about the asked one\n   server-side for every Omnigent session on the machine. The\n   maintainer installs it, and nothing here depends on it alone (ADR 0006); as of\n   2026-09-29 it is built but not installed. Omnigent's bridge runs its own\n   `sys_os_*` tools without any policy while its relay does not advertise them,\n   and there only the rule in `.claude/settings.json` holds. Not yet measured: whether `omnigent claude`\n   started inside a worktree keeps that directory as the session's working\n   directory in every case.\n6. **After the merge, the worktree goes.** `git worktree remove\n   .claude/worktrees/<name>` and the branch with it. A worktree nobody works in\n   is a place where a later session finds an old state and takes it for the\n   current one.\n\nIsolation between sessions is a working agreement, not a wall: worktrees share\ngit's refs, hooks and configuration (`docs/architecture/2026-09-17-gap-analysis.md`).\nWhat really does not happen is simultaneous writing *to the same change* — that\nis not a tool question but a division of work.\n\n**What i",

      "statement": "The documented worktree layer fixes four things the change's Q-1/Q-3/Q-4 answers depart from: placement inside the repository under `.claude/worktrees/<name>` (sibling directories retired), one change/one bead/one branch/one worktree/one session with removal after the merge, isolation as exactly 'three things, no fourth' (worktree, harness sandbox, `permissions.deny`), and the requirement that every new checkout or worktree runs `make venv` and `bash tools/pi/install.sh` once.           "excerpt": "def worktree_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"How many non-bare worktrees are registered with this repository - stale ones included, never pruned.\"\"\"\n    if worktree is None:\n        return f\"{NOT_READ} (worktree: not identified)\"\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"git\", \"-C\", str(worktree), \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\", \"-z\"])\n        records = worktree_records(raw)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        return str(error)\n    count = sum(1 for record in records if \"bare\" not in record)\n    return f\"{count} (git worktree list; non-bare entries, stale registrations included)\"\n",

          "excerpt": "## What a lane is\n\n- **A lane is an ordered queue of changes.** Each item is one bead, one\n  branch and one worktree ([Working in parallel](../README.md#working-in-parallel)).\n  The queues are written down before a run starts. The night plan of\n  2026-10-28 is an example ([night plan](research/2026-10-28-night-run-plan.md)).\n- **One session orchestrates all of them.** It is the only tracker writer. It\n  starts the runner's verbs, decides review rows, writes the record and\n  commits. Models do the explore, draft, implement, repair and review work\n  through `scripts/stage2.py`.\n- **Disjoint files.** Only one lane changes a given hot file (for example\n  the runner, `scripts/stage2.py`). Two lanes never touch the same one.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "def worktree_digests(root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The 8-character record digests of every worktree `git worktree list` names for this root.\n\n    The listing is this repository's, including worktrees whose directories are missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        listing = _git_output(root, \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\")\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"worktree discovery failed: {error}\") from error\n    digests: list[str] = []\n    for line in listing.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(\"worktree \"):\n            continue\n        path = Path(line[len(\"worktree \") :]).resolve()\n        digest = record_key(\"\", path).rsplit(\"@\", 1)[1]\n        if digest not in digests:\n            digests.append(digest)\n    return digests\n",

      "statement": "The failed-call behaviour Q-5 reverses is stated in two places and implemented as a stop: docs/WORKFLOW.md::The routing says that if the model process itself fails the runner restores the worktree to the baseline commit and exits 1, with `implement <change> --stage2-off` as the next step, and docs/WORKFLOW.md::The runner is the only way says 'A failed model process stops instead of silently changing route'; docs/WORKFLOW.md::Repairing taken findings (repair) says a failed call stops the run without a fallback. In code, run_attempts raises `CallFailed` after the failed call's recovery instead of continuing the route list, and restore_baseline's contract is to put every path but `findings.md` back after a failed call. ADR 0017 rejected 'Automatic fallback on Codex call failure' as hiding an availability-driven budget switch and its Consequences require an explicit retry or Stage-1 restart — and the decision names `docs/WORKFLOW.md §3` although the doctrine sentence stands in the §4 section 'The runner is the only way'."

          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",

          "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb. A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2). Before the failure is decided, findings.md is restored outright: every post-run check, cheap\n    or full, reads the runner's file, an edit alone fails nothing, and a completed attempt that edited\n    it carries a quoted restore notice under its audit line (spec, criteria 8 and 9).\n\n    A verb that passes `retain_answer` keeps every attempt's full answer: right at the model-return\n    boundary, before any HEAD check, verification or answer check can stop the run, the protected\n    answer is saved as local evidence and its location joins the attempt's diagnostics - the parser's\n    rejections, the call and verify failures included - and is printed on success (bead\n    coding-harness-hgvp). A failed call keeps the output it returned.\n\n    A verb that passes `protect_lifecycle` snapshots the change's lifecycle fields (`status`,\n    `implementation_status`) in spec, optional design and plan right before every call. Once the\n    attempt's changed-file measurement stands, changed effective values restore the trusted whole\n    frontmatter block, preserving body edits and YAML anchors - before verification, the\n    derived preparation or the checkpoint reads the documents. The same per-attempt snapshot serves\n    the early exits: a failed call and a retry recover whole snapshotted inputs, a moved HEAD keeps\n    its commit while the safe working-tree fields go back, a refused checkpoint puts the fields back\n    before the run stops, and every attempt's bookkeeping names what was restored or says the fields\n    stayed unchanged (status-fields-restore). A deleted document or an unreadable header is the\n    existing snapshotted-input recovery's to repair; the attempt is rejected, never accepted on\n    invented surrounding content.\n\n    The failed-check listing and the changed-file entries pass through `protect_diagnostics` once, on\n    every route, the keyless ones included; the block in findings.md and the retry prompt both take that\n    one safe text, so a fixture secret a check printed blocks neither the next attempt's l",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Worktrees — one per change",
          "end_line": 911,
          "excerpt": "### Worktrees — one per change\n\nWritten 2026-09-29 from D-5 (worktrees in the repository, through the tool's own\nmechanism), ADR 0006 (parallel work, one worktree per session) and the\nmeasurement of 2026-09-23 (`docs/research/2026-09-23-worktree-tracker-writes.md`).\nThe same rule holds in `lakeswitch-ai`, with the differences its\n`docs/workflow.md` §9 lists.\n\n1. **One change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.** Two sessions\n   never share a worktree, and nobody switches the branch of the main checkout\n   while another session runs.\n2. **In the repository, under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`.** That directory is in\n   `.gitignore` already, and it is where Claude Code puts its own worktrees\n   (`claude --worktree <name>`, and a sub-agent's `isolation: worktree`). By\n   hand: `git fetch origin && git worktree add -b <branch>\n   .claude/worktrees/<name> origin/main`. `bd worktree create` works as well but\n   writes the worktree's path into the tracked `.gitignore`, which is one more\n   change in the diff. Sibling directories beside the repository are retired\n   (D-5); worktrees that still sit there are finished and removed, not moved.\n3. **Always from a freshly fetched `origin/main`.** A worktree on a stale base\n   produces a pull request that is behind before it opens.\n4. **The tracker needs nothing.** `tools/bd` in a worktree finds the main\n   checkout's tracker through the shared git directory — no variable, no\n   redirect file, no copy. Concurrent writers lose nothing and a contested\n   claim has exactly one winner (measured 2026-09-23 with bd 1.3.0). Who may\n   write is house rule 4: the first writing session writes the tracker; every\n   other session claims its one bead with `tools/bd update <id> --claim\n   --actor <session>` and leaves its handover comment on that bead, nothing\n   more. After tracker writes: `tools/bd dolt push` first, `git push` second.\n5. **Omnigent starts inside the worktree.** Omnigent runs Claude Code as its\n   authors intend (`omnigent claude --use-native-config`, ADR 0006); the session\n   is started from the worktree's directory, so its hooks, its\n   `.claude/settings.json` and `tools/bd` all resolve there. Omnigent's own\n   tools reach the session as `mcp__omnigent__<tool>`, and neither Claude\n   Code's path rules, the hooks on its file tools nor Omnigent's own Claude Code\n   hook see what they do. Each one that writes, runs, spawns or changes state is\n   therefore denied by name in `.claude/settings.json`; the read-only ones stay\n   usable, except one that may send the task text to a routing judge\n   (`sys_advise_models`), which the user is asked about each time\n   (`permissions.ask`; decision of 2026-09-29). The one list, with a reason per\n   tool, is `scripts/omnigent_policy.py`. Read-only tools stay usable.\n   The default policy in `tools/omnigent/` is the second layer, rendered from\n   that same list. It refuses the denied ones and asks about the asked one\n   server-side for every Omnigent session on the machine. The\n   maintainer installs it, and nothing here depends on it alone (ADR 0006); as of\n   2026-09-29 it is built but not installed. Omnigent's bridge runs its own\n   `sys_os_*` tools without any policy while its relay does not advertise them,\n   and there only the rule in `.claude/settings.json` holds. Not yet measured: whether `omnigent claude`\n   started inside a worktree keeps that directory as the session's working\n   directory in every case.\n6. **After the merge, the worktree goes.** `git worktree remove\n   .claude/worktrees/<name>` and the branch with it. A worktree nobody works in\n   is a place where a later session finds an old state and takes it for the\n   current one.\n\nIsolation between sessions is a working agreement, not a wall: worktrees share\ngit's refs, hooks and configuration (`docs/architecture/2026-09-17-gap-analysis.md`).\nWhat really does not happen is simultaneous writing *to the same change* — that\nis not a tool question but a division of work.\n\n**What i",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::The runner is the only way",
          "end_line": 1535,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",

          "end_line": 186,
          "excerpt": "## Sessions across checkouts\n\n- **Another session in the same checkout:** say so before changing a file,\n  committing or switching the branch, and offer a worktree. House rule 4 holds\n  for the tracker meanwhile.\n- **Worktrees: one change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.**\n  A worktree lives under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`, is branched from a freshly fetched `origin/main`,\n  and is removed after the merge; tracker access, claims and sibling directories: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3.\n  Each new checkout or worktree runs `make venv` and `bash tools/pi/install.sh` once before `make verify`\n  (`PYTHON=` picks a 3.12+ interpreter; one that does not match the lock fails the suite, bead\n  coding-harness-ei0; the Pi tests and the swarms need the pinned Pi, bead coding-harness-hs0o).\n- **A text-only change (Markdown outside `scripts/`, `tests/`, `prompts/`,\n  `decisions/`) skips the local `make verify`;** CI is its gate.\n- **Omnigent starts inside the worktree** (ADR 0006). Its default policy (`tools/omnigent/`) is a second layer;\n  nothing depends on it alone. Which tools are denied or asked, and why: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3, \"Worktrees\".\n- **What could not be read is \"not read\", never \"none\"** — an unopened file\n  and an empty query say different things.\n- **A standing rule belongs in the repository's `AGENTS.md`** — every harness\n  reads it; chat, memory and a user file do not reach the next one. Where an\n  agent may not write it (lakeswitch: `human-decided`), propose the text.\n- **Research about this repository lives in `docs/research/`.** A vault note,\n  chat or rendered page is a view of it: it names the source path and commit,\n  and a finding is never first written there. Personal reasons to care stay\n  outside the repository.\n- **The maintainer's Claude Code display** (status line, session entry, handover safety net, `/handover`) lives\n  in `tools/claude-code/`; change it there and reinstall with `tools/claude-code/install.sh`, never only in `~/.claude`.\n- **Sub-agents survive a budget pause** (maintainer, 2026-10-06). Each commits\n  and pushes after every green step and ends its report with a `Resume:` line;\n  the orchestrator keeps a list (agent id, branch, last pushed commit, next\n  step) and resumes or restarts there. One change at a time, with few agents\n  and a visible queue. A long runner job starts in the harness's background mode, one job per call — never with `&` or `nohup` inside a command, which ends without a notice and leaves a lane idle unseen (maintainer, 2026-11-04). Every night run arms a recurring 30-minute wake, keeps the machine awake, and checks and logs its lanes as described in `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, ‘Night runs’.\n- **Pull requests stay mergeable:** synced daily, asked about after five working\n  days, three per hot file, sliced over ~800 lines, merged through the merge queue at their exact head (without it: one at a time against the new head once every check completed); questions in one 15:00 block (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n- **Findings returned as text** (when the harness refuses a reviewer's write)\n  are committed unchanged by the orchestrator, which says so in the commit.\n  MINOR rows on tests, security or false statements are repaired without asking; style rows\n  are accepted limits named in the PR. A second finding of one mechanism ends case repair; a mechanism no choke point closes gets a `Boundary` in its spec; a hand repair marks the loop row `fixed`, regenerates the index after a header edit and stamps after local midnight (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4).\n- **An exhausted review ladder goes to phase 6** (maintainer, 2026-11-20): when\n  `review-loop` refuses because every stage of its run is consumed and the last\n  round was not clean, and every taken row of that round is repaired, the lane\n  goes to the phase-6 review instead of a new loop run; phase 6 checks that last\n  repair. Reason: a run's history cannot be reset, and asking each time stopped\n  lanes overnight.\n\n",

Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",

          "excerpt": "### Worktrees — one per change\n\nWritten 2026-09-29 from D-5 (worktrees in the repository, through the tool's own\nmechanism), ADR 0006 (parallel work, one worktree per session) and the\nmeasurement of 2026-09-23 (`docs/research/2026-09-23-worktree-tracker-writes.md`).\nThe same rule holds in `lakeswitch-ai`, with the differences its\n`docs/workflow.md` §9 lists.\n\n1. **One change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.** Two sessions\n   never share a worktree, and nobody switches the branch of the main checkout\n   while another session runs.\n2. **In the repository, under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`.** That directory is in\n   `.gitignore` already, and it is where Claude Code puts its own worktrees\n   (`claude --worktree <name>`, and a sub-agent's `isolation: worktree`).           "excerpt": "## Sessions across checkouts\n\n- **Another session in the same checkout:** say so before changing a file,\n  committing or switching the branch, and offer a worktree. House rule 4 holds\n  for the tracker meanwhile.\n- **Worktrees: one change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.**\n  A worktree lives under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`, is branched from a freshly fetched `origin/main`,\n  and is removed after the merge; tracker access, claims and sibling directories: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3.\n  Each new checkout or worktree runs `make venv` and `bash tools/pi/install.sh` once before `make verify`\n  (`PYTHON=` picks a 3.12+ interpreter; one that does not match the lock fails the suite, bead\n  coding-harness-ei0; the Pi tests and the swarms need the pinned Pi, bead coding-harness-hs0o).\n- **A text-only change (Markdown outside `scripts/`, `tests/`, `prompts/`,\n  `decisions/`) skips the local `make verify`;** CI is its gate.\n- **Omnigent starts inside the worktree** (ADR 0006). Its default policy (`tools/omnigent/`) is a second layer;\n  nothing depends on it alone. Which tools are denied or asked, and why: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3, \"Worktrees\".\n- **What could not be read is \"not read\", never \"none\"** — an unopened file\n  and an empty query say different things.\n- **A standing rule belongs in the repository's `AGENTS.md`** — every harness\n  reads it; chat, memory and a user file do not reach the next one. Where an\n  agent may not write it (lakeswitch: `human-decided`), propose the text.\n- **Research about this repository lives in `docs/research/`.** A vault note,\n  chat or rendered page is a view of it: it names the source path and commit,\n  and a finding is never first written there. Personal reasons to care stay\n  outside the repository.\n- **The maintainer's Claude Code display** (status line, session entry, handover safety net, `/handover`) lives\n  in `tools/claude-code/`; change it there and reinstall with `tools/claude-code/install.sh`, never only in `~/.claude`.\n- **Sub-agents survive a budget pause** (maintainer, 2026-10-06). Each commits\n  and pushes after every green step and ends its report with a `Resume:` line;\n  the orchestrator keeps a list (agent id, branch, last pushed commit, next\n  step) and resumes or restarts there. One change at a time, with few agents\n  and a visible queue. A long runner job starts in the harness's background mode, one job per call — never with `&` or `nohup` inside a command, which ends without a notice and leaves a lane idle unseen (maintainer, 2026-11-04). Every night run arms a recurring 30-minute wake, keeps the machine awake, and checks and logs its lanes as described in `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, ‘Night runs’.\n- **Pull requests stay mergeable:** synced daily, asked about after five working\n  days, three per hot file, sliced over ~800 lines, merged through the merge queue at their exact head (without it: one at a time against the new head once every check completed); questions in one 15:00 block (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n- **Findings returned as text** (when the harness refuses a reviewer's write)\n  are committed unchanged by the orchestrator, which says so in the commit.\n  MINOR rows on tests, security or false statements are repaired without asking; style rows\n  are accepted limits named in the PR. A second finding of one mechanism ends case repair; a mechanism no choke point closes gets a `Boundary` in its spec; a hand repair marks the loop row `fixed`, regenerates the index after a header edit and stamps after local midnight (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4).\n- **An exhausted review ladder goes to phase 6** (maintainer, 2026-11-20): when\n  `review-loop` refuses because every stage of its run is consumed and the last\n  round was not clean, and every taken row of that round is repaired, the lane\n  goes to the phase-6 review instead of a new loop run; phase 6 checks that last\n  repair. Reason: a run's history cannot be reset, and asking each time stopped\n  lanes overnight.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Agent decisions on the third phase-2a rows S-14..S-18 — 2026-11-18\n\nThird and last spec-review round (maintainer rule of 2026-11-18: triage each\nround, at most three rounds). `[DETAIL]` decisions by the orchestrating\nsession (Opus 5.5), shown as one list and accepted as proposed (\"A: So\nübernehmen\"). Reason: no round number is\n  given twice and no restart line misstates its round.\n- **S-15, no way out.** `--supersedes` is allowed with no pending audit call\n  when the named key holds an active record of the change; the line then says\n  \"audit calls 0\". Reason: the maintainer can always restart without deleting\n  a record directory by hand.\n- **S-16, which keys are \"other worktree keys\".** Only digests of this\n  repository's worktrees as `git worktree list` reports them; a record of\n  another repository with a change of the same name is never named, refused\n  on or archived. A worktree still listed by git remains discoverable even if its directory\n  is gone; once pruned from git metadata, its record is not seen — a named limit. Reason: no command may touch another repository's state.\n- **S-17, archive layout for several keys.**\n  `<change>@<digest of the superseding worktree>@<UTC timestamp>/<key>/…`,\n  one subdirectory per superseded key, with the manifest at the top; the\n  accounting line lists each key with its round range and archive\n  subdirectory. Reason: two `loop.md` files cannot collide, and every key\n  stays findable.\n- **S-18, an interrupted supersession whose key set changed before the\n  retry.** Not recoverable by a verb in this change: a named limit in\n  plan.md; follow-up bead coding-harness-0aht adds a verb to abandon or roll back such a\n  supersession. What **advances** the ladder is only a post-run-check failure (`verify_attempt` problems, `answer_check`): the attempt's block is appended to `findings.md` (`attempt_block`, `attempt_files`, bounds `ATTEMPT_FILES = 40` and `QUOTE_LINE_CHARS = 500`), inputs are restored, the next route starts. What **stops the run outright** is: a failed model call including an empty Codex answer (`CallFailed` raised after recovery — the attempt is saved under `refs/stage2/attempts/` by `save_attempt`, answers kept by `save_answer_evidence` in the git directory, baseline restored); a Codex attempt that moved HEAD; a failed answer-evidence write; `cannot_start` (\"`make verify` could not be run … no further attempt\"); and a leaked credential (`Refused` — docs/WORKFLOW.md: \"A leak refusal always stops the call; it never selects the fallback\"). The living spec `plans/specs/implementation-verification/spec.md` fixes the derived-file preparation that runs before *every* attempt, \"including retries\".\n\n2. **The review loop's member failures** (`scripts/stage2.py`, `run_swarm` and the round assembly).           "excerpt": "## Supported models and prerequisites\n\nThe currently usable positive path is `--model gpt-6.1-sol`, through the\ndeclared `openai-codex` endpoint and official Codex CLI. The Pi path accepts\n`opencode-go/<model>` only when the `opencode-go` endpoint lists that model\nfor framework content in `model-endpoints.yaml` (declared by ADR 0011; the\nid names the endpoint, not the launcher, Q-5). The runner does not invent a\nreview ordering and starts only the Pi pinned by `require_pi` (1.1.0); any\nother Pi is refused before dispatch. Fixture-only positive tests supply an\nexplicitly declared endpoint, not a production allow-list.\n\nThe dedicated worktree of change `<change>` is the canonical path\n`<main checkout>/.claude/worktrees/<change>`, where the main checkout is the\nparent of git's shared `.git` directory. A change folder copied into another\nworktree does not confer ownership; only this path with an attached branch\nqualifies. The invocation's working directory and runner root must both be\nthat canonical worktree root, not a subdirectory, another worktree or main.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "def validate_given_neighbours(header, frozen_sources, own_spec):\n    \"\"\"Missing and explicit empty headers have different meanings before dispatch.\"\"\"\n    message = \"add neighbours: [] or a unique list of existing frozen neighbour specs\"\n    if not neighbour_spec_form(own_spec):\n        raise ResearchMapError(\"invalid own-spec context; \" + message, 2)\n    values = header.get(\"neighbours\") if isinstance(header, dict) else None\n    if not isinstance(values, list) or any(not isinstance(item, str) for item in values):\n        raise ResearchMapError(message, 2)\n    if len(set(values)) != len(values):\n        raise ResearchMapError(message + \"; duplicate neighbour\", 2)\n    for path in values:\n        if not neighbour_spec_form(path) or path == own_spec or path not in frozen_sources:\n            raise ResearchMapError(message + f\"; invalid neighbour: {path}\", 2)\n    return list(values)\n",

          "path": "scripts/stage2_research_map.py",
          "reference": "validate_given_neighbours",

          "supported": true,

          "citation": "scripts/check_research_handoff.py::_parity",
          "end_line": 946,
          "excerpt": "def _parity(out: Outcome, label: str, spec_text: str, complete: list[ParsedRun], records: list[QRecord]) -> None:\n    header = _header(spec_text).get(\"neighbours\")\n    if not _is_list_of(header, str):\n        out.findings.append(f\"{label}: spec.md needs a neighbours: list of spec paths\")\n        return\n    problems = False\n    if len(set(header)) != len(header):\n        out.findings.append(f\"{label}: the neighbours header repeats a path\")\n        problems = True\n    for path in header:\n        if not neighbour_form(path):\n            out.findings.append(\n                f\"{label}: the neighbours header path {path!r} has none of the three permitted spec forms\"\n            )\n            problems = True\n    required = {\n        n[\"path\"]\n        for run in complete\n        for n in (run.derived or {})[\"neighbours\"]\n        if n[\"status\"] in (\"given\", \"confirmed\")\n    }\n    required |= {p for r in records for p in (*r.keep, *r.add)}\n    required -= {p for r in records for p in r.drop}\n    if problems:\n        return\n    for path in sorted(required - set(header)):\n        out.findings.append(f\"{label}: the neighbours header lacks the required path {path}\")\n    for path in sorted(set(header) - required):\n        out.findings.append(\n            f\"{label}: the neighbours header holds {path}, which no complete run confirmed or gave and no maintainer record keeps or adds\"\n        )\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "truncated": false

          "excerpt": "# Spec — verify-cheap-before-admission\n\nCatch all cheap blocking faults before waiting for the machine's expensive-work\nslot, everywhere the kit's full check runs (bead coding-harness-bxxt.6 — cheap\nverification before admission).           "end_line": 129,
          "excerpt": "# isolated-attempts — Decisions\n\nClass: architectural (bead coding-harness-s9r; it changes how every writing verb of the runner runs a model and amends the doctrine sentence in `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3). The interview ran in the conversation on 2026-11-22; the answers are recorded below with the options as they were put. Earlier decisions it builds on: the shared design of 2026-10-16 (beads coding-harness-6ie and coding-harness-s9r), the design of 2026-11-12 that folded coding-harness-c99h, -t3s3, -znc and -6ie into this bead, and the retention answer of 2026-11-03 (coding-harness-c99h Q-1).\n\n## Q-1 · Direction: own worktree per attempt, or the three-way comparison\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — open the lane now on the 2026-11-12 design, without the three-way comparison of 2026-10-23; the orchestrator re-checks it against the alternatives.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: how a writing attempt is isolated.\n  Intention: a failed attempt leaves its changes in the lane worktree and the next step trips over them; on 2026-11-22 this happened three times (u1ha, ttic, i76l).\n  Today: every attempt writes in the lane worktree.\n  Repository change: Options: A open now on the 2026-11-12 design (own git worktree per attempt from the fixed base, failed attempt saved as a side ref, fallback builds on it); B after Monday in a block with the maintainer; C first compare worktree, container (Podman/Docker) and k3s/OpenShift.\n  Architecture change: a new attempt lifecycle for all writing verbs.\n\nIn the context of writing attempts that damage the next one, facing a cheap per-attempt worktree or a heavier container or cluster, we decided to build the per-attempt worktree now, to achieve an end to the hand clean-up at the lowest cost, accepting that network access and foreign file reads are not covered by this change. — 2026-11-22\n\nThe orchestrator's re-check: the worktree covers the damage class (lane and runner inputs) at seconds per attempt; a container adds a network lock and blocks foreign reads but needs a Linux VM on macOS and stalled on 2026-10-15 (branch explore/isolated-attempts); k3s/OpenShift is heavier still. A container can later sit on top of the worktree (bead coding-harness-yw2p).\n\n## Q-2 · Threat model\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — an attempt may damage its own worktree in any way (delete, edit, symlink, replace inputs); the lane and every file the runner reads its next prompt from stay untouched; network access and reading foreign files are out of scope, with their own bead (coding-harness-yw2p).\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: which model behaviour the runner must withstand.\n  Intention: the spec states the threat model (bead).\n  Today: no stated model; each repair closed one case (codex-repairs F-8, F-10..F-14).\n  Repository change: Options: A lane and runner inputs only; B also block foreign file reads without a container; C container from the start.\n  Architecture change: none beyond Q-1.\n\nIn the context of the threat model, facing a narrow or a wide scope, we decided to protect the lane and the runner's inputs only, to achieve a small change that can be built and checked in days, accepting that network and foreign reads wait for the container bead. — 2026-11-22\n\n## Q-3 · Environment in the attempt worktree\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — the attempt worktree links the lane's .venv and installed Pi; a lane without them is refused before the model call with the remedy (make venv, tools/pi/install.sh); the runner checksums the shared environment before and after each attempt and rejects the attempt on a difference.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: where an attempt worktree gets its Python environment and Pi.\n  Intention: without the pinned Pi about 110 tests fail and an attempt goes red for an environment reason (0zhf attempts 2 and 3, 2026-11-22).\n  Today: the lane worktree carries both.\n  Repository change: Options: A link the lane's environme",
