          "excerpt": "## Needed from the maintainer\n\nSix questions for the 15:00 block (Europe/Berlin), first the one that blocks\nmost work:\n\n1. **Self-closing beads (bead coding-harness-l1if): accept the two structural\n   remedies?** Phase 6 found a second finding of two mechanisms, which ends\n   case-by-case repair (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4).\n   - F6-4 (MAJOR, same mechanism as F6-1): a carriage return inside a commit\n     trailer value is turned into a line break, so the wrong bead can close.\n     Remedy: read Git's output as raw bytes and accept only a full match of\n     the bead-id pattern.\n   - F6-5 (MAJOR, same mechanism as F6-2/F6-3): a deleted subdirectory of\n     this checkout is classified as \"other\" and passes. Remedy: fail closed —\n     a peer counts as unrelated only when its directory exists outside every\n     Git repository.\n   - Recommendation: accept both; each replaces a class of cases.\n2. **Red-first proofs in a private clone (bead coding-harness-wkxm): continue\n   past the appetite?** The time used is past the plan's appetite (recorded in\n   its `plan.md`); round 4 has two structural rows open (L4-1 one outer\n   cleanup, L4-3 one shared test-tree snapshot).           "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. A leak refusal still never falls back.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: what follows a model call that ends without an answer.\n  Intention: on 2026-11-22 two u1ha repairs stopped at the Codex usage limit and Sonnet had to be started by hand.\n  Today: the call stops; docs/WORKFLOW.md §3 says a failed model process stops instead of silently changing route.\n  Repository change: Options: A fall through on every failed call except a leak refusal; B only for known causes; C keep stopping.\n  Architecture change: the §3 doctrine sentence, with an ADR addendum.\n\nIn the context of failed model calls, facing a stop or a visible fall-through, we decided to fall through to the next route with the reason recorded, to achieve night runs that do not stall, accepting that an unknown failure is answered by the next route instead of a stop. — 2026-11-22\n\n",

The maintainer put the ladder to the\nloop alone on 2026-10-08 — after\nCodex's phase 6 found two real BLOCKERs in a change the loop had passed, as on\nevery change of the night run — so GLM has left the reviewer roles.\n**Since 2026-10-06** (maintainer) GLM 5.3 Flash\n(`glm-5.3-flash`, the Z.ai endpoint) also explores (phase 1) and implements\n(phase 4) — the two phases that read the repository broadly and write its\ncode. **Since 2026-10-12** (ADR 0015) GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`, the same endpoint)\nrepaired the findings the orchestrator takes, of the loop (4b) and of phase 6;\n**since the merge of ADR 0017** Codex (`gpt-6.1-sol` until 2026-11-15, `gpt-6.1-terra` since) does, with Sonnet 5.5\nafter two failed post-run checks, through the runner's `repair` verb — since the\nfirst day `taken` on a row means\ndecided and waiting for the repair, and `fixed` means repaired.           "excerpt": "## Implement and draft amendment — the targeted check covers more verbs, 2026-11-12\n\nThe maintainer answered the interview of the change\n`targeted-check-more-verbs` on 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12\n(`plans/changes/targeted-check-more-verbs/decisions.md`, Q-1 to Q-6; bead\ncoding-harness-0swp). An implement attempt whose new production code (an added Python or shell\n   file) no test reaches, as the current link inventory proves, is refused\n   before any test runs and before a full fallback is admitted; its\n   diagnostics name the file and ask for its test. An unreadable inventory\n   proves nothing and keeps the fallback (Q-4).\n3. A targeted red fails the attempt; the full check never runs to override\n   it. The existing guards of each route (cheap checks, answer proofs,\n   protected-path and checkpoint guards) remain mandatory.\n4. A draft's post-run check runs only the locally runnable document gates of\n   the gate registry, without pytest or code gates and outside the\n   machine-wide verify admission; its existing artefact checks and its one\n   tolerated missing ADR answer stay as they were (Q-2).\n5. Decision 3 stands unchanged: a fresh green full `make verify` of the head\n   under review precedes phase 6, and CI keeps running the complete suite.\n6.           "citation": "plans/changes/isolated-attempts/decisions.md::Q-6 · Scope, order and structure",
          "end_line": 115,
          "excerpt": "## Q-6 · Scope, order and structure\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — one change, two pull requests: PR 1 the shared attempt lifecycle, isolation switched on for repair; PR 2 switches it on for draft and implement after one night of use. Checked, at the maintainer's request, against modularisation and centralisation (AGENTS.md rule 9, bead coding-harness-vg9): the lifecycle lives in one new module scripts/stage2_attempts.py, the single choke point all three verbs call from PR 1 on; isolation is a declared per-verb parameter, so no second attempt path stands beside it at any time; the module has its own command-line entry for other harnesses; a check goes red when a writing verb starts a model outside it.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: how much changes at once and where the code lives.\n  Intention: scripts/stage2.py has 12,511 lines on origin/main (2026-11-22) and many lanes change it at once.\n  Today: each verb runs its own attempt loop inside stage2.py.\n  Repository change: Options: A one change, two PRs, repair first; B all three verbs in one PR; C repair only, the rest in a later bead.\n  Architecture change: a new module as the one attempt path.\n\nIn the context of a large shared runner file, facing one big or two staged pull requests, we decided on one module as the single attempt path with isolation as a per-verb parameter switched on in two steps, to achieve a small first merge without a side route, accepting one night in which draft and implement run through the module without isolation. — 2026-11-22\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "plans/changes/isolated-attempts/decisions.md",
          "reference": "Q-6 · Scope, order and structure",
          "start_line": 101,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "plans/changes/isolated-attempts/decisions.md::Q-7 · When side refs are deleted",
          "end_line": 129,
          "excerpt": "## Q-7 · When side refs are deleted\n\nasked: 2026-11-03\nanswer: \"nach dem Merge\" — after a change merges, the clean-up after merge (bead coding-harness-kpaq) deletes that change's refs under refs/stage2/attempts/<change>/, locally and on origin (asked 2026-11-03 under coding-harness-c99h, which this bead absorbed on 2026-11-12).\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: retention of side refs of stopped attempts.\n  Intention: the refs grow without bound (11 on origin, measured 2026-11-03).\n  Today: nothing deletes them.\n  Repository change: Options: delete after the merge; keep 14 days; keep forever.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of side refs that keep stopped attempts, facing unbounded growth or a retention rule, we decided that a change's attempt refs are deleted after its merge, locally and on origin, accepting that a stopped attempt of a merged change can no longer be inspected. — 2026-11-03\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "plans/changes/isolated-attempts/decisions.md",
          "reference": "Q-7 · When side refs are deleted",
          "start_line": 116,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "plans/changes/isolated-attempts/decisions.md::Q-3 · Environment in the attempt worktree",
          "end_line": 70,
          "excerpt": "## Q-3 · Environment in the attempt worktree\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — the attempt worktree links the lane's .venv and installed Pi; a lane without them is refused before the model call with the remedy (make venv, tools/pi/install.sh); the runner checksums the shared environment before and after each attempt and rejects the attempt on a difference.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: where an attempt worktree gets its Python environment and Pi.\n  Intention: without the pinned Pi about 110 tests fail and an attempt goes red for an environment reason (0zhf attempts 2 and 3, 2026-11-22).\n  Today: the lane worktree carries both.\n  Repository change: Options: A link the lane's environment; B fresh install per attempt; C copy per attempt.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of the attempt environment, facing links, fresh installs or copies, we decided to link the lane's environment with a before-and-after checksum, to achieve seconds per attempt and the same environment for every attempt, accepting that a changed environment rejects the attempt instead of being repaired. — 2026-11-22\n\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "reference": "Q-3 · Environment in the attempt worktree",

          "excerpt": "## Q-3 · Environment in the attempt worktree\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — the attempt worktree links the lane's .venv and installed Pi; a lane without them is refused before the model call with the remedy (make venv, tools/pi/install.sh); the runner checksums the shared environment before and after each attempt and rejects the attempt on a difference.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: where an attempt worktree gets its Python environment and Pi.\n  Intention: without the pinned Pi about 110 tests fail and an attempt goes red for an environment reason (0zhf attempts 2 and 3, 2026-11-22).\n  Today: the lane worktree carries both.\n  Repository change: Options: A link the lane's environment; B fresh install per attempt; C copy per attempt.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of the attempt environment, facing links, fresh installs or copies, we decided to link the lane's environment with a before-and-after checksum, to achieve seconds per attempt and the same environment for every attempt, accepting that a changed environment rejects the attempt instead of being repaired. — 2026-11-22\n\n",

          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",

          "end_line": 115,
          "excerpt": "## Q-6 · Scope, order and structure\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — one change, two pull requests: PR 1 the shared attempt lifecycle, isolation switched on for repair; PR 2 switches it on for draft and implement after one night of use. Checked, at the maintainer's request, against modularisation and centralisation (AGENTS.md rule 9, bead coding-harness-vg9): the lifecycle lives in one new module scripts/stage2_attempts.py, the single choke point all three verbs call from PR 1 on; isolation is a declared per-verb parameter, so no second attempt path stands beside it at any time; the module has its own command-line entry for other harnesses; a check goes red when a writing verb starts a model outside it.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: how much changes at once and where the code lives.\n  Intention: scripts/stage2.py has 12,511 lines on origin/main (2026-11-22) and many lanes change it at once.\n  Today: each verb runs its own attempt loop inside stage2.py.\n  Repository change: Options: A one change, two PRs, repair first; B all three verbs in one PR; C repair only, the rest in a later bead.\n  Architecture change: a new module as the one attempt path.\n\nIn the context of a large shared runner file, facing one big or two staged pull requests, we decided on one module as the single attempt path with isolation as a per-verb parameter switched on in two steps, to achieve a small first merge without a side route, accepting one night in which draft and implement run through the module without isolation. — 2026-11-22\n\n",

          "excerpt": "def _run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:\n    \"\"\"The verb `main` parsed, with the runner's refusals mapped to their exit codes.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        if (\n           "excerpt": "def worktree_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"How many non-bare worktrees are registered with this repository - stale ones included, never pruned.\"\"\"\n    if worktree is None:\n        return f\"{NOT_READ} (worktree: not identified)\"\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"git\", \"-C\", str(worktree), \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\", \"-z\"])\n        records = worktree_records(raw)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        return str(error)\n    count = sum(1 for record in records if \"bare\" not in record)\n    return f\"{count} (git worktree list; non-bare entries, stale registrations included)\"\n",

          "end_line": 5320,
          "excerpt": "def _supersede_loop_locked(root: Path, change: str, keys: list[str], reason: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Archive another worktree's loop record and restart the loop here (bead coding-harness-e82i).\n\n    The maintainer repeats `--supersedes <key>` for every active other-worktree key a refusal names.\n    Every selected record is read only under its lock, moved whole - everything a release would\n    delete, `availability.json` included, never the research siblings - into one unique archive\n    directory beside the records, and accounted for in one `Loop restarted:` line. The next\n    `review-loop` here is a fresh run whose rounds continue after the highest round ever assigned; the\n    old key can no longer continue the archived record.\n    \"\"\"\n    reason = \" \".join(reason.split())\n    if not reason:\n        raise Refused(\"--supersedes needs a non-empty --reason: the maintainer's request must be readable.\")\n    keys = sorted(set(keys))\n    current = record_key(change, root)\n    base = record_base()\n    archive_base = base.parent / ARCHIVE_DIR_NAME\n    listed = set(record_keys_of_worktrees(change, root))\n    for key in keys:\n        if re.fullmatch(rf\"{re.escape(change)}@[0-9a-f]{{8}}\", key) is None:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"`{key}` is no record key of {change}: a key is `<change>@<digest>`, as the refusals name them.\"\n            )\n        if key == current:\n            raise Refused(f\"`{key}` is this worktree's own record key; supersession takes another worktree's key.\")\n        if key not in listed:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"`{key}` names no worktree of this repository (`git worktree list`); the record of a removed \"\n                \"worktree or of another repository is not superseded.\"\n            )\n        if (base / key).is_symlink():\n            raise Refused(f\"the record directory of `{key}` is a symlink; supersession takes a real record directory.\")\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_a_failed_model_call_saves_the_attempt_before_restoring(\n    world: World, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]\n) -> None:\n    # Bead coding-harness-znc. Planted fault: the restore runs without the snapshot, and an\n    # attempt's edits - hours of them when a budget runs out - are gone with it.\n    head = git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\")\n    world.script(\n        claude=[\n            {\n                \"stderr\": \"budget spent\",\n                \"exit\": 1,\n                \"plant\": {\"src/half.py\": \"x = 1\\n\"},\n                \"append\": {\"src/app.py\": \"# edit\\n\"},\n            }\n        ]\n    )\n    assert world.run(\"implement\") == 1\n    err = capsys.readouterr().err\n    refs = git(world.root, \"for-each-ref\", \"--format=%(refname)\", \"refs/stage2/attempts/demo/\").splitlines()\n    assert len(refs) == 1 and refs[0].startswith(\"refs/stage2/attempts/demo/implement-attempt-1-\")\n    assert refs[0] in err and \"restored the worktree\" in err\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", f\"{refs[0]}^\") == head\n    assert git(world.root, \"show\", f\"{refs[0]}:src/half.py\") == \"x = 1\"\n    assert git(world.root, \"show\", f\"{refs[0]}:src/app.py\").endswith(\"# edit\")\n    # The snapshot carries the runner's identity, not the machine's: CI has no git user (PR #153).\n    assert git(world.root, \"log\", \"-1\", \"--format=%an <%ae>|%cn <%ce>\", refs[0]) == (\n        \"stage2 runner <stage2@localhost>|stage2 runner <stage2@localhost>\"\n    )\n    # The restore still leaves the tree clean and HEAD and the real index untouched.\n    assert not (world.root / \"src/half.py\").exists()\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\") == head\n    assert git(world.root, \"status\", \"--porcelain\", \"--\", \".\", \":(exclude)plans/changes/demo/findings.md\") == \"\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_a_failed_flash_process_restores_the_baseline_so_stage2_off_can_proceed(world: World) -> None:\n    head = git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\")\n    plan_before = world.plan.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    world.script(\n        claude=[\n            {\n                \"stderr\": \"Z.ai outage\",\n                \"exit\": 1,\n                \"plant\": {\"src/half.py\": \"x = 1\\n\"},\n                \"append\": {\"plans/changes/demo/plan.md\": \"2026-10-07 10:00–10:05, 5 min\\n\", \"src/app.py\": \"# edit\\n\"},\n            },\n            {\n                \"stdout\": \"built\",\n                \"plant\": {\"src/app.py\": \"value = 3\\n\"},\n                \"append\": {\"plans/changes/demo/plan.md\": \"2026-10-07 11:00–11:05, 5 min\\n\"},\n            },\n        ],\n        make=[{\"stdout\": \"green\\n\"}],\n    )\n    assert world.run(\"implement\") == 1\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\") == head\n    assert not (world.root / \"src/half.py\").exists()\n    assert world.plan.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == plan_before\n    assert git(world.root, \"status\", \"--porcelain\", \"--\", \".\", \":(exclude)plans/changes/demo/findings.md\") == \"\"\n    assert \"Stage-2 call\" in world.text()  # the audit line stays in findings.md\n    assert world.run(\"implement\", \"demo\", \"--stage2-off\", \"Z.ai outage\") == 0\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-list\", \"--count\", f\"{head}..HEAD\") == \"1\"\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::tool_state",
          "end_line": 5630,
          "excerpt": "def tool_state(root: Path) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The digest of the worktree's `.venv/` tree, taken before the model runs (R-21).\n\n    `.venv/` is ignored by git: a file there is invisible to `changed_paths` and survives\n    `restore_baseline`, so this digest is the only thing that shows an overwritten tool, a planted\n    `*.pth` file or a replaced package. Every file maps to the SHA-256 of its bytes and every symlink\n    to its target; the runner's steps run with the interpreter, ruff and packages of this tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    state: dict[str, str] = {}\n    venv = root / \".venv\"\n    try:\n        info = venv.lstat()\n        if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode):\n            # Record the root link AND digest its tools: an unchanged link must not hide\n            # overwritten target bytes. os.walk traverses its root even with followlinks=False;\n            # nested directory links remain opaque, and _unlink_cache still rejects this root.\n            state[\".venv\"] = \"link:\" + str(venv.readlink())\n    except FileNotFoundError:\n        return state\n    except OSError:\n        return {\".venv\": UNREADABLE}\n\n    def unreadable_directory(error: OSError) -> None:\n        # os.walk otherwise silently skips failed scandir calls, hiding newly planted caches.\n        path = Path(error.filename) if error.filename is not None else venv\n        state[path.relative_to(root).as_posix()] = UNREADABLE\n\n    for directory, names, files in os.walk(venv, onerror=unreadable_directory):\n        for name in sorted([*names, *files]):\n            path = Path(directory) / name\n            relative = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()\n            try:\n                if path.is_symlink():\n                    state[relative] = \"link:\" + str(path.readlink())\n                elif path.is_file():\n                    state[relative] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()\n            except OSError:\n                state[relative] = UNREADABLE\n    return state\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "excerpt": "def tool_problem(root: Path, before: dict[str, str] | None) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The first path of `.venv/` that is not what the runner saw before the call, named; `None` when none is.\n\n    A new or content-changed regular file below an exact `__pycache__` component inside `.venv/` is\n    deleted before any runner-owned step: pytest's assertion rewriting writes bytecode there during\n    an attempt, and a deleted cache is rebuilt, so that write is normalized instead of refused (bead\n    coding-harness-q94b). Every other difference keeps the refusal with the first path named. The\n    baseline bookkeeping stays narrow: each successful unlink immediately removes that path's old\n    entry from the shared `before` dictionary, even if a later check fails. This records only the\n    runner's own deletions. Nothing that survives is rebaselined; recreated caches are deleted again.\n    \"\"\"\n    if before is None:\n        return None\n\n    def differences(now: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:\n        return sorted(path for path in before.keys() | now.keys() if before.get(path) != now.get(path))\n\n    now = tool_state(root)\n    cleaned = False\n    for path in sorted(before.keys() | now.keys()):\n        if UNREADABLE in (before.get(path), now.get(path)):\n            return f\"`{path}` cannot be inspected, and a tool the attempt wrote is not run\"\n        if not _is_cache_path(path):\n            continue  # retain the difference, but still clean eligible caches that sort later\n        if before.get(path) == now.get(path):\n            continue\n        if before.get(path, \"\").startswith(\"link:\"):\n            continue  # removing a baseline symlink is never a cache-byte change\n        deleted = _unlink_cache(root, path)\n        if deleted is None:\n            continue  # a linked or non-regular cache-looking path stays a difference\n        if not deleted:\n            return f\"`{path}` cannot be deleted, and a tool the attempt wrote is not run\"\n        before.pop(path, None)  # record each runner-owned deletion even if a later check ",

          "excerpt": "def test_a_failed_model_call_saves_the_attempt_before_restoring(\n    world: World, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]\n) -> None:\n    # Bead coding-harness-znc. Planted fault: the restore runs without the snapshot, and an\n    # attempt's edits - hours of them when a budget runs out - are gone with it.\n    head = git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\")\n    world.script(\n        claude=[\n            {\n                \"stderr\": \"budget spent\",\n                \"exit\": 1,\n                \"plant\": {\"src/half.py\": \"x = 1\\n\"},\n                \"append\": {\"src/app.py\": \"# edit\\n\"},\n            }\n        ]\n    )\n    assert world.run(\"implement\") == 1\n    err = capsys.readouterr().err\n    refs = git(world.root, \"for-each-ref\", \"--format=%(refname)\", \"refs/stage2/attempts/demo/\").splitlines()\n    assert len(refs) == 1 and refs[0].startswith(\"refs/stage2/attempts/demo/implement-attempt-1-\")\n    assert refs[0] in err and \"restored the worktree\" in err\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", f\"{refs[0]}^\") == head\n    assert git(world.root, \"show\", f\"{refs[0]}:src/half.py\") == \"x = 1\"\n    assert git(world.root, \"show\", f\"{refs[0]}:src/app.py\").endswith(\"# edit\")\n    # The snapshot carries the runner's identity, not the machine's: CI has no git user (PR #153).\n    assert git(world.root, \"log\", \"-1\", \"--format=%an <%ae>|%cn <%ce>\", refs[0]) == (\n        \"stage2 runner <stage2@localhost>|stage2 runner <stage2@localhost>\"\n    )\n    # The restore still leaves the tree clean and HEAD and the real index untouched.\n    assert not (world.root / \"src/half.py\").exists()\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\") == head\n    assert git(world.root, \"status\", \"--porcelain\", \"--\", \".\", \":(exclude)plans/changes/demo/findings.md\") == \"\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_a_failed_flash_process_restores_the_baseline_so_stage2_off_can_proceed(world: World) -> None:\n    head = git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\")\n    plan_before = world.plan.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    world.script(\n        claude=[\n            {\n                \"stderr\": \"Z.ai outage\",\n                \"exit\": 1,\n                \"plant\": {\"src/half.py\": \"x = 1\\n\"},\n                \"append\": {\"plans/changes/demo/plan.md\": \"2026-10-07 10:00–10:05, 5 min\\n\", \"src/app.py\": \"# edit\\n\"},\n            },\n            {\n                \"stdout\": \"built\",\n                \"plant\": {\"src/app.py\": \"value = 3\\n\"},\n                \"append\": {\"plans/changes/demo/plan.md\": \"2026-10-07 11:00–11:05, 5 min\\n\"},\n            },\n        ],\n        make=[{\"stdout\": \"green\\n\"}],\n    )\n    assert world.run(\"implement\") == 1\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\") == head\n    assert not (world.root / \"src/half.py\").exists()\n    assert world.plan.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == plan_before\n    assert git(world.root, \"status\", \"--porcelain\", \"--\", \".\", \":(exclude)plans/changes/demo/findings.md\") == \"\"\n    assert \"Stage-2 call\" in world.text()  # the audit line stays in findings.md\n    assert world.run(\"implement\", \"demo\", \"--stage2-off\", \"Z.ai outage\") == 0\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-list\", \"--count\", f\"{head}..HEAD\") == \"1\"\n",

          "end_line": 3216,
          "excerpt": "class ScriptedPrograms:\n    \"\"\"A process double at the runner's `Popen` boundary, moved by one fake clock.\n\n    A test lists the commands to double as `(matcher, plan)` pairs; every other\n    command runs for real through the genuine `Popen`, so git and the stand-in\n    programs keep working. While the double stands, the fake pids exist nowhere\n    in the operating system and group operations on them never reach\n    `os.killpg` — fake pids and intercepted group operations are used together.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, clock: FakeClock, plans: list[tuple]) -> None:\n        self.clock = clock\n        self.plans = plans\n        self.launched: list[dict] = []\n        self.communications: list[dict] = []\n        # The genuine functions, captured at import: a second double installed while a first\n        # still stands must fall back to the operating system, not to the first double.\n        real_popen, real_killpg = GENUINE_POPEN, GENUINE_KILLPG\n        double = self\n\n        class Popen:\n            def __new__(cls, command, *args, **kwargs):\n                for matcher, plan in double.plans:\n                    if matcher(command):\n                        return ScriptedProcess(double, command, plan)\n                return real_popen(command, *args, **kwargs)\n\n        def killpg(group, signum):\n            if group >= FAKE_PID_BASE:\n                raise ProcessLookupError(f\"no such process group: the doubled pid {group} exists nowhere\")\n            return real_killpg(group, signum)\n\n        monkeypatch.setattr(subprocess, \"Popen\", Popen)\n        monkeypatch.setattr(os, \"killpg\", killpg)\n\n    def of(self, command: list[str] | None = None) -> list[dict]:\n        \"\"\"The doubled communications, optionally only those of one command.\"\"\"\n        return [row for row in self.communications if command is None or row[\"command\"] == command]\n\n    def waits(self, command: list[str] | None = None) -> list[dict]:\n        \"\"\"The doubled programs' own waits: every first `communicate`, the cleanup drain left out.\n\n        A stopped program is drained a second time at the kill, and that\n        bounded cleanup has a communication row of its own (`outcome:\n        \"drained\"`, the `KILL_DRAIN_SECONDS` argument on record); the policy\n        verdicts read the wait rows alone.\n        \"\"\"\n        return [row for row in self.of(command) if row[\"outcome\"] != \"drained\"]\n",

          "excerpt": "def restore_baseline(\n    root: Path,\n    baseline: str,\n    keep: set[Path],\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None = None,\n    planned: tuple[list[str], list[Path]] | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"After a failed model call, put every path but `keep` back at the baseline; say what was undone.\n\n    The runner refused pre-existing changes outside `keep` before the first call, so what differs\n    from the baseline outside it is the run's own - including a half-finished edit of a dead process.\n    Gitignored paths the attempt created are removed too: `changed_paths` cannot see them and\n    `git clean` without `-x` keeps them, so the run's earlier snapshot of the ignored files tells them\n    apart from the ones that stood before (phase 6, F-5). This implementation/repair rollback's\n    tracked destinations and newly created ignored cleanup paths are checked for an unsafe parent\n    before its first `git restore`, `git clean`, `unlink`, `rmtree` or parent removal; a refusal\n    leaves this recovery batch unwritten and ends the run.\n    \"\"\"\n    if planned is None:\n        planned = plan_baseline_restore(root, keep, ignored_before, baseline)\n    touched, created = planned\n    if not touched and not created:\n        return \"the worktree needed no restore.\"\n    spec = [f\":(exclude){path.as_posix()}\" for path in sorted(keep, key=lambda path: path.as_posix())]\n    try:\n        _git_output(root, \"restore\", f\"--source={baseline}\", \"--staged\", \"--worktree\", \"--\", \".\", *spec)\n        _git_output(root, \"clean\", \"-fdq\", \"--\", \".\", *spec)\n    except Refused as error:\n        listing = \", \".join([*touched, *(path.as_posix() for path in created)])\n        return f\"restoring the worktree to {baseline[:12]} failed ({error}); discard {listing} by hand.\"\n    removed = []\n    for relative in created:\n        path = root / relative\n        try:\n            if path.is_dir() and not path.is_symlink():\n                shutil.rmtree(path)\n            else:\n                path.unlink()\n        except OSError:\n            continue\n        removed.append(relative.as_posix())\n        parent = path.parent\n        while parent not in (root, parent.parent):\n            try:\n                parent.rmdir()\n            except OSError:\n                break\n            parent = parent.parent\n    undone = f\"undone: {', '.join(touched)}\" if touched else \"\"\n    ignored = f\"ignored paths removed: {', '.join(removed)}\" if removed else \"\"\n    inner = \"; \".join(part for part in (undone, ignored) if part)\n    return f\"the runner restored the worktree to {baseline[:12]} ({inner}); rerun the verb or add --stage2-off.\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def save_attempt(root: Path, baseline: str, change: str, label: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Save the worktree as it stands after a failed call on a local ref; say where, or why not.\n\n    A failed call is not a worthless one: a run that hits a spent budget after hours of edits still\n    holds them (bead coding-harness-znc). The snapshot goes through a temporary index, so the real\n    index and the files stay untouched; tracked and untracked files go in, gitignored ones do not.\n    The temporary index is seeded with the baseline, as in `worktree_tree`, so a file tracked although\n    ignored stays in the snapshot. The commit's parent is the baseline, so `git diff <baseline> <ref>`\n    shows everything the run left in the tree: this attempt, any earlier attempt of the run whose tree\n    it started on, and the runner's own writes. The ref lives under `refs/stage2/attempts/`, which no\n    branch push carries. A save that fails is named and never blocks the restore that follows.\n    The commit carries the runner's own identity, so a machine without a configured git user (a CI\n    runner) saves as well, and the ref says who wrote it.\n    \"\"\"\n    stamp = utc_now().strftime(\"%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ\")\n    ref = f\"refs/stage2/attempts/{change}/{label}-{stamp}\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-save-\") as scratch:\n        env = {**os.environ, \"GIT_INDEX_FILE\": str(Path(scratch) / \"index\"), **SAVE_IDENTITY}\n        try:\n            _git_output(root, \"read-tree\", baseline, env=env)\n            _git_output(root, \"add\", \"-A\", \"--\", \".\", env=env)\n            tree = _git_output(root, \"write-tree\", env=env).strip()\n            commit = _git_output(\n                root, \"commit-tree\", tree, \"-p\", baseline, \"-m\", f\"stage2: saved {label} of {change}\", env=env\n            ).strip()\n            _git_output(root, \"update-ref\", ref, commit)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            return f\"saving the attempt failed ({error})\"\n    return f\"the attempt is saved at {ref} ({commit[:12]}); `git diff {baseline[:12]} {ref}` shows it\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def save_answer_evidence(root: Path, change: str, token: str, attempt: int, answer: str, key: str | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Save one attempt's full answer as protected evidence below the worktree's own git directory.\n\n    Written at the model-return boundary, before any HEAD check, verification or answer check can\n    stop the run, so a rejected answer stays diagnosable from what the model actually returned (bead\n    coding-harness-hgvp). The directory is git's resolved per-worktree `stage2/attempts/<change>/` - in\n    a linked worktree below the main checkout's `.git/worktrees/<name>/`, which the diagnostics name\n    as an absolute path - local evidence like `refs/stage2/attempts/`, tracked by no path and carried by no branch push.\n    The answer passes `protect_diagnostics` once on every route, the keyless ones included; an empty\n    or unavailable answer is recorded as such, never fabricated or retried. The file is created\n    exclusively, so an earlier attempt's evidence is never overwritten; an aliased destination, a\n    protection failure or a failed write raises, so no checkpoint stands on lost or unprotected\n    evidence. Returns the saved file, as the diagnostics name it.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        git_dir = Path(_git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"--absolute-git-dir\").strip())\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise CallFailed(f\"the answer evidence directory could not be resolved ({error})\") from error\n    if not git_dir.is_absolute():\n        git_dir = root / git_dir\n    body = protect_diagnostics(answer, key) if answer.strip() else \"(no answer was returned)\\n\"\n    directory = git_dir / \"stage2\" / \"attempts\" / change\n    expected = Path(os.path.realpath(git_dir)) / \"stage2\" / \"attempts\" / change\n    if directory.is_symlink() or os.path.realpath(directory) != str(expected):\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the answer evidence directory {directory} is not this worktree's own stage2/attempts/{change}; \"",

          "excerpt": "def worktree_digests(root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The 8-character record digests of every worktree `git worktree list` names for this root.\n\n    The listing is this repository's, including worktrees whose directories are missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        listing = _git_output(root, \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\")\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"worktree discovery failed: {error}\") from error\n    digests: list[str] = []\n    for line in listing.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(\"worktree \"):\n            continue\n        path = Path(line[len(\"worktree \") :]).resolve()\n        digest = record_key(\"\", path).rsplit(\"@\", 1)[1]\n        if digest not in digests:\n            digests.append(digest)\n    return digests\n",

          "excerpt": "def tool_state(root: Path) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The digest of the worktree's `.venv/` tree, taken before the model runs (R-21).\n\n    `.venv/` is ignored by git: a file there is invisible to `changed_paths` and survives\n    `restore_baseline`, so this digest is the only thing that shows an overwritten tool, a planted\n    `*.pth` file or a replaced package. Every file maps to the SHA-256 of its bytes and every symlink\n    to its target; the runner's steps run with the interpreter, ruff and packages of this tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    state: dict[str, str] = {}\n    venv = root / \".venv\"\n    try:\n        info = venv.lstat()\n        if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode):\n            # Record the root link AND digest its tools: an unchanged link must not hide\n            # overwritten target bytes. os.walk traverses its root even with followlinks=False;\n            # nested directory links remain opaque, and _unlink_cache still rejects this root.\n            state[\".venv\"] = \"link:\" + str(venv.readlink())\n    except FileNotFoundError:\n        return state\n    except OSError:\n        return {\".venv\": UNREADABLE}\n\n    def unreadable_directory(error: OSError) -> None:\n        # os.walk otherwise silently skips failed scandir calls, hiding newly planted caches.\n        path = Path(error.filename) if error.filename is not None else venv\n        state[path.relative_to(root).as_posix()] = UNREADABLE\n\n    for directory, names, files in os.walk(venv, onerror=unreadable_directory):\n        for name in sorted([*names, *files]):\n            path = Path(directory) / name\n            relative = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()\n            try:\n                if path.is_symlink():\n                    state[relative] = \"link:\" + str(path.readlink())\n                elif path.is_file():\n                    state[relative] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()\n            except OSError:\n                state[relative] = UNREADABLE\n    return state\n",

          "excerpt": "def tool_problem(root: Path, before: dict[str, str] | None) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The first path of `.venv/` that is not what the runner saw before the call, named; `None` when none is.\n\n    A new or content-changed regular file below an exact `__pycache__` component inside `.venv/` is\n    deleted before any runner-owned step: pytest's assertion rewriting writes bytecode there during\n    an attempt, and a deleted cache is rebuilt, so that write is normalized instead of refused (bead\n    coding-harness-q94b). Every other difference keeps the refusal with the first path named. The\n    baseline bookkeeping stays narrow: each successful unlink immediately removes that path's old\n    entry from the shared `before` dictionary, even if a later check fails. This records only the\n    runner's own deletions. Nothing that survives is rebaselined; recreated caches are deleted again.\n    \"\"\"\n    if before is None:\n        return None\n\n    def differences(now: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:\n        return sorted(path for path in before.keys() | now.keys() if before.get(path) != now.get(path))\n\n    now = tool_state(root)\n    cleaned = False\n    for path in sorted(before.keys() | now.keys()):\n        if UNREADABLE in (before.get(path), now.get(path)):\n            return f\"`{path}` cannot be inspected, and a tool the attempt wrote is not run\"\n        if not _is_cache_path(path):\n            continue  # retain the difference, but still clean eligible caches that sort later\n        if before.get(path) == now.get(path):\n            continue\n        if before.get(path, \"\").startswith(\"link:\"):\n            continue  # removing a baseline symlink is never a cache-byte change\n        deleted = _unlink_cache(root, path)\n        if deleted is None:\n            continue  # a linked or non-regular cache-looking path stays a difference\n        if not deleted:\n            return f\"`{path}` cannot be deleted, and a tool the attempt wrote is not run\"\n        before.pop(path, None)  # record each runner-owned deletion even if a later check ",

          "excerpt": "def run_work_model(\n    ctx: Context,\n    prompt: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    writable: bool,\n    key: str | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One non-interactive Claude Code work call with file tools only.\"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        prompt_file = Path(tmp) / \"work-prompt.md\"\n        prompt_file.write_text(prompt, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        command = [\n            \"claude\",\n            \"-p\",\n            f\"Run the phase for {ctx.change} exactly as the appended instructions say.\",\n            \"--append-system-prompt-file\",\n            str(prompt_file),\n            \"--model\",\n            endpoint[1],\n        ]\n        if endpoint[2]:\n            command += [\"--effort\", endpoint[2]]\n        command += [\n            \"--tools\",\n            WORK_WRITE_TOOLS if writable else WORK_READ_TOOLS,\n            \"--restricted\",\n            \"--safe-mode\",\n            \"--strict-mcp-config\",\n            \"--permission-mode\",\n            \"acceptEdits\" if writable else \"dontAsk\",\n            \"--permission-prompts\",\n            \"none\",\n            \"--no-session-persistence\",\n            \"--output-format\",\n            \"text\",\n        ]\n        if key is None:\n            env = foreign_env({})\n        else:\n            config_dir = Path(tmp) / \"claude-config\"\n            config_dir.mkdir()\n            env = glm_env(key, config_dir, endpoint[1])\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, env, key, timeout=timeout, limit=limit)\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        error = fail(\"claude\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\", key)\n        # A failed call's printed answer travels along for the repair evidence; nothing else changes.\n        error.partial_answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n        raise error\n    answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n    if not answer.strip():\n        raise fail(\"claude\", done, \"the answer is empty\", key)\n    return answer\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_codex(\n    ctx: Context, prompt: str, resume: str | None = None, writable: bool = False, *, verb: str\n) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"One Codex call, first or resumed, pinned the same way. Returns (answer, thread id).\n\n    A review reads in the CLI's `read-only` sandbox; a draft writes in\n    `workspace-write`, and the runner puts back what lands outside the change\n    folder. No call takes a bypass flag (spec, criterion 1). Until it does, the\n  bounds are stated and not enforced; the maintainer's display warns of a\n  second session in the same checkout (`tools/claude-code/`). Building the\n  guard is its own change.\n* **Bead coding-harness-36z** (workers claim their own bead, proven in M0)\n  loses its M0 proof. It is to be re-scoped to the D-60 guard and the\n  events-journal check; this ADR does not write the tracker.\n* **Worktrees are not a security boundary.** Without an Omnigent sandbox, a\n  worktree keeps sessions from colliding; it does not confine what an agent\n  can reach.           "excerpt": "### Worktrees — one per change\n\nWritten 2026-09-29 from D-5 (worktrees in the repository, through the tool's own\nmechanism), ADR 0006 (parallel work, one worktree per session) and the\nmeasurement of 2026-09-23 (`docs/research/2026-09-23-worktree-tracker-writes.md`).\nThe same rule holds in `lakeswitch-ai`, with the differences its\n`docs/workflow.md` §9 lists.\n\n1. **One change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.** Two sessions\n   never share a worktree, and nobody switches the branch of the main checkout\n   while another session runs.\n2. **In the repository, under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`.** That directory is in\n   `.gitignore` already, and it is where Claude Code puts its own worktrees\n   (`claude --worktree <name>`, and a sub-agent's `isolation: worktree`). By\n   hand: `git fetch origin && git worktree add -b <branch>\n   .claude/worktrees/<name> origin/main`. `bd worktree create` works as well but\n   writes the worktree's path into the tracked `.gitignore`, which is one more\n   change in the diff. Sibling directories beside the repository are retired\n   (D-5); worktrees that still sit there are finished and removed, not moved.\n3. **Always from a freshly fetched `origin/main`.** A worktree on a stale base\n   produces a pull request that is behind before it opens.\n4. **The tracker needs nothing.** `tools/bd` in a worktree finds the main\n   checkout's tracker through the shared git directory — no variable, no\n   redirect file, no copy. Concurrent writers lose nothing and a contested\n   claim has exactly one winner (meas",

          "excerpt": "def test_findings_restore_preserves_recovery_and_repair_guards(world: World, monkeypatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Ledger 8, guards. Planted fault: restoration bypassed the recovery guards or fixed-line validation.\"\"\"\n    # A destination whose parent is a link the attempt created is refused before any write, and\n    # nothing travels through the link to its outside target.\n    outside = world.root.parent / \"outside-guard\"\n    outside.mkdir(parents=True)\n    linked = world.root / \"scratch\" / \"linked\"\n    linked.parent.mkdir()\n    linked.symlink_to(outside, target_is_directory=True)\n    (outside / \"findings.md\").write_text(\"target bytes\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    with pytest.raises(stage2.RestorationRefused):\n        stage2.restore_work_input(world.root, linked / \"findings.md\", b\"restored bytes\\n\")\n    assert (outside / \"findings.md\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == \"target bytes\\n\", \"a parent link was followed\"\n    #           "excerpt": "## Q-2 · Threat model\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — an attempt may damage its own worktree in any way (delete, edit, symlink, replace inputs); the lane and every file the runner reads its next prompt from stay untouched; network access and reading foreign files are out of scope, with their own bead (coding-harness-yw2p).\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: which model behaviour the runner must withstand.\n  Intention: the spec states the threat model (bead).\n  Today: no stated model; each repair closed one case (codex-repairs F-8, F-10..F-14).\n  Repository change: Options: A lane and runner inputs only; B also block foreign file reads without a container; C container from the start.\n  Architecture change: none beyond Q-1.\n\nIn the context of the threat model, facing a narrow or a wide scope, we decided to protect the lane and the runner's inputs only, to achieve a small change that can be built and checked in days, accepting that network and foreign reads wait for the container bead. — 2026-11-22\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Consequences\n\n* **ADR 0001 is superseded.** Its pilot, its throwaway repository and its\n  W0/W1 prerequisites lapse. The serial path stays available; it is simply\n  one writing session.\n* **ADR 0005 is superseded in part.** Its layer 2 (the Omnigent session\n  policy) and its validation \"in M0\" lapse; the write guard of D-60 takes\n  layer 2's place. Of its decision, a worker's claim of its own bead stays\n  in force, and a worker's creating follow-up work and closing its bead\n  pass to the first session, as D-60 has it.\n* **ADR 0002 is superseded in part** as well: its pilot store, its W1\n  activation condition and its M0 validation lapse with the pilot. Its\n  rules on stale or duplicate results stay and apply to coordinated runs,\n  when there are any.\n* **Until the maintainer rewrites house rule 4.** AGENTS.md house rule 4\n  says that while another session runs, none writes the tracker. With no\n  Omnigent workers, every session is interactive, so the rule binds them\n  all. Until the maintainer rewrites it (owed item \"Coding Harness 7\" of\n  the lakeswitch-ai decision record, the maintainer's own edit), parallel\n  sessions work in worktrees of their own but make no tracker writes while\n  another session runs; the worker claim above waits for that edit.\n* **Owed before this holds by tool rather than by rule.** The write guard\n  of D-60 — the per-checkout lock, the session cap and the tracker-write\n  refusal — does not exist yet in either repository. Until it does, the\n  bounds are stated and not enforced; the maintainer's display warns of a\n  second session in the same checkout (`tools/claude-code/`). Building the\n  guard is its own change.\n* **Bead coding-harness-36z** (workers claim their own bead, proven in M0)\n  loses its M0 proof. It is to be re-scoped to the D-60 guard and the\n  events-journal check; this ADR does not write the tracker.\n* **Worktrees are not a security boundary.** Without an Omnigent sandbox, a\n  worktree keeps sessions from colliding; it does not confine what an agent\n  can reach. The target document's trust contracts that assume a sandbox\n  are open, not settled by this ADR.\n* The target document (`docs/architecture/2026-09-17-omnigent-first-target.md`)\n  still describes the M0 design. A notice at its top, in its D-3 and D-7\n  rows and in its tracker section records this decision; the rest of its M0\n  text is kept as the record of the earlier design, as it was for ADR 0005.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "def changed_paths(\n    root: Path,\n    env: dict[str, str] | None = None,\n    against: str = \"HEAD\",\n    *,\n    skip_undecodable: bool = False,\n) -> set[Path]:\n    \"\"\"Tracked changes against `against`, in the working tree or the index, and untracked files.\n\n    `git diff <commit>` reads only the working tree, so a path staged and then put back in the file\n    differs from the commit in the index alone; `--cached` lists it (bead coding-harness-0c8).\n\n    Preserve undecodable bytes with surrogate escapes so other callers still see every path.\n    Preliminary formatting/test selection may skip them; targeted coverage must reject them and\n    require full verification. Intent-to-add handles the raw bytes independently.\n    \"\"\"\n    # `--no-renames`: a rename must list both names, or the deleted one is invisible (O192-1).\n    # Text-mode subprocess output translates CR to LF even with NUL delimiters.\n    tracked = _git_bytes(root, \"diff\", \"--no-renames\", \"--name-only\", \"-z\", against, env=env).split(b\"\\0\")\n    tracked += _git_bytes(root, \"diff\", \"--cached\", \"--no-renames\", \"--name-only\", \"-z\", against, env=env).split(b\"\\0\")\n    untracked = _git_bytes(root, \"ls-files\", \"-z\", \"--others\", \"--exclude-standard\", env=env).split(b\"\\0\")\n    paths: set[Path] = set()\n    for raw in [*tracked, *untracked]:\n        if not raw:\n            continue\n        try:\n            name = raw.decode(\"utf-8\")\n        except UnicodeDecodeError:\n            if skip_undecodable:\n                continue\n            name = raw.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"surrogateescape\")\n        path = Path(name)\n        # Git lists an untracked nested repository as a directory ending in '/'.\n        # That suffix is an inventory marker, not an unsafe pathname conversion.\n        if path.is_absolute() or \"..\" in path.parts or name not in (path.as_posix(), path.as_posix() + \"/\"):\n            raise Refused(\"a changed Git path cannot be mapped safely\")\n        paths.add(path)\n    return paths\n",

          "excerpt": "def _supersede_loop_locked(root: Path, change: str, keys: list[str], reason: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Archive another worktree's loop record and restart the loop here (bead coding-harness-e82i).\n\n    The maintainer repeats `--supersedes <key>` for every active other-worktree key a refusal names.\n    Every selected record is read only under its lock, moved whole - everything a release would\n    delete, `availability.json` included, never the research siblings - into one unique archive\n    directory beside the records, and accounted for in one `Loop restarted:` line. The next\n    `review-loop` here is a fresh run whose rounds continue after the highest round ever assigned; the\n    old key can no longer continue the archived record.\n    \"\"\"\n    reason = \" \".join(reason.split())\n    if not reason:\n        raise Refused(\"--supersedes needs a non-empty --reason: the maintainer's request must be readable.\")\n    keys = sorted(set(keys))\n    current = record_key(change, root)\n    base = record_base()\n    archive_base = base.parent / ARCHIVE_DIR_NAME\n    listed = set(record_keys_of_worktrees(change, root))\n    for key in keys:\n        if re.fullmatch(rf\"{re.escape(change)}@[0-9a-f]{{8}}\", key) is None:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"`{key}` is no record key of {change}: a key is `<change>@<digest>`, as the refusals name them.\"\n            )\n        if key == current:\n            raise Refused(f\"`{key}` is this worktree's own record key; supersession takes another worktree's key.\")\n        if key not in listed:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"`{key}` names no worktree of this repository (`git worktree list`); the record of a removed \"\n                \"worktree or of another repository is not superseded.\"\n            )\n        if (base / key).is_symlink():\n            raise Refused(f\"the record directory of `{key}` is a symlink;           "excerpt": "def worktree_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"How many non-bare worktrees are registered with this repository - stale ones included, never pruned.\"\"\"\n    if worktree is None:\n        return f\"{NOT_READ} (worktree: not identified)\"\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"git\", \"-C\", str(worktree), \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\", \"-z\"])\n        records = worktree_records(raw)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        return str(error)\n    count = sum(1 for record in records if \"bare\" not in record)\n    return f\"{count} (git worktree list; non-bare entries, stale registrations included)\"\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "end_line": 3499,
          "excerpt": "def worktree_digests(root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The 8-character record digests of every worktree `git worktree list` names for this root.\n\n    The listing is this repository's, including worktrees whose directories are missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        listing = _git_output(root, \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\")\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"worktree discovery failed: {error}\") from error\n    digests: list[str] = []\n    for line in listing.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(\"worktree \"):\n            continue\n        path = Path(line[len(\"worktree \") :]).resolve()\n        digest = record_key(\"\", path).rsplit(\"@\", 1)[1]\n        if digest not in digests:\n            digests.append(digest)\n    return digests\n",

          "excerpt": "def record_key(change: str, root: Path) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The record's name: the change and a digest of the resolved repository root.\n\n    Two worktrees may hold the same change folder, and one `release-loop` must not delete the\n    other's record or hand it another's state (R-2 of the review-swarm review).\n    \"\"\"\n    return f\"{change}@{hashlib.sha256(str(root.resolve()).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:8]}\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def tool_state(root: Path) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The digest of the worktree's `.venv/` tree, taken before the model runs (R-21).\n\n    `.venv/` is ignored by git: a file there is invisible to `changed_paths` and survives\n    `restore_baseline`, so this digest is the only thing that shows an overwritten tool, a planted\n    `*.pth` file or a replaced package. Every file maps to the SHA-256 of its bytes and every symlink\n    to its target; the runner's steps run with the interpreter, ruff and packages of this tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    state: dict[str, str] = {}\n    venv = root / \".venv\"\n    try:\n        info = venv.lstat()\n        if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode):\n            # Record the root link AND digest its tools: an unchanged link must not hide\n            # overwritten target bytes. os.walk traverses its root even with followlinks=False;\n            # nested directory links remain opaque, and _unlink_cache still rejects this root.\n            state[\".venv\"] = \"link:\" + str(venv.readlink())\n    except FileNotFoundError:\n        return state\n    except OSError:\n        return {\".venv\": UNREADABLE}\n\n    def unreadable_directory(error: OSError) -> None:\n        # os.walk otherwise silently skips failed scandir calls, hiding newly planted caches.\n        path = Path(error.filename) if error.filename is not None else venv\n        state[path.relative_to(root).as_posix()] = UNREADABLE\n\n    for directory, names, files in os.walk(venv, onerror=unreadable_directory):\n        for name in sorted([*names, *files]):\n            path = Path(directory) / name\n            relative = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()\n            try:\n                if path.is_symlink():\n                    state[relative] = \"link:\" + str(path.readlink())\n                elif path.is_file():\n                    state[relative] = hashli",

          "excerpt": "## Q-7 · When side refs are deleted\n\nasked: 2026-11-03\nanswer: \"nach dem Merge\" — after a change merges, the clean-up after merge (bead coding-harness-kpaq) deletes that change's refs under refs/stage2/attempts/<change>/, locally and on origin (asked 2026-11-03 under coding-harness-c99h, which this bead absorbed on 2026-11-12).\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: retention of side refs of stopped attempts.\n  Intention: the refs grow without bound (11 on origin, measured 2026-11-03).\n  Today: nothing deletes them.\n  Repository change: Options: delete after the merge; keep 14 days; keep forever.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of side refs that keep stopped attempts, facing unbounded growth or a retention rule, we decided that a change's attempt refs are deleted after its merge, locally and on origin, accepting that a stopped attempt of a merged change can no longer be inspected. — 2026-11-03\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::save_attempt",
          "end_line": 5963,
          "excerpt": "def save_attempt(root: Path, baseline: str, change: str, label: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Save the worktree as it stands after a failed call on a local ref; say where, or why not.\n\n    A failed call is not a worthless one: a run that hits a spent budget after hours of edits still\n    holds them (bead coding-harness-znc). The snapshot goes through a temporary index, so the real\n    index and the files stay untouched; tracked and untracked files go in, gitignored ones do not.\n    The temporary index is seeded with the baseline, as in `worktree_tree`, so a file tracked although\n    ignored stays in the snapshot. The commit's parent is the baseline, so `git diff <baseline> <ref>`\n    shows everything the run left in the tree: this attempt, any earlier attempt of the run whose tree\n    it started on, and the runner's own writes. The ref lives under `refs/stage2/attempts/`, which no\n    branch push carries. A save that fails is named and never blocks the restore that follows.\n    The commit carries the runner's own identity, so a machine without a configured git user (a CI\n    runner) saves as well, and the ref says who wrote it.\n    \"\"\"\n    stamp = utc_now().strftime(\"%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ\")\n    ref = f\"refs/stage2/attempts/{change}/{label}-{stamp}\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-save-\") as scratch:\n        env = {**os.environ, \"GIT_INDEX_FILE\": str(Path(scratch) / \"index\"), **SAVE_IDENTITY}\n        try:\n            _git_output(root, \"read-tree\", baseline, env=env)\n            _git_output(root, \"add\", \"-A\", \"--\", \".\", env=env)\n            tree = _git_output(root, \"write-tree\", env=env).strip()\n            commit = _git_output(\n                root, \"commit-tree\", tree, \"-p\", baseline, \"-m\", f\"stage2: saved {label} of {change}\", env=env\n            ).strip()\n            _git_output(root, \"update-ref\", ref, commit)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            return f\"saving the attempt failed ({error})\"\n    return f\"the attempt is saved at {ref} ({commit[:12]}); `git diff {baseline[:12]} {ref}` shows it\"\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "save_attempt",
          "start_line": 5935,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },

          "end_line": 6063,
          "excerpt": "def save_answer_evidence(root: Path, change: str, token: str, attempt: int, answer: str, key: str | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Save one attempt's full answer as protected evidence below the worktree's own git directory.\n\n    Written at the model-return boundary, before any HEAD check, verification or answer check can\n    stop the run, so a rejected answer stays diagnosable from what the model actually returned (bead\n    coding-harness-hgvp). The directory is git's resolved per-worktree `stage2/attempts/<change>/` - in\n    a linked worktree below the main checkout's `.git/worktrees/<name>/`, which the diagnostics name\n    as an absolute path - local evidence like `refs/stage2/attempts/`, tracked by no path and carried by no branch push.\n    The answer passes `protect_diagnostics` once on every route, the keyless ones included; an empty\n    or unavailable answer is recorded as such, never fabricated or retried. The file is created\n    exclusively, so an earlier attempt's evidence is never overwritten; an aliased destination, a\n    protection failure or a failed write raises, so no checkpoint stands on lost or unprotected\n    evidence. Returns the saved file, as the diagnostics name it.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        git_dir = Path(_git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"--absolute-git-dir\").strip())\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise CallFailed(f\"the answer evidence directory could not be resolved ({error})\") from error\n    if not git_dir.is_absolute():\n        git_dir = root / git_dir\n    body = protect_diagnostics(answer, key) if answer.strip() else \"(no answer was returned)\\n\"\n    directory = git_dir / \"stage2\" / \"attempts\" / change\n    expected = Path(os.path.realpath(git_dir)) / \"stage2\" / \"attempts\" / change\n    if directory.is_symlink() or os.path.realpath(directory) != str(expected):\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the answer evidence directory {directory} is not this worktree's own stage2/attempts/{change}; \"\n            \"no evidence is written and no checkpoint is made\"\n        )\n    destination = directory / f\"attempt-{attempt}-{token}.md\"\n    created = False\n    try:\n        directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        handle = os.open(destination, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o600)\n        created = True\n        with os.fdopen(handle, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as file:\n            file.write(body if body.endswith(\"\\n\") else body + \"\\n\")\n        if destination.is_symlink() or destination.stat().st_nlink > 1:\n            raise OSError(f\"the destination is aliased ({destination})\")\n    except OSError as error:\n        # Remove only the file this call created, never an earlier exclusive destination.\n        cleanup = \"no evidence is written\"\n        if created:\n            try:\n                destination.unlink()\n            except OSError as cleanup_error:\n                cleanup = f\"incomplete evidence remains at {destination} (cleanup failed: {cleanup_error})\"\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the answer evidence could not be saved ({error}); {cleanup} and no checkpoint is made\"\n        ) from error\n    return str(destination)\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_codex(\n    ctx: Context, prompt: str, resume: str | None = None, writable: bool = False, *, verb: str\n) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"One Codex call, first or resumed, pinned the same way. Returns (answer, thread id).\n\n    A review reads in the CLI's `read-only` sandbox; a draft writes in\n    `workspace-write`, and the runner puts back what lands outside the change\n    folder. No call takes a bypass flag (spec, criterion 1). The reasoning\n    effort is the caller verb's entry of `CODEX_EFFORTS`, passed explicitly on\n    every argv, a resumed call included; that a resumed thread actually runs at\n    that effort inside Codex is not asserted (bead coding-harness-yzk, Q-6).\n    Only the verbs `CODEX_EFFORTS` names (draft, repair, review) may carry a\n    Codex route; any other verb stops with a `KeyError` before the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    _, model, _ = CODEX\n    effort = CODEX_EFFORTS[verb]\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        answer_file = Path(tmp) / \"answer.md\"\n        command = [\"codex\", \"exec\"]\n        if resume:\n            command += [\"resume\", resume]\n        command += [\n            \"--json\",\n            \"-m\",\n            model,\n            \"-c\",\n            f'model_reasoning_effort=\"{effort}\"',\n            \"-c\",\n            f'sandbox_mode=\"{\"workspace-write\" if writable else \"read-only\"}\"',\n            \"--disable\",\n            \"hooks\",\n            \"--disable\",\n            \"memories\",\n            \"-o\",\n            str(answer_file),\n            prompt,\n        ]\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, foreign_env({}))\n        thread = thread_id(done.stdout or \"\")\n        if done.returncode != 0:\n            raise failed_with_answer_file(fail(\"codex\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\"), answer_file)\n        if thread is None:\n            raise failed_with_answer_file(fail(\"codex\", done, \"no thread.started event\"), answer_file)\n        try:\n            answer = answer_file.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n            raise fail(\"codex\", done, \"no answer file\") from error\n    return answer, thread\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_work_model(\n    ctx: Context,\n    prompt: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    writable: bool,\n    key: str | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One non-interactive Claude Code work call with file tools only.\"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        prompt_file = Path(tmp) / \"work-prompt.md\"\n        prompt_file.write_text(prompt, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        command = [\n            \"claude\",\n            \"-p\",\n            f\"Run the phase for {ctx.change} exactly as the appended instructions say.\",\n            \"--append-system-prompt-file\",\n            str(prompt_file),\n            \"--model\",\n            endpoint[1],\n        ]\n        if endpoint[2]:\n            command += [\"--effort\", endpoint[2]]\n        command += [\n            \"--tools\",\n            WORK_WRITE_TOOLS if writable else WORK_READ_TOOLS,\n            \"--restricted\",\n            \"--safe-mode\",\n            \"--strict-mcp-config\",\n            \"--permission-mode\",\n            \"acceptEdits\" if writable else \"dontAsk\",\n            \"--permission-prompts\",\n            \"none\",\n            \"--no-session-persistence\",\n            \"--output-format\",\n            \"text\",\n        ]\n        if key is None:\n            env = foreign_env({})\n        else:\n            config_dir = Path(tmp) / \"claude-config\"\n            config_dir.mkdir()\n            env = glm_env(key, config_dir, endpoint[1])\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, env, key, timeout=timeout, limit=limit)\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        error = fail(\"claude\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\", key)\n        # A failed call's printed answer travels along for the repair evidence; nothing else changes.\n        error.partial_answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n        raise error\n    answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n    if n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::restore_baseline",
          "end_line": 6117,
          "excerpt": "def restore_baseline(\n    root: Path,\n    baseline: str,\n    keep: set[Path],\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None = None,\n    planned: tuple[list[str], list[Path]] | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"After a failed model call, put every path but `keep` back at the baseline; say what was undone.\n\n    The runner refused pre-existing changes outside `keep` before the first call, so what differs\n    from the baseline outside it is the run's own - including a half-finished edit of a dead process.\n    Gitignored paths the attempt created are removed too: `changed_paths` cannot see them and\n    `git clean` without `-x` keeps them, so the run's earlier snapshot of the ignored files tells them\n    apart from the ones that stood before (phase 6, F-5). This implementation/repair rollback's\n    tracked destinations and newly created ignored cleanup paths are checked for an unsafe parent\n    before its first `git restore`, `git clean`, `unlink`, `rmtree` or parent removal; a refusal\n    leaves this recovery batch unwritten and ends the run.\n    \"\"\"\n    if planned is None:\n        planned = plan_baseline_restore(root, keep, ignored_before, baseline)\n    touched, created = planned\n    if not touched and not created:\n        return \"the worktree needed no restore.\"\n    spec = [f\":(exclude){path.as_posix()}\" for path in sorted(keep, key=lambda path: path.as_posix())]\n    try:\n        _git_output(root, \"restore\", f\"--source={baseline}\", \"--staged\", \"--worktree\", \"--\", \".\", *spec)\n        _git_output(root, \"clean\", \"-fdq\", \"--\", \".\", *spec)\n    except Refused as error:\n        listing = \", \".join([*touched, *(path.as_posix() for path in created)])\n        return f\"restoring the worktree to {baseline[:12]} failed ({error}); discard {listing} by hand.\"\n    removed = []\n    for relative in created:\n        path = root / relative\n        try:\n            if path.is_dir() and not path.is_symlink():\n                shutil.rmtree(path)\n            else:\n                path.unlink()\n        except OSError:\n            continue\n        removed.append(relative.as_posix())\n        parent = path.parent\n        while parent not in (root, parent.parent):\n            try:\n                parent.rmdir()\n            except OSError:\n                break\n            parent = parent.parent\n    undone = f\"undone: {', '.join(touched)}\" if touched else \"\"\n    ignored = f\"ignored paths removed: {', '.join(removed)}\" if removed else \"\"\n    inner = \"; \".join(part for part in (undone, ignored) if part)\n    return f\"the runner restored the worktree to {baseline[:12]} ({inner}); rerun the verb or add --stage2-off.\"\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "restore_baseline",
          "start_line": 6066,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
