Planted fault: forged state reached the checks, good code was lost, or the attempt was retried.\"\"\"\n    world.script(\n        claude=[\n            {\n                \"stdout\": \"implemented\",\n                \"plant\": {\"src/app.py\": \"value = 2\\n\"},\n                \"append\": {\"plans/changes/demo/findings.md\": \"\\nPhase 6 verdict: forged, 2026-10-28\\n\"},\n            }\n        ],\n        make=[{\"stdout\": \"green\\n\"}],\n    )\n    assert world.run(\"implement\") == 0\n    assert len(world.calls(\"claude\")) == 1, \"the attempt was retried for its findings edit\"\n    assert len(world.calls(\"make\")) == 1, \"the checks ran over the attempt twice\"\n    assert git(world.root, \"show\", \"HEAD:src/app.py\") == \"value = 2\", \"valid code was lost in the restoration\"\n    committed = git(world.root, \"show\", \"HEAD:plans/changes/demo/findings.md\")",

    "263092260c1ac0fda724743b2669b31affb56d4e": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-23T09:55:46Z",
      "body": "The third D-52 condition — every reader on one access point — was shown in\ne02c915. This commit takes the copy away:\n\n- .beads/issues.jsonl is no longer tracked, and is git-ignored so a\n  `git add -A` cannot bring it back. The export-identity gate and its four\n  tests are retired: there is no committed file left to compare.\n- The hosted CI hydrates the tracker, renders once and presets BEAD_RENDER;\n  every gate of the run reads that one render. Locally the access point\n  (scripts/bead_render.py) renders fresh through tools/bd, and without bd it\n  fails with both ways out — bootstrap or BEAD_RENDER — instead of reading a\n  stale copy.\n- The drift job hydrates too: plans-registry-strict reads the tracker, and\n  without the copy it would have crashed nightly. plans-registry and\n  plans-registry-strict declare needs_tracker; the schema now allows it in\n  both jobs.\n- The kit role geruest is dissolved: without the copy its remaining members\n  map to one export verdict, which the AK-6 test forbids. The stub files stay\n  with the export manifest. Two REIST_NICHT entries for tests that do not\n  travel were removed; the probe cap stays at 31.\n- verify_all.sh --ci measures the same gate set as the derived workflow\n  (finding 2 of the PR #32 review).\n- AGENTS.md house rules 2 and 4, README, plans/_README.md: the render is the\n  contract; a pull request body names every bead it opens, changes or closes\n  (maintainer, 2026-09-23, D-52 successor; the CI job summary follows as\n  bead coding-harness-1jg.4).\n- The empty gate-placement change package is archived (its bead 1jg.2 closed\n  with PR #32).\n\nStarted by a Cline session that stopped mid-way (uncommitted, last edit\n10:28); finished and corrected by Claude Code.\n\nVerified 2026-09-23: make verify VERIFY GREEN (325 passed, 15 skipped);\nverify_all.sh --job drift VERIFY GREEN, measuring the tracker locally.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

      "author_utc": "2026-11-14T18:59:01Z",
      "body": "The tree baseline is measured only for a run with protected work - the one\ncase that reuses cheap results across the admission. The cheap phase's not-run header\nnames every blocking red gate instead of claiming a stop at the first\n(L2-7). A refusal names the paths that moved. The worker rule lives once in\nverify_run.worker_bound, used by the full and the targeted check (L2-6).\nThe gates' default interpreter comes from the env argument (L2-9).\n\nL2-1 is rejected: ruff and pytest self-ignore their caches; the new proof\ntest_real_tool_caches_keep_the_baseline_stable runs both inside a checkout\nwithout user-level excludes and stays stable.\n\nOrchestrator hand edit (Opus subagent, maintainer's word of 2026-11-14).\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

    "82a013b92bfab78830cdeeb982d597e217216c64": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-20T11:20:58Z",
      "body": "Main brings the shared two-phase scheduler (scripts/verify_run.py, PR #416,\nbead coding-harness-bxxt.6), venv_guard (PR #415) and the journal citation\ngate (PR #418). The slip counter (bead coding-harness-bxxt.7) is carried into\nmain's structure; nothing of either side is reverted.\n\nConflict resolutions:\n\n- scripts/verify_duration.py: main's in-process writers stay (record_start,\n  record_gate, record_end with root, state_root and env). The slip counter's\n  comparison evidence is attached to them: record_start records\n  common_git_dir for its root, reads the runner-owned comparison variables\n  from the scheduler's env (_comparison_fields(env), falling back to the\n  process environment for the CLI), and creates the targeted history beside\n  the duration history under the same state root at the first version-2\n  marker. append_event/_open_history take both the slip counter's\n  `destination` (the targeted history) and main's keyword `state_root`;\n  targeted_history_path accepts a state root too. Imports keep both\n  Sequence and dataclass/field; _git and _gate_file_digest take main's form.\n  New COMPARISON_ENV_NAMES lists the three variables.\n- scripts/stage2.py: main's scheduler path stays the one full check. The\n  slip counter's single entry point full_verify(root, env, key, change,\n  prepare) is kept, now built on main's body: prepare runs first, outside\n  any admission (main's intent for the full-mode attempt), then\n  intent-to-add, then _scheduled_verify with\n  verify_duration.full_run_context(_checked_tree(root, change), change)\n  added to the scheduler's environment. verify_attempt's full mode hands its\n  preparation (format, cheap checks, ledger clearing, prepare_derived) to\n  full_verify as `prepare` instead of duplicating the intent-to-add,\n  scheduler and cleanup block (house rule 9: one path).\n- scripts/verify_run.py (no conflict, one addition): after recording the\n  start, run_verification drops the comparison variables from the gates'\n  environment, so a gate never inherits them and a check a gate starts is\n  never recorded as a second full run of the same change and tree.\n- tests/test_stage2.py: both sides' new tests kept. The slip end-to-end test\n  now uses the world's committed gate list instead of creating its own\n  decisions/ folder, and its `make` stub is the scheduler's protected gate:\n  it records nothing (the scheduler records start, gate and end) and fails if\n  it inherits the comparison context.\n- tests/test_verify_duration.py: the slip counter's version of the\n  derived-never-persisted test (the reader `slips` is exposed) replaces\n  main's deferral assertions; main's criterion-8 completion-context test is\n  kept.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9DrQg7dkn7zUzrqUEk\n",

A diff header that cannot be read with\ncertainty (a quoted name) is scanned in full.\n\nMaintainer's decision of 2026-10-07 on open item O-4 of the stage-2 change;\nthe accepted consequence is that a real key committed in a test file is not\nfound. The secret patterns live in the maintainer's denylist, not in this\nscript, so the marker is a name prefix and each machine sets it itself.\n\nThe log now runs with --no-renames (the staged scan already did) so a diff\nheader names one path, and splits message from patch by a marker line the log\nformat writes. Docstring and WORKFLOW state the exemption.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",

    "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T14:07:20Z",
      "body": "A feature can decide something that belongs in an architecture decision\nrecord, and nothing here asked. Each change anchor now states its class;\na feature states its name and a proposal, and owes an answer file\ndecisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml in the LakeSwitch pilot's format, so\nLakeSwitch can read it unchanged.\n\nscripts/check_adr_answers.py is the gate and the one reader of the\nformat: strict YAML (a duplicate key is refused, a bare no is a boolean),\nevery rule of the answer file, active and archived anchors, one report\nline per cause, exit 0/1/3. It holds existence and format only; it cannot\nsee who wrote or merged an answer, and no line claims it.\n\nscripts/harness.py decide adr asks each open question in a terminal, or\nrecords one answer the maintainer stated elsewhere (--change, --answer,\n--reason, --stated-in). It writes the answer files and a commit message\nwhere git says, and never stages, commits, pushes or merges. Who answered\ncomes from provenance.yaml, which now maps decisions/answers/ to\nhuman-decided with owner_role framework-architect.\n\nThe gate is in decisions/gates.yaml (block, not floor), ci.yml is\nregenerated, both scripts and their tests travel with the kit and the\nanswers do not. The kit probe's exemption for\ntest_the_two_manifests_really_disagree_somewhere is struck and its cap\nlowered to 31: with four more mechanism files the throwaway repository\npasses that test now.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",

      "author_utc": "2026-11-15T10:48:31Z",
      "body": "Conflict resolution, file by file:\n\n- scripts/stage2.py `full_verify`: the branch's scheduler body (cheap gates\n  before admission, the scheduler holds the admission); the docstring takes\n  main's \"targeted route\" wording.\n- scripts/stage2.py `verify_draft`: main's version (bead coding-harness-0swp).\n  The draft runs the registry's local document gates directly through\n  `run_gates`, outside any admission, instead of the branch's scheduler on the\n  `docs` subset. This narrows the draft leg of criterion 10 of this change\n  (draft document verification \"uses the same admission-by-gate behavior\"):\n  it takes no admission at all now, and its bound is the per-gate tool limit,\n  not the shared VERIFY_SECONDS allowance. Left for the maintainer to confirm;\n  spec.md is unchanged.\n- tests/test_stage2.py: the draft tests take main's expectations; tests that\n  reach the full check keep the branch's shape. The world's `bash` stand-in\n  regains its document-vector branch (keyed on the test module's DOCS_ARGV,\n  since main removed stage2.DOCS_VERIFY), because the world's gate list\n  declares the document subset as `bash scripts/verify_all.sh --job docs`.\n  A new `uncovered_implementation` helper reaches the full check, since main's\n  `successful_implementation` now takes the targeted route.\n- tests/test_stage2_fail_fast.py, tests/test_verify_duration.py: both sides\n  kept.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

It states\nthat the guard does not exist yet, so until it is built the bounds are\nstated, not enforced.\n\nThe decision-continuity map now names ADR 0006 for D-3, D-7 and the\ncoordinator permission, so the gate checks that the new ADR speaks for\nthem.\n\nStatus stays \"proposed\"; the maintainer's signed commit accepts it and\nrecords the supersession in ADR 0001, ADR 0005 and the target document.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

          "excerpt": "def tool_state(root: Path) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The digest of the worktree's `.venv/` tree, taken before the model runs (R-21).\n\n    `.venv/` is ignored by git: a file there is invisible to `changed_paths` and survives\n    `restore_baseline`, so this digest is the only thing that shows an overwritten tool, a planted\n    `*.pth` file or a replaced package. Every file maps to the SHA-256 of its bytes and every symlink\n    to its target; the runner's steps run with the interpreter, ruff and packages of this tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    state: dict[str, str] = {}\n    venv = root / \".venv\"\n    try:\n        info = venv.lstat()\n        if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode):\n            # Record the root link AND digest its tools: an unchanged link must not hide\n            # overwritten target bytes. os.walk traverses its root even with followlinks=False;\n            # nested directory links remain opaque, and _unlink_cache still rejects this root.\n            state[\".venv\"] = \"link:\" + str(venv.readlink())\n    except FileNotFoundError:\n        return state\n    except OSError:\n        return {\".venv\": UNREADABLE}\n\n    def unreadable_directory(error: OSError) -> None:\n        # os.walk otherwise silently skips failed scandir calls, hiding newly planted caches.\n        path = Path(error.filename) if error.filename is not None else venv\n        state[path.relative_to(root).as_posix()] = UNREADABLE\n\n    for directory, names, files in os.walk(venv, onerror=unreadable_directory):\n        for name in sorted([*names, *files]):\n            path = Path(directory) / name\n            relative = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()\n            try:\n                if path.is_symlink():\n                    state[relative] = \"link:\" + str(path.readlink())\n                elif path.is_file():\n                    state[relative] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()\n            except OSError:\n                state[relative] = UNREADABLE\n    return state\n",

          "excerpt": "def tool_problem(root: Path, before: dict[str, str] | None) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The first path of `.venv/` that is not what the runner saw before the call, named; `None` when none is.\n\n    A new or content-changed regular file below an exact `__pycache__` component inside `.venv/` is\n    deleted before any runner-owned step: pytest's assertion rewriting writes bytecode there during\n    an attempt, and a deleted cache is rebuilt, so that write is normalized instead of refused (bead\n    coding-harness-q94b). Every other difference keeps the refusal with the first path named. The\n    baseline bookkeeping stays narrow: each successful unlink immediately removes that path's old\n    entry from the shared `before` dictionary, even if a later check fails. Nothing that survives is rebaselined; recreated caches are deleted again.\n    \"\"\"\n    if before is None:\n        return None\n\n    def differences(now: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:\n        return sorted(path for path in before.keys() | now.keys() if before.get(path) != now.get(path))\n\n    now = tool_state(root)\n    cleaned = False\n    for path in sorted(before.keys() | now.keys()):\n        if UNREADABLE in (before.get(path), now.get(path)):\n            return f\"`{path}` cannot be inspected, and a tool the attempt wrote is not run\"\n        if not _is_cache_path(path):\n            continue  # retain the difference, but still clean eligible caches that sort later\n        if before.get(path) == now.get(path):\n            continue\n        if before.get(path, \"\").startswith(\"link:\"):\n            continue  # removing a baseline symlink is never a cache-byte change\n        deleted = _unlink_cache(root, path)\n        if deleted is None:\n            continue  # a linked or non-regular cache-looking path stays a difference\n        if not deleted:\n            return f\"`{path}` cannot be deleted, and a tool the attempt wrote is not run\"\n        before.pop(path, None)  # record each runner-owned deletion even if a later check ",

          "excerpt": "def _private_repository(root: Path, destination: Path, checkout: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create a proof's private repository at `destination`, its checkout materialized at `checkout`.\n\n    The clone carries the source's objects wholesale - unreferenced ones included - with no\n    hardlinks and no object alternates, so the proof runs against bytes of its own and a local\n    object copy carries the fixed tree `worktree_tree` wrote without a ref. Every source ref is\n    preserved under its own name first, so a ref the source already had stays a move in the\n    proof's store, not an accidental creation; the remote configuration goes, so an ordinary\n    Git operation in the proof has no path back to the source. HEAD is detached at `checkout`\n    when it names the baseline commit, or at the source's HEAD for a fixed-code tree id.\n    `checkout` is read into the index and the working tree, leaving a baseline clean against\n    its own commit. The source's refs, index and worktree are read here, never\n    written (spec, criteria 1 and 6).\n    \"\"\"\n    # Snapshot before copying objects: later source refs may name objects the clone never saw.\n    refs = _ref_targets(root)\n    head = refs.pop(\"HEAD\").split(\" \", 1)[0]\n    _git_output(root, \"clone\", \"--quiet\", \"--no-hardlinks\", str(root), str(destination))\n    # An alternates file makes the clone depend on another object store. Refuse rather than\n    # silently discarding that dependency and assuming all required objects were copied.\n    alternates = destination / \".git\" / \"objects\" / \"info\" / \"alternates\"\n    if alternates.exists() or alternates.is_symlink():\n        raise Refused(\"the private repository contains objects/info/alternates\")\n    _git_output(destination, \"remote\", \"remove\", \"origin\")\n    if _git_output(destination, \"cat-file\", \"-t\", checkout).strip() == \"commit\":\n        head = checkout\n    # Detach HEAD in its own transaction before updating its former referent. Git\n    # otherwise refuses both names in one transaction, even with --no-deref.\n    _git_output(\n        destination,\n        \"update-ref\",\n        \"--no-deref\",\n        \"--stdin\",\n        stdin=(\n            f\"start\\nupdate HEAD {head}\\nprepare\\ncommit\\nstart\\n\"\n            + \"\".join(f\"update {name} {target}\\n\" for name, target in refs.items() if \" \" not in target)\n            + \"prepare\\ncommit\\n\"\n        ),\n    )\n    # Measurements retain both the resolved object and symbolic target. Restore\n    # symbolic refs by kind, using symbolic-ref for Git versions without symref-update.\n    for name, target in refs.items():\n        _, _, symbolic = target.partition(\" \")\n        if symbolic:\n            _git_output(destination, \"symbolic-ref\", name, symbolic)\n    _git_output(destination, \"read-tree\", \"--reset\", \"-u\", checkout)\n",

          "excerpt": "def record_key(change: str, root: Path) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The record's name: the change and a digest of the resolved repository root.\n\n    Two worktrees may hold the same change folder, and one `release-loop` must not delete the\n    other's record or hand it another's state (R-2 of the review-swarm review).\n    \"\"\"\n    return f\"{change}@{hashlib.sha256(str(root.resolve()).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:8]}\"\n",

          "end_line": 3499,
          "excerpt": "def worktree_digests(root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The 8-character record digests of every worktree `git worktree list` names for this root.\n\n    The listing is this repository's, including worktrees whose directories are missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        listing = _git_output(root, \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\")\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"worktree discovery failed: {error}\") from error\n    digests: list[str] = []\n    for line in listing.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(\"worktree \"):\n            continue\n        path = Path(line[len(\"worktree \") :]).resolve()\n        digest = record_key(\"\", path).rsplit(\"@\", 1)[1]\n        if digest not in digests:\n            digests.append(digest)\n    return digests\n",

          "excerpt": "def other_record_keys(change: str, root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The active record keys of this change under this repository's other worktrees, sorted.\n\n    A key is active when its record's `loop.md` stands in the current state directory: an emptied\n    directory after a release, and the research siblings a release leaves, are no record. The key of\n    this worktree, of a removed worktree and of another repository is never derived, so it is never\n    named, and no record's contents are read here - existence is all discovery needs.\n    \"\"\"\n    current = record_key(change, root)\n    keys = []\n    for key in record_keys_of_worktrees(change, root):\n        if key != current and (record_base() / key / \"loop.md\").exists():\n            keys.append(key)\n    return keys\n",

          "end_line": 5320,
          "excerpt": "def _supersede_loop_locked(root: Path, change: str, keys: list[str], reason: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Archive another worktree's loop record and restart the loop here (bead coding-harness-e82i).\n\n    The maintainer repeats `--supersedes <key>` for every active other-worktree key a refusal names.\n    Every selected record is read only under its lock, moved whole - everything a release would\n    delete, `availability.json` included, never the research siblings - into one unique archive\n    directory beside the records, and accounted for in one `Loop restarted:` line. The next\n    `review-loop` here is a fresh run whose rounds continue after the highest round ever assigned; the\n    old key can no longer continue the archived record.\n    \"\"\"\n    reason = \" \".join(reason.split())\n    if not reason:\n        raise Refused(\"--supersedes needs a non-empty --reason: the maintainer's request must be readable.\")\n    keys = sorted(set(keys))\n    current = record_key(change, root)\n    base = record_base()\n    archive_base = base.parent / ARCHIVE_DIR_NAME\n    listed = set(record_keys_of_worktrees(change, root))\n    for key in keys:\n        if re.fullmatch(rf\"{re.escape(change)}@[0-9a-f]{{8}}\", key) is None:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"`{key}` is no record key of {change}: a key is `<change>@<digest>`, as the refusals name them.\"\n            )\n        if key == current:\n            raise Refused(f\"`{key}` is this worktree's own record key; supersession takes another worktree's key.\")\n        if key not in listed:\n            raise Refused(\n                f\"`{key}` names no worktree of this repository (`git worktree list`); the record of a removed \"\n                \"worktree or of another repository is not superseded.\"\n            )\n        if (base / key).is_symlink():\n            raise Refused(f\"the record directory of `{key}` is a symlink; supersession takes a real record directory.\")\n    listing = _git_output(root, \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\")\n    worktrees = {\n        record_key(change, Path(line[9:])): Path(line[9:])\n",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Worktrees — one per change",
          "end_line": 911,
          "excerpt": "### Worktrees — one per change\n\nWritten 2026-09-29 from D-5 (worktrees in the repository, through the tool's own\nmechanism), ADR 0006 (parallel work, one worktree per session) and the\nmeasurement of 2026-09-23 (`docs/research/2026-09-23-worktree-tracker-writes.md`).\nThe same rule holds in `lakeswitch-ai`, with the differences its\n`docs/workflow.md` §9 lists.\n\n1. **One change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.** Two sessions\n   never share a worktree, and nobody switches the branch of the main checkout\n   while another session runs.\n2. **In the repository, under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`.** That directory is in\n   `.gitignore` already, and it is where Claude Code puts its own worktrees\n   (`claude --worktree <name>`, and a sub-agent's `isolation: worktree`). By\n   hand: `git fetch origin && git worktree add -b <branch>\n   .claude/worktrees/<name> origin/main`. `bd worktree create` works as well but\n   writes the worktree's path into the tracked `.gitignore`, which is one more\n   change in the diff. Sibling directories beside the repository are retired\n   (D-5); worktrees that still sit there are finished and removed, not moved.\n3. **Always from a freshly fetched `origin/main`.** A worktree on a stale base\n   produces a pull request that is behind before it opens.\n4. **The tracker needs nothing.** `tools/bd` in a worktree finds the main\n   checkout's tracker through the shared git directory — no variable, no\n   redirect file, no copy. Concurrent writers lose nothing and a contested\n   claim has exactly one winner (measured 2026-09-23 with bd 1.3.0). Who may\n   write is house rule 4: the first writing session writes the tracker; every\n   other session claims its one bead with `tools/bd update <id> --claim\n   --actor <session>` and leaves its handover comment on that bead, nothing\n   more. After tracker writes: `tools/bd dolt push` first, `git push` second.\n5. **Omnigent starts inside the worktree.** Omnigent runs Claude Code as its\n   authors intend (`omnigent claude --use-native-config`, ADR 0006); the session\n   is started from the worktree's directory, so its hooks, its\n   `.claude/settings.json` and `tools/bd` all resolve there. Omnigent's own\n   tools reach the session as `mcp__omnigent__<tool>`, and neither Claude\n   Code's path rules, the hooks on its file tools nor Omnigent's own Claude Code\n   hook see what they do. Each one that writes, runs, spawns or changes state is\n   therefore denied by name in `.claude/settings.json`; the read-only ones stay\n   usable, except one that may send the task text to a routing judge\n   (`sys_advise_models`), which the user is asked about each time\n   (`permissions.ask`; decision of 2026-09-29). Read-only tools stay usable.\n   The default policy in `tools/omnigent/` is the second layer, rendered from\n   that same list.           "excerpt": "def tool_state(root: Path) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The digest of the worktree's `.venv/` tree, taken before the model runs (R-21).\n\n    `.venv/` is ignored by git: a file there is invisible to `changed_paths` and survives\n    `restore_baseline`, so this digest is the only thing that shows an overwritten tool, a planted\n    `*.pth` file or a replaced package. Every file maps to the SHA-256 of its bytes and every symlink\n    to its target; the runner's steps run with the interpreter, ruff and packages of this tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    state: dict[str, str] = {}\n    venv = root / \".venv\"\n    try:\n        info = venv.lstat()\n        if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode):\n            # Record the root link AND digest its tools: an unchanged link must not hide\n            # overwritten target bytes. os.walk traverses its root even with followlinks=False;\n            # nested directory links remain opaque, and _unlink_cache still rejects this root.\n            state[\".venv\"] = \"link:\" + str(venv.readlink())\n    except FileNotFoundError:\n        return state\n    except OSError:\n        return {\".venv\": UNREADABLE}\n\n    def unreadable_directory(error: OSError) -> None:\n        # os.walk otherwise silently skips failed scandir calls, hiding newly planted caches.\n        path = Path(error.filename) if error.filename is not None else venv\n        state[path.relative_to(root).as_posix()] = UNREADABLE\n\n    for directory, names, files in os.walk(venv, onerror=unreadable_directory):\n        for name in sorted([*names, *files]):\n            path = Path(directory) / name\n            relative = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()\n            try:\n                if path.is_symlink():\n                    state[relative] = \"link:\" + str(path.readlink())\n                elif path.is_file():\n                    state[relative] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()\n            except OSError:\n                state[relative] = UNREADABLE\n    return state\n",

          "excerpt": "def save_attempt(root: Path, baseline: str, change: str, label: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Save the worktree as it stands after a failed call on a local ref; say where, or why not.\n\n    A failed call is not a worthless one: a run that hits a spent budget after hours of edits still\n    holds them (bead coding-harness-znc). The snapshot goes through a temporary index, so the real\n    index and the files stay untouched; tracked and untracked files go in, gitignored ones do not.\n    The temporary index is seeded with the baseline, as in `worktree_tree`, so a file tracked although\n    ignored stays in the snapshot. The commit's parent is the baseline, so `git diff <baseline> <ref>`\n    shows everything the run left in the tree: this attempt, any earlier attempt of the run whose tree\n    it started on, and the runner's own writes. The ref lives under `refs/stage2/attempts/`, which no\n    branch push carries. A save that fails is named and never blocks the restore that follows.\n    The commit carries the runner's own identity, so a machine without a configured git user (a CI\n    runner) saves as well, and the ref says who wrote it.\n    \"\"\"\n    stamp = utc_now().strftime(\"%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ\")\n    ref = f\"refs/stage2/attempts/{change}/{label}-{stamp}\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-save-\") as scratch:\n        env = {**os.environ, \"GIT_INDEX_FILE\": str(Path(scratch) / \"index\"), **SAVE_IDENTITY}\n        try:\n            _git_output(root, \"read-tree\", baseline, env=env)\n            _git_output(root, \"add\", \"-A\", \"--\", \".\", env=env)\n            tree = _git_output(root, \"write-tree\", env=env).strip()\n            commit = _git_output(\n                root, \"commit-tree\", tree, \"-p\", baseline, \"-m\", f\"stage2: saved {label} of {change}\", env=env\n            ).strip()\n            _git_output(root, \"update-ref\", ref, commit)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            return f\"saving the attempt failed ({error})\"\n    return f\"the attempt is saved at {ref} ({commit[:12]}); `git diff {baseline[:12]} {ref}` shows it\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def restore_baseline(\n    root: Path,\n    baseline: str,\n    keep: set[Path],\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None = None,\n    planned: tuple[list[str], list[Path]] | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"After a failed model call, put every path but `keep` back at the baseline; say what was undone.\n\n    The runner refused pre-existing changes outside `keep` before the first call, so what differs\n    from the baseline outside it is the run's own - including a half-finished edit of a dead process.\n    Gitignored paths the attempt created are removed too: `changed_paths` cannot see them and\n    `git clean` without `-x` keeps them, so the run's earlier snapshot of the ignored files tells them\n    apart from the ones that stood before (phase 6, F-5). This implementation/repair rollback's\n    tracked destinations and newly created ignored cleanup paths are checked for an unsafe parent\n    before its first `git restore`, `git clean`, `unlink`, `rmtree` or parent removal; a refusal\n    leaves this recovery batch unwritten and ends the run.\n    \"\"\"\n    if planned is None:\n        planned = plan_baseline_restore(root, keep, ignored_before, baseline)\n    touched, created = planned\n    if not touched and not created:\n        return \"the worktree needed no restore.\"\n    spec = [f\":(exclude){path.as_posix()}\" for path in sorted(keep, key=lambda path: path.as_posix())]\n    try:\n        _git_output(root, \"restore\", f\"--source={baseline}\", \"--staged\", \"--worktree\", \"--\", \".\", *spec)\n        _git_output(root, \"clean\", \"-fdq\", \"--\", \".\", *spec)\n    except Refused as error:\n        listing = \", \".join([*touched, *(path.as_posix() for path in created)])\n        return f\"restoring the worktree to {baseline[:12]} failed ({error}); discard {listing} by hand.\"\n    removed = []\n    for relative in created:\n        path = root / relative\n        try:\n            if path.is_dir() and not path.is_symlink():\n                shutil.rmtree(path)\n            else:\n                path.unlink()\n        except OSError:\n            continue\n        removed.append(relative.as_posix())\n        parent = path.parent\n        while parent not in (root, parent.parent):\n            try:\n                parent.rmdir()\n            except OSError:\n                break\n            parent = parent.parent\n    undone = f\"undone: {', '.join(touched)}\" if touched else \"\"\n    ignored = f\"ignored paths removed: {', '.join(removed)}\" if removed else \"\"\n    inner = \"; \".join(part for part in (undone, ignored) if part)\n    return f\"the runner restored the worktree to {baseline[:12]} ({inner}); rerun the verb or add --stage2-off.\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def alias_baseline(root: Path, baseline: str, ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None) -> AliasBaseline:\n    \"\"\"The links that stood before the attempt: tracked ones from the baseline, ignored ones by their stat.\n\n    Recovery compares every link in a destination's parent chain with this record instead of\n    simulating what the recovery would do to it (decisions.md, Q-2): an attempt's own link, or a\n    baseline link it replaced or changed, refuses the batch before its first mutation.\n    \"\"\"\n    links: dict[Path, Path] = {}\n    try:\n        for entry in filter(None, _git_output(root, \"ls-tree\", \"-rz\", baseline).split(\"\\0\")):\n            metadata, name = entry.split(\"\\t\", 1)\n            mode, _, oid = metadata.split()\n            if mode == \"120000\":\n                links[Path(name)] = Path(_git_output(root, \"cat-file\", \"blob\", oid))\n    except (Refused, OSError, ValueError) as error:\n        raise RestorationRefused(\n            f\"restoration is refused: the links of the rollback baseline cannot be read ({error})\"\n        ) from error\n    return links, dict(ignored_before or {})\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_codex(\n    ctx: Context, prompt: str, resume: str | None = None, writable: bool = False, *, verb: str\n) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"One Codex call, first or resumed, pinned the same way. Returns (answer, thread id).\n\n    A review reads in the CLI's `read-only` sandbox; a draft writes in\n    `workspace-write`, and the runner puts back what lands outside the change\n    folder. No call takes a bypass flag (spec, criterion 1). The reasoning\n    effort is the caller verb's entry of `CODEX_EFFORTS`, passed explicitly on\n    every argv, a resumed call included; that a resumed thread actually runs at\n    that effort inside Codex is not asserted (bead coding-harness-yzk, Q-6).\n    Only the verbs `CODEX_EFFORTS` names (draft, repair, review) may carry a\n    Codex route; any other verb stops with a `KeyError` before the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    _, model, _ = CODEX\n    effort = CODEX_EFFORTS[verb]\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        answer_file = Path(tmp) / \"answer.md\"\n        command = [\"codex\", \"exec\"]\n        if resume:\n            command += [\"resume\", resume]\n        command += [\n            \"--json\",\n            \"-m\",\n            model,\n            \"-c\",\n            f'model_reasoning_effort=\"{effort}\"',\n            \"-c\",\n            f'sandbox_mode=\"{\"workspace-write\" if writable else \"read-only\"}\"',\n            \"--disable\",\n            \"hooks\",\n            \"--disable\",\n            \"memories\",\n            \"-o\",\n            str(answer_file),\n            prompt,\n        ]\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, foreign_env({}))\n        thread = thread_id(done.stdout or \"\")\n        if done.returncode != 0:\n            raise failed_with_answer_file(fail(\"codex\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\"), answer_file)\n        if thread is None:\n            raise failed_with_answer_file(fail(\"codex\", done, \"no thread.started event\"), answer_file)\n        try:\n            answer = answer_file.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n            raise fail(\"codex\", done, \"no answer file\") from error\n    return answer, thread\n",

          "excerpt": "def worktree_digests(root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The 8-character record digests of every worktree `git worktree list` names for this root.\n\n    The listing is this repository's, including worktrees whose directories are missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        listing = _git_output(root, \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\")\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"worktree discovery failed: {error}\") from error\n    digests: list[str] = []\n    for line in listing.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(\"worktree \"):\n            continue\n        path = Path(line[len(\"worktree \") :]).resolve()\n        digest = record_key(\"\", path).rsplit(\"@\", 1)[1]\n        if digest not in digests:\n            digests.append(digest)\n    return digests\n",

          "end_line": 6255,
          "excerpt": "def run_work_model(\n    ctx: Context,\n    prompt: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    writable: bool,\n    key: str | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One non-interactive Claude Code work call with file tools only.\"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        prompt_file = Path(tmp) / \"work-prompt.md\"\n        prompt_file.write_text(prompt, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        command = [\n            \"claude\",\n            \"-p\",\n            f\"Run the phase for {ctx.change} exactly as the appended instructions say.\",\n            \"--append-system-prompt-file\",\n            str(prompt_file),\n            \"--model\",\n            endpoint[1],\n        ]\n        if endpoint[2]:\n            command += [\"--effort\", endpoint[2]]\n        command += [\n            \"--tools\",\n            WORK_WRITE_TOOLS if writable else WORK_READ_TOOLS,\n            \"--restricted\",\n            \"--safe-mode\",\n            \"--strict-mcp-config\",\n            \"--permission-mode\",\n            \"acceptEdits\" if writable else \"dontAsk\",\n            \"--permission-prompts\",\n            \"none\",\n            \"--no-session-persistence\",\n            \"--output-format\",\n            \"text\",\n        ]\n        if key is None:\n            env = foreign_env({})\n        else:\n            config_dir = Path(tmp) / \"claude-config\"\n            config_dir.mkdir()\n            env = glm_env(key, config_dir, endpoint[1])\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, env, key, timeout=timeout, limit=limit)\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        error = fail(\"claude\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\", key)\n        # A failed call's printed answer travels along for the repair evidence; nothing else changes.\n        error.partial_answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n        raise error\n    answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n    if not answer.strip():\n        raise fail(\"claude\", done, \"the answer is empty\", key)\n    return answer\n",

          "end_line": 12403,
          "excerpt": "def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        description=__doc__,\n        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,\n        allow_abbrev=False,\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\"verb\", choices=sorted([*VERBS, \"session\", \"prepare-explore\"]))\n    parser.add_argument(\"change\", nargs=\"?\", default=\"\", help=\"folder name under plans/changes/\")\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"row_status\",\n        nargs=\"?\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"ROW=STATUS\",\n        help=(\n            \"triage only: the loop row and its new status, e.g. 'L1-1=taken — not a test'; \"\n            \"refuses ordinary taken for test-only locations: use taken — not a test — <reason>\"\n        ),\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"reason_text\",\n        nargs=\"?\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"REASON\",\n        help=(\n            \"triage only: the decision's own single-line reason; \"\n            \"the Broke a test proof mark stays the runner's; triage supplies no repair evidence\"\n        ),\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--stage2-off\",\n        nargs=\"?\",\n        const=\"stage 2 disabled by caller\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"REASON\",\n        help=\"use the Stage-1 route for explore, implement or repair and record the optional reason\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--model\",\n        default=None,\n        help=\"session only: the model id, exactly as model-endpoints.yaml lists it\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--class\",\n        dest=\"klass\",\n        default=None,\n        choices=CLASSES,\n        help=\"explore only: the change class before a spec exists, agreeing with every stated one\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--availability-reported\",\n        dest=\"availability_reported\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"ID\",\n        help=(\n            \"the id printed by prepare-loop (review-loop) or prepare-explore (explore, swarm classes) \"\n            \"after its selection was reported to the maintainer\"\n        ),\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--seats\",\n        action=\"append\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"TRIO=MODELS\",\n        help=\"prepare-explore only: the maintainer's Go models for a trio, e.g. repository=a,b\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--handover\",\n        default=None,\n        help=\"session only: a handover file inside the worktree (default: the change's handover.md)\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--stage-failed\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"MODEL\",\n        help=\"release-loop only: retire the stage this model belongs to, so the loop can go on\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--reason\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"TEXT\",\n        help=\"release-loop only: why the stage is retired or the loop restarted; lands in the record\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--restart\",\n        action=\"store_true\",\n        help=\"release-loop only, on the maintainer's request: restart a completed loop as a fresh run\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--supersedes\",\n        action=\"append\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"KEY\",\n        help=(\n            \"release-loop --restart only: archive the named other worktree's active loop record and \"\n            \"restart here; repeat for every active other-worktree key a refusal names\"\n        ),\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\"--root\", default=str(REPO_ROOT), help=argparse.SUPPRESS)\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    _LAUNCH_STOPPED.clear()\n    # SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGQUIT stop the run like Ctrl-C: the running programs' groups are\n    # killed before the exit (DL-B-5, F6-8). The handlers are the runner's only while main runs,\n    # and only from the main thread.\n    previous = {}\n    if threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread():\n        for signum in TERMINATING_SIGNALS:\n            previous[signum] = signal.signal(signum, _terminate)\n    try:\n        return _run(args)\n    except (KeyboardInterrupt, Terminated) ",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::The runner is the only way",
          "end_line": 1535,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",

          "end_line": 3499,
          "excerpt": "def worktree_digests(root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The 8-character record digests of every worktree `git worktree list` names for this root.\n\n    The listing is this repository's, including worktrees whose directories are missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        listing = _git_output(root, \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\")\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"worktree discovery failed: {error}\") from error\n    digests: list[str] = []\n    for line in listing.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(\"worktree \"):\n            continue\n        path = Path(line[len(\"worktree \") :]).resolve()\n        digest = record_key(\"\", path).rsplit(\"@\", 1)[1]\n        if digest not in digests:\n            digests.append(digest)\n    return digests\n",

          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",

          "excerpt": "def implement(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: Flash, one Flash repair and Sonnet fallback, checked and committed by the runner.\"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else GLM_FLASH\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    time_log(ctx.plan)  # Require the initial time heading before a model call starts.\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        routes = [\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash\", None),\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash-repair\", \"first Flash post-run check failed\"),\n            (SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", \"two Flash post-run checks failed\"),\n        ]\n    else:\n        key = None\n        routes = [(SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", stage2_off)]\n    standing: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def snapshot() -> str:\n        text = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        standing[\"text\"] = text\n        return text\n\n    def check(_answer: str) -> list[str]:\n        # The implementing model writes code, never loop state. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike.           "end_line": 11036,
          "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb. A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2). Before the failure is decided, findings.md is restored outright: every post-run check, cheap\n    or full, reads the runner's file, an edit alone fails nothing, and a completed attempt that edited\n    it carries a quoted restore notice under its audit line (spec, criteria 8 and 9).\n\n    A verb that passes `retain_answer` keeps every attempt's full answer: right at the model-return\n    boundary, before any HEAD check, verification or answer check can stop the run, the protected\n    answer is saved as local evidence and its location joins the attempt's diagnostics - the parser's\n    rejections, the call and verify failures included - and is printed on success (bead\n    coding-harness-hgvp). A failed call keeps the output it returned.\n\n    A verb that passes `protect_lifecycle` snapshots the change's lifecycle fields (`status`,\n    `implementation_status`) in spec, optional design and plan right before every call. Once the\n    attempt's changed-file measurement stands, changed effective values restore the trusted whole\n    frontmatter block, preserving body edits and YAML anchors - before verification, the\n    derived preparation or the checkpoint reads the documents. The same per-attempt snapshot serves\n    the early exits: a failed call and a retry recover whole snapshotted inputs, a moved HEAD keeps\n    its commit while the safe working-tree fields go back, a refused checkpoint puts the fields back\n    before the run stops, and every attempt's bookkeeping names what was restored or says the fields\n    stayed unchanged (status-fields-restore).           "excerpt": "def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        description=__doc__,\n        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,\n        allow_abbrev=False,\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\"verb\", choices=sorted([*VERBS, \"session\", \"prepare-explore\"]))\n    parser.add_argument(\"change\", nargs=\"?\", default=\"\", help=\"folder name under plans/changes/\")\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"row_status\",\n        nargs=\"?\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"ROW=STATUS\",\n        help=(\n            \"triage only: the loop row and its new status, e.g. 'L1-1=taken — not a test'; \"\n            \"refuses ordinary taken for test-only locations: use taken — not a test — <reason>\"\n        ),\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"reason_text\",\n        nargs=\"?\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"REASON\",\n        help=(\n            \"triage only: the decision's own single-line reason; \"\n            \"the Broke a test proof mark stays the runner's; triage supplies no repair evidence\"\n        ),\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--stage2-off\",\n        nargs=\"?\",\n        const=\"stage 2 disabled by caller\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"REASON\",\n        help=\"use the Stage-1 route for explore, implement or repair and record the optional reason\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--model\",\n        default=None,\n        help=\"session only: the model id, exactly as model-endpoints.yaml lists it\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--class\",\n        dest=\"klass\",\n        default=None,\n        choices=CLASSES,\n        help=\"explore only: the change class before a spec exists, agreeing with every stated one\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--availability-reported\",\n        dest=\"availability_reported\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"ID\",\n        help=(\n            \"the id printed by prepare-loop (review-loop) or prepare-explore (explore, swarm classes) \"\n            \"after its selection was reported to the maintainer\"\n        ),\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--seats\",\n        action=\"append\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"TRIO=MODELS\",\n        help=\"prepare-explore only: the maintainer's Go models for a trio, e.g. repository=a,b\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--handover\",\n        default=None,\n        help=\"session only: a handover file inside the worktree (default: the change's handover.md)\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--stage-failed\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"MODEL\",\n        help=\"release-loop only: retire the stage this model belongs to, so the loop can go on\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--reason\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"TEXT\",\n        help=\"release-loop only: why the stage is retired or the loop restarted; lands in the record\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--restart\",\n        action=\"store_true\",\n        help=\"release-loop only, on the maintainer's request: restart a completed loop as a fresh run\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--supersedes\",\n        action=\"append\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"KEY\",\n        help=(\n            \"release-loop --restart only: archive the named other worktree's active loop record and \"\n            \"restart here; repeat for every active other-worktree key a refusal names\"\n        ),\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\"--root\", default=str(REPO_ROOT), help=argparse.SUPPRESS)\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n    _LAUNCH_STOPPED.clear()\n    # SIGTERM, SIGHUP and SIGQUIT stop the run like Ctrl-C: the running programs' groups are\n    # killed before the exit (DL-B-5, F6-8). The handlers are the runner's only while main runs,\n    # and only from the main thread.\n    previous = {}\n    if threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread():\n        for signum in TERMINATING_SIGNALS:\n            previous[signum] = signal.signal(signum, _terminate)\n    try:\n        return _run(args)\n    except (KeyboardInterrupt, Terminated) ",

          "excerpt": "def run_work_model(\n    ctx: Context,\n    prompt: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    writable: bool,\n    key: str | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One non-interactive Claude Code work call with file tools only.\"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        prompt_file = Path(tmp) / \"work-prompt.md\"\n        prompt_file.write_text(prompt, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        command = [\n            \"claude\",\n            \"-p\",\n            f\"Run the phase for {ctx.change} exactly as the appended instructions say.\",\n            \"--append-system-prompt-file\",\n            str(prompt_file),\n            \"--model\",\n            endpoint[1],\n        ]\n        if endpoint[2]:\n            command += [\"--effort\", endpoint[2]]\n        command += [\n            \"--tools\",\n            WORK_WRITE_TOOLS if writable else WORK_READ_TOOLS,\n            \"--restricted\",\n            \"--safe-mode\",\n            \"--strict-mcp-config\",\n            \"--permission-mode\",\n            \"acceptEdits\" if writable else \"dontAsk\",\n            \"--permission-prompts\",\n            \"none\",\n            \"--no-session-persistence\",\n            \"--output-format\",\n            \"text\",\n        ]\n        if key is None:\n            env = foreign_env({})\n        else:\n            config_dir = Path(tmp) / \"claude-config\"\n            config_dir.mkdir()\n            env = glm_env(key, config_dir, endpoint[1])\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, env, key, timeout=timeout, limit=limit)\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        error = fail(\"claude\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\", key)\n        # A failed call's printed answer travels along for the repair evidence;           "excerpt": "def run_codex(\n    ctx: Context, prompt: str, resume: str | None = None, writable: bool = False, *, verb: str\n) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"One Codex call, first or resumed, pinned the same way.           "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::save_attempt",
          "end_line": 5963,
          "excerpt": "def save_attempt(root: Path, baseline: str, change: str, label: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Save the worktree as it stands after a failed call on a local ref; say where, or why not.\n\n    A failed call is not a worthless one: a run that hits a spent budget after hours of edits still\n    holds them (bead coding-harness-znc). The snapshot goes through a temporary index, so the real\n    index and the files stay untouched; tracked and untracked files go in, gitignored ones do not.\n    The temporary index is seeded with the baseline, as in `worktree_tree`, so a file tracked although\n    ignored stays in the snapshot. The commit's parent is the baseline, so `git diff <baseline> <ref>`\n    shows everything the run left in the tree: this attempt, any earlier attempt of the run whose tree\n    it started on, and the runner's own writes. The ref lives under `refs/stage2/attempts/`, which no\n    branch push carries. A save that fails is named and never blocks the restore that follows.\n    The commit carries the runner's own identity, so a machine without a configured git user (a CI\n    runner) saves as well, and the ref says who wrote it.\n    \"\"\"\n    stamp = utc_now().strftime(\"%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ\")\n    ref = f\"refs/stage2/attempts/{change}/{label}-{stamp}\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-save-\") as scratch:\n        env = {**os.environ, \"GIT_INDEX_FILE\": str(Path(scratch) / \"index\"), **SAVE_IDENTITY}\n        try:\n            _git_output(root, \"read-tree\", baseline, env=env)\n            _git_output(root, \"add\", \"-A\", \"--\", \".\", env=env)\n            tree = _git_output(root, \"write-tree\", env=env).strip()\n            commit = _git_output(\n                root, \"commit-tree\", tree, \"-p\", baseline, \"-m\", f\"stage2: saved {label} of {change}\", env=env\n            ).strip()\n            _git_output(root, \"update-ref\", ref, commit)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            return f\"saving the attempt failed ({error})\"\n    return f\"the attempt is saved at {ref} ({commit[:12]}); `git diff {baseline[:12]} {ref}` shows it\"\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "save_attempt",

          "excerpt": "## Q-7 · When side refs are deleted\n\nasked: 2026-11-03\nanswer: \"nach dem Merge\" — after a change merges, the clean-up after merge (bead coding-harness-kpaq) deletes that change's refs under refs/stage2/attempts/<change>/, locally and on origin (asked 2026-11-03 under coding-harness-c99h, which this bead absorbed on 2026-11-12).\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: retention of side refs of stopped attempts.\n  Intention: the refs grow without bound (11 on origin, measured 2026-11-03).\n  Today: nothing deletes them.\n  Repository change: Options: delete after the merge; keep 14 days; keep forever.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of side refs that keep stopped attempts, facing unbounded growth or a retention rule, we decided that a change's attempt refs are deleted after its merge, locally and on origin, accepting that a stopped attempt of a merged change can no longer be inspected. — 2026-11-03\n",

          "end_line": 4059,
          "excerpt": "def record_key(change: str, root: Path) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The record's name: the change and a digest of the resolved repository root.\n\n    Two worktrees may hold the same change folder, and one `release-loop` must not delete the\n    other's record or hand it another's state (R-2 of the review-swarm review).\n    \"\"\"\n    return f\"{change}@{hashlib.sha256(str(root.resolve()).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:8]}\"\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "record_key",
          "start_line": 4053,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::worktree_digests",
          "end_line": 3499,
          "excerpt": "def worktree_digests(root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The 8-character record digests of every worktree `git worktree list` names for this root.\n\n    The listing is this repository's, including worktrees whose directories are missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        listing = _git_output(root, \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\")\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"worktree discovery failed: {error}\") from error\n    digests: list[str] = []\n    for line in listing.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(\"worktree \"):\n            continue\n        path = Path(line[len(\"worktree \") :]).resolve()\n        digest = record_key(\"\", path).rsplit(\"@\", 1)[1]\n        if digest not in digests:\n            digests.append(digest)\n    return digests\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "worktree_digests",

          "truncated": false

          "excerpt": "def implement(root: Path, change: str, stage2_off: str | None = None) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 4: Flash, one Flash repair and Sonnet fallback, checked and committed by the runner.\"\"\"\n    first = SONNET if stage2_off is not None else GLM_FLASH\n    ctx = preflight(root, change, first, required=(\"plan.md\",))\n    allowed = {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\n    refuse_preexisting(root, allowed)\n    baseline = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\").strip()\n    time_log(ctx.plan)  # Require the initial time heading before a model call starts.\n    ignored_before = ignored_snapshot(root)\n    if stage2_off is None:\n        key = read_secret(\"GLM_KEY\")\n        if key is None:\n            raise Refused(f\"GLM_KEY is not in the secrets file {secrets_path()}.\")\n        routes = [\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash\", None),\n            (GLM_FLASH, key, \"flash-repair\", \"first Flash post-run check failed\"),\n            (SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", \"two Flash post-run checks failed\"),\n        ]\n    else:\n        key = None\n        routes = [(SONNET, None, \"stage-1\", stage2_off)]\n    standing: dict[str, str] = {}\n\n    def snapshot() -> str:\n        text = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        standing[\"text\"] = text\n        return text\n\n    def check(_answer: str) -> list[str]:\n        # The implementing model writes code, never loop state. The runner puts findings.md back\n        # before this check (spec, criterion 8), so a model edit alone never fails here; the\n        # comparison stays as the guard that the restore held (review row L3-2).\n        now = ctx.findings.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") if ctx.findings.exists() else \"\"\n        problem = findings_body_problem(standing.get(\"text\", \"\"), now)\n        return [problem] if problem else []\n\n    run_attempts(\n        ctx,\n        \"implement\",\n        routes,\n        lambda diagnostics, _endpoint, inputs: implementation_prompt(ctx, baseline, diagnostics, inputs),\n        baseline,\n        key,\n        ignored_before,\n        commit_message=f\"feat({change}): implement accepted plan\",\n        closing=(\n            \"implementation post-run checks failed after the allowed attempts; why each attempt failed and \"\n            f\"the files it changed: {ctx.findings.relative_to(root)}\"\n        ),\n        answer_check=check,\n        snapshot_findings=snapshot,\n        restore_findings=lambda text: restore_work_input(root, ctx.findings, text.encode(\"utf-8\")),\n        # Every model route's post-run check is targeted when the coverage is safe (bead\n        # coding-harness-0swp): the covered initial, retry and stage-1 routes alike. New production\n        # code without a reachable test refuses before any test runs or a fallback is admitted.\n        verify_mode=\"targeted\",\n        new_file_guard=True,\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"Codex repairs both kinds, with a fresh Codex re-check\",\nbecause it implements the maintainer's model choice without weakening the\nrepair evidence contract.\n\n1. **Codex repairs all taken findings in one batch** through `python3\n   scripts/stage2.py repair <change>`: loop-record rows, released loop rows\n   and phase-6 findings. Each Codex attempt starts `gpt-6.1-sol` at effort\n   `max` in a fresh session, with the existing `workspace-write` configuration,\n   hooks and memories off, and no added directory, automatic approval or\n   bypass. Repair reads no GLM key and never routes to `glm-coding-plan`.\n2. **Only post-run failures advance the chain:** Codex; a fresh Codex attempt\n   with the first attempt's diagnostics; Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` on\n   Stage 1 with both diagnostics.           "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Decider: maintainer ·\n  prepared by Claude Code. Acceptance is the merge commit; the review header\n  remains pending.\n* Date: 2026-11-08 · takes effect on merge.\n\n## Context\n\nADR 0021 decision 6 ends \"requiring `make verify` green after repair as\ntoday\". The workflow\nrecords a full run at 12 to 13 minutes (measured 2026-10-30); the lane times\nthis decision should shorten are not measured.\n\nThe maintainer had already let a targeted check stand in for a full one after\na hand repair by the orchestrator (2026-10-30, bead coding-harness-24ag). The\nchange `repair-targeted-check` extends that rule to runner repairs and adds an\nenforced full check before phase 6 (`plans/changes/repair-targeted-check/`,\non the branch of #343). Without this amendment the ADR would contradict the\ngate the runner enforces (review-loop row L8-3 of that change; bead\ncoding-harness-firy).\n\n## Decision\n\nADR 0021 decision 6's last sentence is replaced by:\n\n1.           "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. There is no commit signing in\nCoding Harness (ADR 0008, 2026-09-30). A pull request that adds, changes or\nremoves a file `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` — an ADR, an ADR\nanswer, the rule set — is a **decision pull request**: its title is\n`decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n`decision`, and its body begins with the block from\n`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` — what is decided, that the merge\nis the confirmation, what it confirms, the options and what follows. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\".\n\nWhat this does not do:\n\n- The gate holds existence and format only. It cannot see who wrote an answer\n  or who merged it.\n- Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account, so nobody can tell from\n  GitHub who pressed merge. The merge rule is a rule, not proof.\n- The ask rules in `.claude/settings.json` are a brake against an accidental\n  merge, not a lock. Since the night-stall-guard change (2026-11-09) they match\n  precise",
