          "citation": "docs/adr/0017-codex-repairs-taken-findings.md::Considered Options",
          "end_line": 70,
          "excerpt": "## Considered Options\n\n* **Codex repairs both kinds, with a fresh Codex re-check** — chosen (Q-1, Q-2).\n* **Keep GLM 5.3 repairs** — preserves model separation but spends the budget\n  the maintainer wants to reserve.\n* **Codex repairs only one kind of finding** — retains two repair routes and\n  some GLM repair spend; rejected in Q-2.\n* **Another phase-6 model or an extra loop round** — adds independent model\n  review or another pass, but moves its budget or changes the round count;\n  rejected in Q-1.\n* **GLM as last attempt, or no last attempt** — respectively spends Z.ai\n  budget or abandons a repair after two post-check failures; Q-3 chose Sonnet.\n* **Automatic fallback on Codex call failure** — avoids an explicit restart\n  but hides an availability-driven budget switch; rejected in Q-4.\n\n",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::The runner is the only way",
          "end_line": 1535,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n",

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::Sessions across checkouts",
          "end_line": 186,
          "excerpt": "## Sessions across checkouts\n\n- **Another session in the same checkout:** say so before changing a file,\n  committing or switching the branch, and offer a worktree. House rule 4 holds\n  for the tracker meanwhile.\n- **Worktrees: one change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.**\n  A worktree lives under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`, is branched from a freshly fetched `origin/main`,\n  and is removed after the merge; tracker access, claims and sibling directories: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3.\n  Each new checkout or worktree runs `make venv` and `bash tools/pi/install.sh` once before `make verify`\n  (`PYTHON=` picks a 3.12+ interpreter; one that does not match the lock fails the suite, bead\n  coding-harness-ei0; the Pi tests and the swarms need the pinned Pi, bead coding-harness-hs0o).\n- **A text-only change (Markdown outside `scripts/`, `tests/`, `prompts/`,\n  `decisions/`) skips the local `make verify`;** CI is its gate.\n- **Omnigent starts inside the worktree** (ADR 0006). Its default policy (`tools/omnigent/`) is a second layer;\n  nothing depends on it alone. Which tools are denied or asked, and why: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3, \"Worktrees\".\n- **What could not be read is \"not read\", never \"none\"** — an unopened file\n  and an empty query say different things.\n- **A standing rule belongs in the repository's `AGENTS.md`** — every harness\n  reads it; chat, memory and a user file do not reach the next one. Where an\n  agent may not write it (lakeswitch: `human-decided`), propose the text.\n- **Research about this repository lives in `docs/research/`.** A vault note,\n  chat or rendered page is a view of it: it names the source path and commit,\n  and a finding is never first written there. Personal reasons to care stay\n  outside the repository.\n- **The maintainer's Claude Code display** (status line, session entry, handover safety net, `/handover`) lives\n  in `tools/claude-code/`; change it there and reinstall with `tools/claude-code/install.sh`, never only in `~/.claude`.\n- **Sub-agents survive a budget pause** (maintainer, 2026-10-06). Each commits\n  and pushes after every green step and ends its report with a `Resume:` line;\n  the orchestrator keeps a list (agent id, branch, last pushed commit, next\n  step) and resumes or restarts there. One change at a time, with few agents\n  and a visible queue. A long runner job starts in the harness's background mode, one job per call — never with `&` or `nohup` inside a command, which ends without a notice and leaves a lane idle unseen (maintainer, 2026-11-04). Every night run arms a recurring 30-minute wake, keeps the machine awake, and checks and logs its lanes as described in `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, ‘Night runs’.\n- **Pull requests stay mergeable:** synced daily, asked about after five working\n  days, three per hot file, sliced over ~800 lines, merged through the merge queue at their exact head (without it: one at a time against the new head once every check completed); questions in one 15:00 block (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n- **Findings returned as text** (when the harness refuses a reviewer's write)\n  are committed unchanged by the orchestrator, which says so in the commit.\n  MINOR rows on tests, security or false statements are repaired without asking; style rows\n  are accepted limits named in the PR. A second finding of one mechanism ends case repair; a mechanism no choke point closes gets a `Boundary` in its spec; a hand repair marks the loop row `fixed`, regenerates the index after a header edit and stamps after local midnight (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4).\n- **An exhausted review ladder goes to phase 6** (maintainer, 2026-11-20): when\n  `review-loop` refuses because every stage of its run is consumed and the last\n  round was not clean, and every taken row of that round is repaired, the lane\n  goes to the phase-6 review instead of a new loop run; phase 6 checks that last\n  repair. Reason: a run's history cannot be reset, and asking each time stopped\n  lanes overnight.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included. The prompts ask them\n   to read nothing outside the worktree and the repository's git directory — a\n   request, not a lock, and the doctrine says so in those words. The\n   maintainer accepted this as a residual risk on 2026-09-30, choosing it over\n   a proof of about one hour's work, for the reviewers. Explore and implement\n   widen what is read and add writes; whether that acceptance reaches them is\n   for the maintainer to confirm by merging this pull request.\n5. **Explore and implement run on GLM 5.3 Flash — decided, not built.** They\n   run there for every change, whatever its class: the class is stated in the\n   spec, after exploration. The runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) has no verb for\n   either phase yet, no plan marking assigns a step to Flash, and no effort is\n   set for it. Until that is built, `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3 runs the two phases:\n   Haiku 4.5 explores and Sonnet 5.5 implements. This is an open item of the\n   change, not a claim that it works.\n6. **Endpoints are architecture; the models on them are declaration\n   (amended on 2026-10-30).** Which endpoints framework content may reach\n   stays this ADR's matter (decision 2) and its amendments'. Which models run\n   on a declared endpoint is set by `model-endpoints.yaml` alone, each through\n   a dated data-terms reading that the runner checks before every call.\n   Admitting, marking, removing or excluding a model there is a decision pull\n   request on that `human-decided` file, never an amendment of this ADR: the\n   OpenCode Go catalog changes too often to be architecture. A newly admitted\n   model takes a place in the review loop's ladder only; any other role\n   (explore, implem",

          "excerpt": "# ADR 0025 — A runner repair passes a targeted check; one full make verify precedes phase 6\n\n* Status: accepted by the merge of the pull request that carries this file.\n  Until that merge, open is proposed and closed is rejected. Amends ADR 0021\n  decision 6; supersedes no ADR. Amends no D- or O-number.\n* Review: the maintainer decided on 2026-11-08, in the conversation, that\n  ADR 0021 decision 6 changes together with the runner change that makes a\n  repair pass on a targeted check (pull request #343, bead\n  coding-harness-gxwg), and that the amendment travels in a decision pull\n  request of its own (answer \"Fertig machen + ADR-PR\"), and answered its\n  interview the same day (`plans/changes/adr-repair-check/decisions.md`,\n  Q-1 to Q-5). Decider: maintainer ·\n  prepared by Claude Code. Acceptance is the merge commit; the review header\n  remains pending.\n* Date: 2026-11-08 · takes effect on merge.\n\n## Context\n\nADR 0021 decision 6 ends \"requiring `make verify` green after repair as\ntoday\". Every runner repair therefore paid for a full `make verify`, even for\na narrow edit. Full checks run one at a time under the machine-wide verify\nadmission (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`, \"One admission per user and machine\"), so a\nrepair cycle waits for the lock and then for the whole suite. The workflow\nrecords a full run at 12 to 13 minutes (measured 2026-10-30); the lane times\nthis decision should shorten are not measured.\n\nThe maintainer had already let a targeted check stand in for a full one after\na hand repair by the orchestrator (2026-10-30, bead coding-harness-24ag). The\nchange `repair-targeted-check` extends that rule to runner repairs and adds an\nenforced full check before phase 6 (`plans/changes/repair-targeted-check/`,\non the branch of #343). Without this amendment the ADR would contradict the\ngate the runner enforces (review-loop row L8-3 of that change; bead\ncoding-harness-firy).\n\n## Decision\n\nADR 0021 decision 6's last sentence is replaced by:\n\n1. After a runner repair the runner runs a targeted check: the tests linked\n   to the touched files, the prior retry selections, ruff on the touched\n   Python files, and the gates the touched file kinds feed.\n2. When that selection is not safe, the full `make verify` runs instead, as\n   the fallback for that repair.\n3. One fresh green full `make verify` on the head under review is required\n   before phase 6. A red, unstartable or timed-out run stops the review;\n   runner audit lines in `findings.md` do not count as a new head.\n4. The orchestrator measures repair duration, verify-lock wait and every\n   failure the full check before phase 6 finds that a targeted check missed,\n   over five changes or two weeks, whichever comes first, and reports the\n   result to the maintainer.\n5. This rule holds from the merge. The testing-strategy spike (bead\n   coding-harness-1ga5) may amend or replace it with an ADR of its own; the\n   measurement of point 4 enters that spike as a finding.\n\nThe rest of ADR 0021 decision 6 stands unchanged.\n\n## Consequences\n\n* A repair cycle no longer waits for a full run unless its selection is\n  unsafe; the effect on cycle and lane times is not yet measured.\n* A targeted check can miss a test the touch map does not link to a touched\n  file. The full `make verify` before phase 6 catches such a miss before the\n  review, and CI remains the full gate of the pull request.\n* A repair can be marked fixed on a targeted result that the full check\n  later turns red; that red stops phase 6 until it is repaired.\n\n## Validation\n\n* #343 carries the runner implementation and its criterion tests; this\n  pull request carries only the ADR text.\n* CI on this pull request is its gate; merge, not this draft, accepts the ADR.\n\n## Implement and draft amendment — the targeted check covers more verbs, 2026-11-12\n\nThe maintainer answered the interview of the change\n`targeted-check-more-verbs` on 2026-11-11 and 2026-11-12\n(`plans/changes/targeted-check-more-verbs/decisions.md`, Q-1 to Q-6; bead\ncoding-harne",

          "excerpt": "## 3. Stuck: where, and why\n\n- **Red-first cannot pass a fix that lives only in test code.** The repair\n  runner demands a new test that is red on the old production code. Three\n  times tonight the right fix was a test or a test helper over code that\n  was already right (yzk L1-1, eao F-1/F-2, yzk L3-1); every runner attempt\n  failed, one by moving checker logic into `scripts/stage2.py` to satisfy\n  the check. The orchestrating session completed these by hand or through\n  an Opus sub-agent. Proposed bead: the runner accepts a \"guard test\" mark\n  whose test plants the fault itself.\n- **The runner misreads repaired loop rows.** For eao it reported \"L1-1: no\n  fixed line\" for a row already repaired by hand, and read words such as\n  `expected:` and `Resume:` from the answer as finding ids. Proposed bead.\n- **The loop silently dropped a round's findings.** Round 2 on the research\n  swarm (mimo-v2.6-flash) numbered its rows `R2-1`… instead of `L2-1`…; the\n  runner kept them as raw text in `findings.md` and reported \"0 rows\", so\n  round 3 never ran. The phase-6 review found it; one of the seven rows was\n  real and new (raised as F-10). Proposed bead: refuse or renumber\n  non-conforming row ids instead of reporting a clean round.\n- **The \"Broke a test\" cell accepts only `yes` or `no`.** A mark with an\n  explanation made the next loop round refuse; the explanation now lives\n  in the commit message.\n- **A Codex repair wrote its own handover file** into the research-swarm\n  branch; removed (`560160d`). The repair prompt should forbid it.\n- **zs7 implement and phase-6 repair failed three attempts each**; the\n  second failure was real: anchoring the date to the statement's end left\n  a live record (`plans/changes/codex-drafts/decisions.md` Q-1) unmeasured.\n  Completed by hand; the allowance is documented in spec, design and plan.\n- **Research swarm implement** failed three runner attempts (three\n  doctrine tests red); an Opus sub-agent completed it. The leak check then\n  blocked the loop on two synthetic test keys in new test files; they are\n  built from parts now. Not done: the offline Pi capture (spec build\n  step 2). An earlier gap between collected and run tests (2081 against\n  2054) did not recur at phase 6 (2100 collected, 2084 passed + 16 skipped);\n  its cause was not measured.\n- **ADR 0018 is claimed by four open changes** (interview-context, research\n  swarm, isolated attempts, loop-until-clean); each later merge renumbers.\n- **Isolated attempts** (coding-harness-s9r) started late: implement\n  (GLM 5.3 Flash) began at about 06:35 in `.claude/worktrees/isolated-attempts`;\n  its result is recorded in that branch's `findings.md`.\n- **Codex usage limit** was hit at about 20:50 the evening before (\"try\n  again at 10:48 PM\"); the runner printed only \"codex call failed: exit 1\",\n  the reason stood only in `~/.codex/sessions/…/rollout-*.jsonl`.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "# ADR 0021 — The review loop runs until a clean round: a free swarm first, then the ladder\n\n* Status: accepted by the merge of the pull request that carries this file.\n  Until that merge, the pull request's state is the decision's state: open\n  is proposed, closed is rejected. Amends ADR 0011 decisions 3 and 8 and\n  ADR 0017 decision 6; supersedes no ADR. Amends no D- or O-number.\n* Review: the maintainer chose the direction in Q-1 through Q-8 on\n  2026-10-14 and corrected free admission, the Flash round, live refresh and\n  configurable selection in Q-9/Q-10 and the addenda of 2026-10-16\n  and paid retention, free exclusions and replacement routing in Q-11 to Q-13\n  on 2026-10-17 (`plans/changes/loop-until-clean/decisions.md`). Acceptance\n  is the merge commit, recorded nowhere else; the header's review remains\n  pending · Decider: maintainer · prepared by Codex through stage 2.\n* Date: 2026-10-16 · takes effect on merge.\n\n## Context\n\nThe loop currently stops at three rounds (ADR 0011 decision 3; ADR 0017\ndecision 6). It refused a needed fourth round in the first night run\n(`docs/journal/handover/2026-10-12-night-run-first-rehearsal.md`, section 4).\nA clean first round still admits round 2, and each round calls one model\n(`plans/changes/loop-until-clean/research.md`, exploration at `e0cea42`,\n2026-10-14). This does not meet the request to review until clean or the\nimplementation-review swarm decision.\n\nOn 2026-10-16 the maintainer clarified that all free Go models found by the\nrun's check enter automatically, and that the three named Flash models\nreview together after the free swarm. These answers replace the earlier\ndraft's undeclared-free-model exclusion and sequential Flash interpretation.\nThe existing ADR answer names this amendment as 0021.\n\nThe repository-pinned Pi and its isolation remain ADR 0019's launch path.\nThe final decisions addendum of 2026-10-16 (after `a0d5bc8`) records a\ncorrected Pi 1.2.0 source reading: `core/remote-catalog-provider.js` obtains\nmodels from `pi.dev` and caches them for four hours;\n`package-manager-cli.js` forces refresh through `pi update --models` (the\nflag spelling the pinned CLI measures in phase 4).\nThe maintainer requested live retrieval and retained Pi's catalog after\nits distinction from Go's own endpoint was explained. They also requested\neasy later changes to the free-model rule. Catalog membership still does\nnot measure whether a model call is actually billed free.\n\n## Decision Drivers\n\n- End on a review with no accepted findings rather than a fixed round count.\n- Honor the free-first and parallel-three-Flash order the maintainer stated.\n- Bound paid review by declared models without repeating the final rung.\n- Admit unread ",

          "excerpt": "def test_every_git_launch_of_the_runner_goes_through_run_git() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Decision Q-8: one helper starts git, so no launch can lose git's diagnostic or the C locale (F6-4, F6-5).\n\n    Modelled on the source check that counts launches naming GIT: a command list whose first element\n    is GIT may stand only inside `run_git`, and there is no exemption.\n    \"\"\"\n    tree = ast.parse((REPO_ROOT / \"scripts\" / \"stage2.py\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    helpers = [node for node in tree.body if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name == \"run_git\"]\n    assert len(helpers) == 1, \"scripts/stage2.py must define exactly one module-level run_git\"\n    inside = {id(node) for node in ast.walk(helpers[0])}\n\n    def names_git(node: ast.AST) -> bool:\n        return (\n            isinstance(node, ast.List | ast.Tuple)\n            and bool(node.elts)\n            and isinstance(node.elts[0], ast.Name)\n            and node.elts[0].id == \"GIT\"\n        )\n\n    bypass = sorted(node.lineno for node in ast.walk(tree) if names_git(node) and id(node) not in inside)\n    assert bypass == [], f\"a git launch bypasses run_git at line(s) {bypass}\"\n    own = [node for node in ast.walk(helpers[0]) if names_git(node)]\n    assert len(own) == 1, \"run_git must build exactly one git command\"\n    calls = [\n        node.lineno\n        for node in ast.walk(tree)\n        if isinstance(node, ast.Call) and isinstance(node.func, ast.Name) and node.func.id == \"run_git\"\n    ]\n    # Seven launch sites at 00d83c67: show, merge-base, archive, merge-base --is-ancestor, cat-file -e,\n    # and the two wrappers `_git_output` and `_git_bytes`.\n    assert len(calls) >= 7, f\"fewer run_git calls than the seven launch sites this check was written against: {calls}\"\n    # Handled failures must name both a nonzero code and its expected diagnostic,\n    # at direct launches and at wrapper calls; a bare tuple of codes cannot establish absence.\n    for call in (node for node in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(node, ast.Call)):\n        if not (isinstance(call.func, ast.Name) and call.func.id in {\"run_git\", \"_git_output\", \"_git_bytes\"}):\n            continue\n        for keyword in call.keywords:\n            if keyword.arg != \"allow\":\n                continue\n            value = keyword.value\n            if isinstance(value, ast.Name):\n                assert value.id == \"allow\", f\"line {call.lineno} forwards an unknown handled-failure declaration\"\n                continue\n            assert isinstance(value, ast.Dict) and value.keys, (\n                f\"line {call.lineno} handles Git failure with bare exit codes instead of diagnostic patterns\"\n            )\n            for",

          "excerpt": "## Q-5 · A failed model call\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — implement the 2026-10-16 decision: a failed model call (error, time or usage limit) counts as a failed attempt and falls through to the next route, building on its saved state; the switch and its reason stand visibly in findings.md; the doctrine sentence in docs/WORKFLOW.md §3 is amended with an ADR addendum. A leak refusal still never falls back.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: what follows a model call that ends without an answer.\n  Intention: on 2026-11-22 two u1ha repairs stopped at the Codex usage limit and Sonnet had to be started by hand.\n  Today: the call stops; docs/WORKFLOW.md §3 says a failed model process stops instead of silently changing route.\n  Repository change: Options: A fall through on every failed call except a leak refusal; B only for known causes; C keep stopping.\n  Architecture change: the §3 doctrine sentence, with an ADR addendum.\n\nIn the context of failed model calls, facing a stop or a visible fall-through, we decided to fall through to the next route with the reason recorded, to achieve night runs that do not stall, accepting that an unknown failure is answered by the next route instead of a stop. — 2026-11-22\n\n",

Planted fault: the repair's private proof repositories or a source worktree\n    entry are left behind.\"\"\"\n    repair_world(world)\n    made: list[str] = []\n    original_mkdtemp = stage2.tempfile.mkdtemp\n\n    def recording_mkdtemp(*args: object, **kwargs: object) -> str:\n        path = original_mkdtemp(*args, **kwargs)  # type: ignore[arg-type]\n        if Path(path).name.startswith(\"stage2-\"):\n            made.append(path)\n        return path\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(stage2.tempfile, \"mkdtemp\", recording_mkdtemp)\n    refs_before = {line.split()[-1] for line in git(world.root, \"for-each-ref\").splitlines()}\n    assert world.run(\"repair\") == 0\n    listed = git(world.root, \"worktree\", \"list\").splitlines()\n    assert len(listed) == 1, listed\n    assert git(world.root, \"status\", \"--porcelain\") == \"\"\n    assert {line.split()[-1] for line in git(world.root, \"for-each-ref\").splitlines()} == refs_before\n    assert made, \"no private repository was created for the proofs\"\n    for left in made:\n        assert not Path(left).exists(), left\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::save_attempt",
          "end_line": 5963,
          "excerpt": "def save_attempt(root: Path, baseline: str, change: str, label: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Save the worktree as it stands after a failed call on a local ref; say where, or why not.\n\n    A failed call is not a worthless one: a run that hits a spent budget after hours of edits still\n    holds them (bead coding-harness-znc). The snapshot goes through a temporary index, so the real\n    index and the files stay untouched; tracked and untracked files go in, gitignored ones do not.\n    The temporary index is seeded with the baseline, as in `worktree_tree`, so a file tracked although\n    ignored stays in the snapshot. The commit's parent is the baseline, so `git diff <baseline> <ref>`\n    shows everything the run left in the tree: this attempt, any earlier attempt of the run whose tree\n    it started on, and the runner's own writes. The ref lives under `refs/stage2/attempts/`, which no\n    branch push carries. A save that fails is named and never blocks the restore that follows.\n    The commit carries the runner's own identity, so a machine without a configured git user (a CI\n    runner) saves as well, and the ref says who wrote it.\n    \"\"\"\n    stamp = utc_now().strftime(\"%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ\")\n    ref = f\"refs/stage2/attempts/{change}/{label}-{stamp}\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-save-\") as scratch:\n        env = {**os.environ, \"GIT_INDEX_FILE\": str(Path(scratch) / \"index\"), **SAVE_IDENTITY}\n        try:\n            _git_output(root, \"read-tree\", baseline, env=env)\n            _git_output(root, \"add\", \"-A\", \"--\", \".\", env=env)\n            tree = _git_output(root, \"write-tree\", env=env).strip()\n            commit = _git_output(\n                root, \"commit-tree\", tree, \"-p\", baseline, \"-m\", f\"stage2: saved {label} of {change}\", env=env\n            ).strip()\n            _git_output(root, \"update-ref\", ref, commit)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            return f\"saving the attempt failed ({error})\"\n    return f\"the attempt is saved at {ref} ({commit[:12]}); `git diff {baseline[:12]} {ref}` shows it\"\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "save_attempt",
          "start_line": 5935,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },

          "excerpt": "def test_script_uses_its_own_checkout_from_another_worktree(tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    ns = _build(tmp_path, name=\"intended\")\n    other = _build(tmp_path, name=\"other\")\n    linked = tmp_path / \"linked\"\n    _git(ns.klon, \"worktree\", \"add\", \"--detach\", str(linked), \"HEAD\")\n    _copy_scripts(linked)\n    _write_stub(linked)\n    # Give the other checkout a different history, so using its cwd is visible.\n    _commit(other.origin, f\"other repository declaration\\n\\nCloses-Bead: {REAL_A}\")\n    result = subprocess.run(\n        [sys.executable, str(linked / \"scripts\" / \"close_merged_beads.py\"), \"--write\"],\n        cwd=other.klon,\n        env=_env(ns),\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        check=False,\n    )\n    assert result.returncode == 0, result.stderr\n    assert len(_closes(ns)) == len(DECLARED)\n    assert ns.main in result.stdout\n    assert not any(line.startswith(f\"close {REAL_A} \") for line in _closes(ns))\n    assert \"dolt push\" in _calls(ns)\n",

          "excerpt": "## Q-7 · When side refs are deleted\n\nasked: 2026-11-03\nanswer: \"nach dem Merge\" — after a change merges, the clean-up after merge (bead coding-harness-kpaq) deletes that change's refs under refs/stage2/attempts/<change>/, locally and on origin (asked 2026-11-03 under coding-harness-c99h, which this bead absorbed on 2026-11-12).\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: retention of side refs of stopped attempts.\n  Intention: the refs grow without bound (11 on origin, measured 2026-11-03).\n  Today: nothing deletes them.\n  Repository change: Options: delete after the merge; keep 14 days; keep forever.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of side refs that keep stopped attempts, facing unbounded growth or a retention rule, we decided that a change's attempt refs are deleted after its merge, locally and on origin, accepting that a stopped attempt of a merged change can no longer be inspected. — 2026-11-03\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_a_failed_flash_process_restores_the_baseline_so_stage2_off_can_proceed(world: World) -> None:\n    head = git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\")\n    plan_before = world.plan.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    world.script(\n        claude=[\n            {\n                \"stderr\": \"Z.ai outage\",\n                \"exit\": 1,\n                \"plant\": {\"src/half.py\": \"x = 1\\n\"},\n                \"append\": {\"plans/changes/demo/plan.md\": \"2026-10-07 10:00–10:05, 5 min\\n\", \"src/app.py\": \"# edit\\n\"},\n            },\n            {\n                \"stdout\": \"built\",\n                \"plant\": {\"src/app.py\": \"value = 3\\n\"},\n                \"append\": {\"plans/changes/demo/plan.md\": \"2026-10-07 11:00–11:05, 5 min\\n\"},\n            },\n        ],\n        make=[{\"stdout\": \"green\\n\"}],\n    )\n    assert world.run(\"implement\") == 1\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\") == head\n    assert not (world.root / \"src/half.py\").exists()\n    assert world.plan.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == plan_before\n    assert git(world.root, \"status\", \"--porcelain\", \"--\", \".\", \":(exclude)plans/changes/demo/findings.md\") == \"\"\n    assert \"Stage-2 call\" in world.text()  # the audit line stays in findings.md\n    assert world.run(\"implement\", \"demo\", \"--stage2-off\", \"Z.ai outage\") == 0\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-list\", \"--count\", f\"{head}..HEAD\") == \"1\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_a_failed_model_call_saves_the_attempt_before_restoring(\n    world: World, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]\n) -> None:\n    # Bead coding-harness-znc. Planted fault: the restore runs without the snapshot, and an\n    # attempt's edits - hours of them when a budget runs out - are gone with it.\n    head = git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\")\n    world.script(\n        claude=[\n            {\n                \"stderr\": \"budget spent\",\n                \"exit\": 1,\n                \"plant\": {\"src/half.py\": \"x = 1\\n\"},\n                \"append\": {\"src/app.py\": \"# edit\\n\"},\n            }\n        ]\n    )\n    assert world.run(\"implement\") == 1\n    err = capsys.readouterr().err\n    refs = git(world.root, \"for-each-ref\", \"--format=%(refname)\", \"refs/stage2/attempts/demo/\").splitlines()\n    assert len(refs) == 1 and refs[0].startswith(\"refs/stage2/attempts/demo/implement-attempt-1-\")\n    assert refs[0] in err and \"restored the worktree\" in err\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", f\"{refs[0]}^\") == head\n    assert git(world.root, \"show\", f\"{refs[0]}:src/half.py\") == \"x = 1\"\n    assert git(world.root, \"show\", f\"{refs[0]}:src/app.py\").endswith(\"# edit\")\n    # The snapshot carries the runner's identity, not the machine's: CI has no git user (PR #153).\n    assert git(world.root, \"log\", \"-1\", \"--format=%an <%ae>|%cn <%ce>\", refs[0]) == (\n        \"stage2 runner <stage2@localhost>|stage2 runner <stage2@localhost>\"\n    )\n    # The restore still leaves the tree clean and HEAD and the real index untouched.\n    assert not (world.root / \"src/half.py\").exists()\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\") == head\n    assert git(world.root, \"status\", \"--porcelain\", \"--\", \".\", \":(exclude)plans/changes/demo/findings.md\") == \"\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_preexisting_venv_root_link_keeps_modified_tools_refused(\n    world: World, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, runner: str, relative: str\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"An unchanged root link must not hide overwritten executable or package bytes.\"\"\"\n    target = world.root / \"linked-env\"\n    tool = target / relative\n    tool.parent.mkdir(parents=True)\n    tool.write_bytes(b\"baseline tool\\n\")\n    cache = target / \"lib/__pycache__/unchanged.pyc\"\n    cache.parent.mkdir(parents=True)\n    cache.write_bytes(b\"baseline cache\\n\")\n    venv = world.root / \".venv\"\n    if venv.is_symlink():\n        venv.unlink()\n    elif venv.exists():\n        # The fixture's installed tools stand in the way: this test links the root itself.\n        shutil.rmtree(venv)\n    venv.symlink_to(target, target_is_directory=True)\n    before = stage2.tool_state(world.root)\n    original = before.copy()\n    assert stage2.tool_problem(world.root, before) is None\n    tool.write_bytes(b\"overwritten tool\\n\")\n\n    problem = stage2.tool_problem(world.root, before)\n    assert problem is not None and f\"`.venv/{relative}`\" in problem\n    assert before[\".venv\"] == \"link:\" + str(target)\n    assert f\".venv/{relative}\" in before\n\n    def forbidden_launch(*_args, **_kwargs):\n        raise AssertionError(\"a runner-owned tool started before integrity refusal\")\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(stage2, \"launch\", forbidden_launch)\n    if runner == \"draft\":\n        ctx = stage2.Context(world.root, \"demo\", world.plan.parent, \"demo-1\")\n        problems, _owed, _scope = stage2.verify_draft(world.root, ctx, None, [], before)\n        assert not _owed\n    else:\n        problems = stage2.verify_attempt(world.root, world.plan, None, None, before)\n    assert len(problems) == 1 and f\"`.venv/{relative}`\" in problems[0]\n    assert before == original\n    assert cache.read_bytes() == b\"baseline cache\\n\"\n    assert tool.read_bytes() == b\"overwritten tool\\n\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_the_runner_prefers_the_checkouts_own_environment(tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"`.venv/bin/python3` of the checkout comes before the `python3` on PATH.\"\"\"\n    log = tmp_path / \"log\"\n    tree = _runner_tree(tmp_path, \"true\")\n    _interpreter_wrapper(tree / \".venv\" / \"bin\" / \"python3\", \"venv\", log)\n    _interpreter_wrapper(tmp_path / \"bin\" / \"python3\", \"path\", log)\n\n    done = _run_runner(tree, tmp_path / \"home\", [tmp_path / \"bin\"])\n    assert done.returncode == 0, f\"exit {done.returncode}\\n{done.stdout}\\n{done.stderr}\"\n    ran = set(log.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").split())\n    assert ran == {\"venv\"}, f\"the interpreters that ran: {sorted(ran)}\"\n\n    # And from another directory the same checkout's environment is the one used:\n    # the runner changes into the root before it chooses.\n    log.unlink()",

          "excerpt": "def test_runner_clock_is_the_only_time_source() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Spec criterion 1. Planted fault: a runner time/date read sits outside the clock boundary.\n\n    The guard reads the runner module as source, so it sees what an alias\n    hides; the boundary exemption is proven necessary, not vacuous, by\n    running the same guard once without it.\n    \"\"\"\n    source = (REPO_ROOT / \"scripts\" / \"stage2.py\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    assert re.search(r\"(?m)^def clock_now\\(\", source), \"the module defines no clock boundary\"\n    assert clock_guard_violations(source) == [], \"a raw clock read bypasses stage2.clock_now\"\n    boundary = [\n        node for node in ast.parse(source).body if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name == \"clock_now\"\n    ]\n    assert len(boundary) == 1, \"the module must define exactly one clock boundary\"\n    body_lines = range(boundary[0].lineno, (boundary[0].end_lineno or boundary[0].lineno) + 1)\n    without_boundary = clock_guard_violations(source, boundary=\"\")\n    assert without_boundary, \"the exemption is vacuous: the boundary body reads no clock\"\n    lines = [int(re.search(r\"at line (\\d+)$\", finding).group(1)) for finding in without_boundary]\n    assert all(line in body_lines for line in lines), without_boundary\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_targeted_mode_is_repair_only(world: World, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 10 (repair-targeted-check). Planted fault: a verb takes the targeted route without naming\n    it at its call site, or the draft's document check returns to the admitted shell runner.\"\"\"\n    for function in (stage2.run_attempts, stage2.verify_attempt):\n        name = \"verify_mode\" if function is stage2.run_attempts else \"mode\"\n        assert inspect.signature(function).parameters[name].default == \"full\"\n    # Exactly the two work verbs name the targeted mode at their call sites; every other caller keeps\n    # the admitted full check as its default (bead coding-harness-0swp).\n    source = (REPO_ROOT / \"scripts\" / \"stage2.py\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    assert \"REPAIR_VERIFY_MODE\" not in source\n    assert source.count('verify_mode=\"targeted\"') == 2\n    # A covered implement runs the targeted check, never the document-only draft subset:\n    commands = targeted_mode(monkeypatch)\n    world.script(\n        claude=[\n            {\n                \"stdout\": \"implemented\",\n                \"plant\": {\"src/app.py\": \"value = 2\\n\", \"tests/test_fix.py\": FIX_TEST},\n                \"append\": {\"plans/changes/demo/plan.md\": \"2026-10-07 10:00–10:05, 5 min\\n\"},\n            }\n        ],\n    )\n    assert world.run(\"implement\") == 0\n    assert commands.of(\"pytest\") and commands.of(\"gate\"), \"the targeted route did not run\"\n    assert commands.of(\"make\") == [], \"a covered implement ran the admitted full check\"\n    # The draft's document check stays out of the admitted shell runner:\n    ctx = stage2.Context(world.root, \"demo\", world.plan.parent, \"demo-1\")\n    world.plan.write_text(PLAN_CARD, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    _problems, _owed, scope = stage2.verify_draft(world.root, ctx, None, [], stage2.tool_state(world.root))\n    assert world.calls(\"bash\") == [], \"the draft's document check went through bash again\"\n    assert commands.of(\"make\") == []\n    assert \"document checks only\" in scope and \"result: green\" in scope\n",

          "excerpt": "def tool_state(root: Path) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The digest of the worktree's `.venv/` tree, taken before the model runs (R-21).\n\n    `.venv/` is ignored by git: a file there is invisible to `changed_paths` and survives\n    `restore_baseline`, so this digest is the only thing that shows an overwritten tool, a planted\n    `*.pth` file or a replaced package. Every file maps to the SHA-256 of its bytes and every symlink\n    to its target; the runner's steps run with the interpreter, ruff and packages of this tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    state: dict[str, str] = {}\n    venv = root / \".venv\"\n    try:\n        info = venv.lstat()\n        if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode):\n            # Record the root link AND digest its tools: an unchanged link must not hide\n            # overwritten target bytes. os.walk traverses its root even with followlinks=False;\n            # nested directory links remain opaque, and _unlink_cache still rejects this root.\n            state[\".venv\"] = \"link:\" + str(venv.readlink())\n    except FileNotFoundError:\n        return state\n    except OSError:\n        return {\".venv\": UNREADABLE}\n\n    def unreadable_directory(error: OSError) -> None:\n        # os.walk otherwise silently skips failed scandir calls, hiding newly planted caches.\n        path = Path(error.filename) if error.filename is not None else venv\n        state[path.relative_to(root).as_posix()] = UNREADABLE\n\n    for directory, names, files in os.walk(venv, onerror=unreadable_directory):\n        for name in sorted([*names, *files]):\n            path = Path(directory) / name\n            relative = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()\n            try:\n                if path.is_symlink():\n                    state[relative] = \"link:\" + str(path.readlink())\n                elif path.is_file():\n                    state[relative] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()\n            except OSError:\n                state[relative] = UNREADABLE\n    return state\n",

          "excerpt": "def tool_problem(root: Path, before: dict[str, str] | None) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The first path of `.venv/` that is not what the runner saw before the call, named; `None` when none is.\n\n    A new or content-changed regular file below an exact `__pycache__` component inside `.venv/` is\n    deleted before any runner-owned step: pytest's assertion rewriting writes bytecode there during\n    an attempt, and a deleted cache is rebuilt, so that write is normalized instead of refused (bead\n    coding-harness-q94b).           "excerpt": "def worktree_digests(root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The 8-character record digests of every worktree `git worktree list` names for this root.\n\n    The listing is this repository's, including worktrees whose directories are missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        listing = _git_output(root, \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\")\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"worktree discovery failed: {error}\") from error\n    digests: list[str] = []\n    for line in listing.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(\"worktree \"):\n            continue\n        path = Path(line[len(\"worktree \") :]).resolve()\n        digest = record_key(\"\", path).rsplit(\"@\", 1)[1]\n        if digest not in digests:\n            digests.append(digest)\n    return digests\n",

          "end_line": 1535,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, ",

          "end_line": 5963,
          "excerpt": "def save_attempt(root: Path, baseline: str, change: str, label: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Save the worktree as it stands after a failed call on a local ref; say where, or why not.\n\n    A failed call is not a worthless one: a run that hits a spent budget after hours of edits still\n    holds them (bead coding-harness-znc). The snapshot goes through a temporary index, so the real\n    index and the files stay untouched; tracked and untracked files go in, gitignored ones do not.\n    The temporary index is seeded with the baseline, as in `worktree_tree`, so a file tracked although\n    ignored stays in the snapshot. The commit's parent is the baseline, so `git diff <baseline> <ref>`\n    shows everything the run left in the tree: this attempt, any earlier attempt of the run whose tree\n    it started on, and the runner's own writes. The ref lives under `refs/stage2/attempts/`, which no\n    branch push carries. A save that fails is named and never blocks the restore that follows.\n    The commit carries the runner's own identity, so a machine without a configured git user (a CI\n    runner) saves as well, and the ref says who wrote it.\n    \"\"\"\n    stamp = utc_now().strftime(\"%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ\")\n    ref = f\"refs/stage2/attempts/{change}/{label}-{stamp}\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-save-\") as scratch:\n        env = {**os.environ, \"GIT_INDEX_FILE\": str(Path(scratch) / \"index\"), **SAVE_IDENTITY}\n        try:\n            _git_output(root, \"read-tree\", baseline, env=env)\n            _git_output(root, \"add\", \"-A\", \"--\", \".\", env=env)\n            tree = _git_output(root, \"write-tree\", env=env).strip()\n            commit = _git_output(\n                root, \"commit-tree\", tree, \"-p\", baseline, \"-m\", f\"stage2: saved {label} of {change}\", env=env\n            ).strip()\n            _git_output(root, \"update-ref\", ref, commit)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            return f\"saving the attempt failed ({error})\"\n    return f\"the attempt is saved at {ref} ({commit[:12]}); `git diff {baseline[:12]} {ref}` shows it\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def save_answer_evidence(root: Path, change: str, token: str, attempt: int, answer: str, key: str | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Save one attempt's full answer as protected evidence below the worktree's own git directory.\n\n    Written at the model-return boundary, before any HEAD check, verification or answer check can\n    stop the run, so a rejected answer stays diagnosable from what the model actually returned (bead\n    coding-harness-hgvp). The directory is git's resolved per-worktree `stage2/attempts/<change>/` - in\n    a linked worktree below the main checkout's `.git/worktrees/<name>/`, which the diagnostics name\n    as an absolute path - local evidence like `refs/stage2/attempts/`, tracked by no path and carried by no branch push.\n    The answer passes `protect_diagnostics` once on every route, the keyless ones included; an empty\n    or unavailable answer is recorded as such, never fabricated or retried. The file is created\n    exclusively, so an earlier attempt's evidence is never overwritten; an aliased destination, a\n    protection failure or a failed write raises, so no checkpoint stands on lost or unprotected\n    evidence. Returns the saved file, as the diagnostics name it.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        git_dir = Path(_git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"--absolute-git-dir\").strip())\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise CallFailed(f\"the answer evidence directory could not be resolved ({error})\") from error\n    if not git_dir.is_absolute():\n        git_dir = root / git_dir\n    body = protect_diagnostics(answer, key) if answer.strip() else \"(no answer was returned)\\n\"\n    directory = git_dir / \"stage2\" / \"attempts\" / change\n    expected = Path(os.path.realpath(git_dir)) / \"stage2\" / \"attempts\" / change\n    if directory.is_symlink() or os.path.realpath(directory) != str(expected):\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the answer evidence directory {directory} is not this worktree's own stage2/attempts/{change}; \"",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::tool_problem",
          "end_line": 5715,
          "excerpt": "def tool_problem(root: Path, before: dict[str, str] | None) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The first path of `.venv/` that is not what the runner saw before the call, named; `None` when none is.\n\n    A new or content-changed regular file below an exact `__pycache__` component inside `.venv/` is\n    deleted before any runner-owned step: pytest's assertion rewriting writes bytecode there during\n    an attempt, and a deleted cache is rebuilt, so that write is normalized instead of refused (bead\n    coding-harness-q94b). Every other difference keeps the refusal with the first path named. The\n    baseline bookkeeping stays narrow: each successful unlink immediately removes that path's old\n    entry from the shared `before` dictionary, even if a later check fails. This records only the\n    runner's own deletions. Nothing that survives is rebaselined; recreated caches are deleted again.\n    \"\"\"\n    if before is None:\n        return None\n\n    def differences(now: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:\n        return sorted(path for path in before.keys() | now.keys() if before.get(path) != now.get(path))\n\n    now = tool_state(root)\n    cleaned = False\n    for path in sorted(before.keys() | now.keys()):\n        if UNREADABLE in (before.get(path), now.get(path)):\n            return f\"`{path}` cannot be inspected, and a tool the attempt wrote is not run\"\n        if not _is_cache_path(path):\n            continue  # retain the difference, but still clean eligible caches that sort later\n        if before.get(path) == now.get(path):\n            continue\n        if before.get(path, \"\").startswith(\"link:\"):\n            continue  # removing a baseline symlink is never a cache-byte change\n        deleted = _unlink_cache(root, path)\n        if deleted is None:\n            continue  # a linked or non-regular cache-looking path stays a difference\n        if not deleted:\n            return f\"`{path}` cannot be deleted, and a tool the attempt wrote is not run\"\n        before.pop(path, None)  # record each runner-owned deletion even if a later check fails\n        cleaned = True\n    if cleaned:\n        now = tool_state(root)  # the tree changed through the runner's own deletions\n    if now == before:\n        return None\n    changed = differences(now)\n    return f\"`{changed[0]}` is not what the runner saw before the call, and a tool the attempt wrote is not run\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_a_changed_venv_file_is_named_and_refused(world: World) -> None:\n    \"\"\"O188-2: the digest covers the whole `.venv/` tree, not only ruff.\"\"\"\n    package = world.root / \".venv\" / \"lib\" / \"python3.x\" / \"site-packages\" / \"yaml\"\n    package.mkdir(parents=True)\n    (package / \"__init__.py\").write_text(\"ok = 1\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    link = world.root / \".venv\" / \"lib\" / \"link\"\n    link.symlink_to(\"python3.x\")\n    before = stage2.tool_state(world.root)\n    assert stage2.tool_problem(world.root, before) is None\n    (package / \"__init__.py\").write_text(\"import os\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    assert \".venv/lib/python3.x/site-packages/yaml/__init__.py\" in stage2.tool_problem(world.root, before)\n    (package / \"__init__.py\").write_text(\"ok = 1\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    (package.parent / \"evil.pth\").write_text(\"import os\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    assert \"evil.pth\" in stage2.tool_problem(world.root, before), \"an added file went unnoticed\"\n    (package.parent / \"evil.pth\").unlink()\n    link.unlink()\n    link.symlink_to(\"elsewhere\")\n    assert \".venv/lib/link\" in stage2.tool_problem(world.root, before), \"a changed symlink target went unnoticed\"\n    link.unlink()\n    assert \".venv/lib/link\" in stage2.tool_problem(world.root, before), \"a removed symlink went unnoticed\"\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::restore_baseline",
          "end_line": 6117,
          "excerpt": "def restore_baseline(\n    root: Path,\n    baseline: str,\n    keep: set[Path],\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None = None,\n    planned: tuple[list[str], list[Path]] | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"After a failed model call, put every path but `keep` back at the baseline; say what was undone.\n\n    The runner refused pre-existing changes outside `keep` before the first call, so what differs\n    from the baseline outside it is the run's own - including a half-finished edit of a dead process.\n    Gitignored paths the attempt created are removed too: `changed_paths` cannot see them and\n    `git clean` without `-x` keeps them, so the run's earlier snapshot of the ignored files tells them\n    apart from the ones that stood before (phase 6, F-5). This implementation/repair rollback's\n    tracked destinations and newly created ignored cleanup paths are checked for an unsafe parent\n    before its first `git restore`, `git clean`, `unlink`, `rmtree` or parent removal; a refusal\n    leaves this recovery batch unwritten and ends the run.\n    \"\"\"\n    if planned is None:\n        planned = plan_baseline_restore(root, keep, ignored_before, baseline)\n    touched, created = planned\n    if not touched and not created:\n        return \"the worktree needed no restore.\"\n    spec = [f\":(exclude){path.as_posix()}\" for path in sorted(keep, key=lambda path: path.as_posix())]\n    try:\n        _git_output(root, \"restore\", f\"--source={baseline}\", \"--staged\", \"--worktree\", \"--\", \".\", *spec)\n        _git_output(root, \"clean\", \"-fdq\", \"--\", \".\", *spec)\n    except Refused as error:\n        listing = \", \".join([*touched, *(path.as_posix() for path in created)])\n        return f\"restoring the worktree to {baseline[:12]} failed ({error}); discard {listing} by hand.\"\n    removed = []\n    for relative in created:\n        path = root / relative\n        try:\n            if path.is_dir() and not path.is_symlink():\n                shutil.rmtree(path)\n            else:\n                path.unlink()\n        except OSError:\n            continue\n        removed.append(relative.as_posix())\n        parent = path.parent\n        while parent not in (root, parent.parent):\n            try:\n                parent.rmdir()\n            except OSError:\n                break\n            parent = parent.parent\n    undone = f\"undone: {', '.join(touched)}\" if touched else \"\"\n    ignored = f\"ignored paths removed: {', '.join(removed)}\" if removed else \"\"\n    inner = \"; \".join(part for part in (undone, ignored) if part)\n    return f\"the runner restored the worktree to {baseline[:12]} ({inner}); rerun the verb or add --stage2-off.\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_restore_baseline_refuses_external_parents_before_mutation(\n    world: World, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, tmp_path: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str], level: str\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 1. Planted fault: Git rollback or ignored cleanup mutates before checking every target.\"\"\"\n    outside = tmp_path / \"outside-baseline\"\n    outside.mkdir()\n    (outside / \"keep.txt\").write_text(\"sentinel\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    deep = world.root / \"src\" / \"deep\"\n    deep.mkdir()\n    (deep / \"keep.txt\").write_text(\"kept\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    git(world.root, \"add\", \"-A\")\n    git(world.root, \"commit\", \"--quiet\", \"-m\", \"a tracked file below a parent that later escapes\")\n\n    def escape() -> None:\n        shutil.rmtree(deep)\n        deep.symlink_to(outside, target_is_directory=True)\n\n    if level == \"unit\":\n        escape()\n        commands: list[tuple[str, ...]] = []\n        real_git_output = stage2._git_output\n\n        def git_output(root, *args, **kwargs):\n            commands.append(args)\n            return real_git_output(root, *args, **kwargs)\n\n        monkeypatch.setattr(stage2, \"_git_output\", git_output)\n        with pytest.raises(stage2.RestorationRefused) as expected:\n            stage2.restore_baseline(world.root, git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\"), set())\n        message = str(expected.value)\n        assert \"src/deep/keep.txt\"",

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::House rules",
          "end_line": 89,
          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone.     "263092260c1ac0fda724743b2669b31affb56d4e": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-23T09:55:46Z",
      "body": "The third D-52 condition — every reader on one access point — was shown in\ne02c915. This commit takes the copy away:\n\n- .beads/issues.jsonl is no longer tracked, and is git-ignored so a\n  `git add -A` cannot bring it back. The export-identity gate and its four\n  tests are retired: there is no committed file left to compare.\n- The hosted CI hydrates the tracker, renders once and presets BEAD_RENDER;\n  every gate of the run reads that one render. Locally the access point\n  (scripts/bead_render.py) renders fresh through tools/bd, and without bd it\n  fails with both ways out — bootstrap or BEAD_RENDER — instead of reading a\n  stale copy.\n- The drift job hydrates too: plans-registry-strict reads the tracker, and\n  without the copy it would have crashed nightly. plans-registry and\n  plans-registry-strict declare needs_tracker; the schema now allows it in\n  both jobs.\n- The kit role geruest is dissolved: without the copy its remaining members\n  map to one export verdict, which the AK-6 test forbids. The stub files stay\n  with the export manifest. Two REIST_NICHT entries for tests that do not\n  travel were removed; the probe cap stays at 31.\n- verify_all.sh --ci measures the same gate set as the derived workflow\n  (finding 2 of the PR #32 review).\n- AGENTS.md house rules 2 and 4, README, plans/_README.md: the render is the\n  contract; a pull request body names every bead it opens, changes or closes\n  (maintainer, 2026-09-23, D-52 successor; the CI job summary follows as\n  bead coding-harness-1jg.4).\n- The empty gate-placement change package is archived (its bead 1jg.2 closed\n  with PR #32).\n\nStarted by a Cline session that stopped mid-way (uncommitted, last edit\n10:28); finished and corrected by Claude Code.\n\nVerified 2026-09-23: make verify VERIFY GREEN (325 passed, 15 skipped);\nverify_all.sh --job drift VERIFY GREEN, measuring the tracker locally.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

      "author_utc": "2026-11-14T18:59:01Z",
      "body": "The tree baseline is measured only for a run with protected work - the one\ncase that reuses cheap results across the admission. A seconds-only job\n(docs, drift) and a cheap pass that ended blocking red rely on no baseline,\nso they no longer refuse over an unmeasurable or moving tree (L2-3, L2-8).\nEvery ending - green, red, refused, refused admission - goes through one\nfinish(): the refused run names the gates it did not run, prints a banner\nand closes its history record red (L2-2). The cheap phase's not-run header\nnames every blocking red gate instead of claiming a stop at the first\n(L2-7). A refusal names the paths that moved. The worker rule lives once in\nverify_run.worker_bound, used by the full and the targeted check (L2-6).\nThe gates' default interpreter comes from the env argument (L2-9).\n\nL2-1 is rejected: ruff and pytest self-ignore their caches; the new proof\ntest_real_tool_caches_keep_the_baseline_stable runs both inside a checkout\nwithout user-level excludes and stays stable.\n\nOrchestrator hand edit (Opus subagent, maintainer's word of 2026-11-14).\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

      "body": "The maintainer accepts ADR 0006 on 2026-09-27. The Omnigent M0 pilot is\ndropped; the adoption path starts at M1; parallel sessions run from then\non, every writing session beyond the first in a worktree of its own, at\nmost writing_sessions_per_repository of them (lakeswitch-ai D-59, D-60).\nThe first writing session writes the tracker; a worker session claims its\nown bead and adds its handover comment, nothing more, as D-60 has it. The\nworker claim waits until the maintainer rewrites AGENTS.md house rule 4.\nThe D-60 write guard takes the place of ADR 0005's Omnigent session\npolicy; it does not exist yet, so until it does, the bounds are stated,\nnot enforced.\n\nADR 0001 is superseded; ADR 0002 and ADR 0005 are superseded in part.\nEach records it in its header. The target document carries a notice at\nits top, in the D-3 and D-7 rows and in its tracker section; its other M0\npassages stay as the record of the earlier design.\n\nOwed item Coding Harness 3 of the lakeswitch-ai decision record.\n\nPrepared by a Claude Code session (the ADR, these notes, this message);\nthe maintainer asked for the acceptance to be prepared as a draft, and an\nagent review in a fresh context read it before signing. The explain-back\nand this commit are the maintainer's, signed with the Touch-ID key.\n\nExplain-back:\nhe owed decision record lands as one signed bundle per repository — coding-harness and lakeswitch-ai — putting the ratified decisions into the files they name.\nhe decisions are ratified and in force; only their promotion is owed, and bundling keeps it reviewable as single signed acts under gate M-30.\nThe bundle edits the very files the guard and gates read, so a wrong entry hits the enforcement layer itself — hence one Bead per item,\n\nPrepared-by: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

    "82a013b92bfab78830cdeeb982d597e217216c64": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-20T11:20:58Z",
      "body": "Main brings the shared two-phase scheduler (scripts/verify_run.py, PR #416,\nbead coding-harness-bxxt.6), venv_guard (PR #415) and the journal citation\ngate (PR #418). The slip counter (bead coding-harness-bxxt.7) is carried into\nmain's structure; nothing of either side is reverted.\n\nConflict resolutions:\n\n- scripts/verify_duration.py: main's in-process writers stay (record_start,\n  record_gate, record_end with root, state_root and env). The slip counter's\n  comparison evidence is attached to them: record_start records\n  common_git_dir for its root, reads the runner-owned comparison variables\n  from the scheduler's env (_comparison_fields(env), falling back to the\n  process environment for the CLI), and creates the targeted history beside\n  the duration history under the same state root at the first version-2\n  marker. append_event/_open_history take both the slip counter's\n  `destination` (the targeted history) and main's keyword `state_root`;\n  targeted_history_path accepts a state root too. Imports keep both\n  Sequence and dataclass/field; _git and _gate_file_digest take main's form.\n  New COMPARISON_ENV_NAMES lists the three variables.\n- scripts/stage2.py: main's scheduler path stays the one full check. The\n  slip counter's single entry point full_verify(root, env, key, change,\n  prepare) is kept, now built on main's body: prepare runs first, outside\n  any admission (main's intent for the full-mode attempt), then\n  intent-to-add, then _scheduled_verify with\n  verify_duration.full_run_context(_checked_tree(root, change), change)\n  added to the scheduler's environment. verify_attempt's full mode hands its\n  preparation (format, cheap checks, ledger clearing, prepare_derived) to\n  full_verify as `prepare` instead of duplicating the intent-to-add,\n  scheduler and cleanup block (house rule 9: one path).\n- scripts/verify_run.py (no conflict, one addition): after recording the\n  start, run_verification drops the comparison variables from the gates'\n  environment, so a gate never inherits them and a check a gate starts is\n  never recorded as a second full run of the same change and tree.\n- tests/test_stage2.py: both sides' new tests kept. The slip end-to-end test\n  now uses the world's committed gate list instead of creating its own\n  decisions/ folder, and its `make` stub is the scheduler's protected gate:\n  it records nothing (the scheduler records start, gate and end) and fails if\n  it inherits the comparison context.\n- tests/test_verify_duration.py: the slip counter's version of the\n  derived-never-persisted test (the reader `slips` is exposed) replaces\n  main's deferral assertions; main's criterion-8 completion-context test is\n  kept.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9DrQg7dkn7zUzrqUEk\n",

      "body": "A rule whose name starts with `secret:` is not applied to a file under the\nrepository's top-level tests/ folder: the working file, and the hunks of a\ncommit patch or of the staged diff that name such a file. Every other rule\nscans tests/ as before, and a secret rule scans everything outside it\n(tests_extra/, docs/tests/, a change's own folder, a link under tests/, a\ncommit message, a prompt text). A diff header that cannot be read with\ncertainty (a quoted name) is scanned in full.\n\nMaintainer's decision of 2026-10-07 on open item O-4 of the stage-2 change;\nthe accepted consequence is that a real key committed in a test file is not\nfound. The secret patterns live in the maintainer's denylist, not in this\nscript, so the marker is a name prefix and each machine sets it itself.\n\nThe log now runs with --no-renames (the staged scan already did) so a diff\nheader names one path, and splits message from patch by a marker line the log\nformat writes. Docstring and WORKFLOW state the exemption.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,

    "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T14:07:20Z",
      "body": "A feature can decide something that belongs in an architecture decision\nrecord, and nothing here asked. Each change anchor now states its class;\na feature states its name and a proposal, and owes an answer file\ndecisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml in the LakeSwitch pilot's format, so\nLakeSwitch can read it unchanged.\n\nscripts/check_adr_answers.py is the gate and the one reader of the\nformat: strict YAML (a duplicate key is refused, a bare no is a boolean),\nevery rule of the answer file, active and archived anchors, one report\nline per cause, exit 0/1/3. It holds existence and format only; it cannot\nsee who wrote or merged an answer, and no line claims it.\n\nscripts/harness.py decide adr asks each open question in a terminal, or\nrecords one answer the maintainer stated elsewhere (--change, --answer,\n--reason, --stated-in). It writes the answer files and a commit message\nwhere git says, and never stages, commits, pushes or merges. Who answered\ncomes from provenance.yaml, which now maps decisions/answers/ to\nhuman-decided with owner_role framework-architect.\n\nThe gate is in decisions/gates.yaml (block, not floor), ci.yml is\nregenerated, both scripts and their tests travel with the kit and the\nanswers do not. The kit probe's exemption for\ntest_the_two_manifests_really_disagree_somewhere is struck and its cap\nlowered to 31: with four more mechanism files the throwaway repository\npasses that test now.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0",
      "subject": "feat(adr): the gate adr-answers and the command decide adr",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "decisions/gates.yaml",
        "provenance.yaml",
        "scripts/ci_gates.py"
      ]
    },

      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T16:16:52Z",
      "body": "scripts/leakcheck.py scans the change folder, every tracked or untracked and\nnot ignored file, the message and patch of every commit on a local or\nremote-tracking branch, and any prompt text, against the denylist kept outside\nthe repository. It reports place, rule name and match length, never the match.\nIt refuses (exit 2, with the reason) when it cannot measure. make leakcheck\nruns it; ci_gates.py and the kit manifest classify it.\n\nReal run, 2026-09-30, before this commit: make leakcheck NAME=stage-2-codex-glm\n-> clean, 186 files, 251 commits, 12 rules.\n\nSlice-1 faults planted, each red, then restored: resolver without the dot form;\nrouting pattern back to one digit and one word; skip untracked files; drop\n--remotes; print the match; exit 0 on a missing denylist.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",

      "body": "Hand repair of phase-6 finding F6-1 (BLOCKER, [DIVERGENT]) after the\nphase-6 verdict of 2026-11-12: the runner already uses the targeted check\nfor implement and a document-only check outside the verify admission for\ndraft, while the held texts still described the old routes.\n\n- docs/WORKFLOW.md: the Flash and cheap-check paragraphs name the post-run\n  check (targeted, full `make verify` on fallback) instead of a full run;\n  the draft section names the locally runnable document gates outside the\n  admission instead of `verify_all.sh --job docs`, and says implement and\n  repair take the targeted check; the targeted-check rule adds implement,\n  the missing-test refusal, the slip definition and the `slips` reader;\n  \"Night runs\" asks the morning handover for the slip count with its\n  repository and interval.\n- prompts/04-implement.md: the gate line and the runner paragraph say an\n  implement attempt takes the targeted check (full fallback), a targeted\n  red fails the attempt, and new production code without a reachable test\n  is refused.\n- docs/adr/0025-targeted-check-after-repair.md: a dated amendment section\n  (2026-11-12) extends decisions 1 to 4 to implement and draft and makes\n  the slip measurement automatic; the original decision text is unchanged.\n  The amendment takes effect only when the maintainer merges the decision\n  pull request that carries it (docs/adr/ is human-decided in\n  provenance.yaml).\n- tools/claude-code/skills/handover/SKILL.md: a night run's morning\n  handover reports the slip count, repository and interval, and an\n  unavailable measurement as such.\n- README.md, docs/orchestration.md: one sentence each no longer says\n  implement always runs the full `make verify`.\n\nTwo tests still pin the old wording and are left for the orchestrator:\ntests/test_stage2.py::test_the_workflow_names_the_draft_document_check and\ntests/test_stage2.py::test_the_doctrine_and_prompts_say_the_flash_verbs_are_live.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9EH4VmSEo7DBu8jUbB\n",
      "body_truncated": false,

          "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb.           "excerpt": "def run_work_model(\n    ctx: Context,\n    prompt: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    writable: bool,\n    key: str | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One non-interactive Claude Code work call with file tools only.\"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        prompt_file = Path(tmp) / \"work-prompt.md\"\n        prompt_file.write_text(prompt, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        command = [\n            \"claude\",\n            \"-p\",\n            f\"Run the phase for {ctx.change} exactly as the appended instructions say.\",\n            \"--append-system-prompt-file\",\n            str(prompt_file),\n            \"--model\",\n            endpoint[1],\n        ]\n        if endpoint[2]:\n            command += [\"--effort\", endpoint[2]]\n        command += [\n            \"--tools\",\n            WORK_WRITE_TOOLS if writable else WORK_READ_TOOLS,\n            \"--restricted\",\n            \"--safe-mode\",\n            \"--strict-mcp-config\",\n            \"--permission-mode\",\n            \"acceptEdits\" if writable else \"dontAsk\",\n            \"--permission-prompts\",\n            \"none\",\n            \"--no-session-persistence\",\n            \"--output-format\",\n            \"text\",\n        ]\n        if key is None:\n            env = foreign_env({})\n        else:\n            config_dir = Path(tmp) / \"claude-config\"\n            config_dir.mkdir()\n            env = glm_env(key, config_dir, endpoint[1])\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, env, key, timeout=timeout, limit=limit)\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        error = fail(\"claude\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\", key)\n        # A failed call's printed answer travels along for the repair evidence; nothing else changes.\n        error.partial_answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n        raise error\n    answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n    if not answer.strip():\n        raise fail(\"claude\", done, \"the answer is empty\", key)\n    return answer\n",

Returns (answer, thread id).\n\n    A review reads in the CLI's `read-only` sandbox; a draft writes in\n    `workspace-write`, and the runner puts back what lands outside the change\n    folder.
