          "excerpt": "def _private_repository(root: Path, destination: Path, checkout: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create a proof's private repository at `destination`, its checkout materialized at `checkout`.\n\n    The clone carries the source's objects wholesale - unreferenced ones included - with no\n    hardlinks and no object alternates, so the proof runs against bytes of its own and a local\n    object copy carries the fixed tree `worktree_tree` wrote without a ref. Every source ref is\n    preserved under its own name first, so a ref the source already had stays a move in the\n    proof's store, not an accidental creation; the remote configuration goes, so an ordinary\n    Git operation in the proof has no path back to the source. HEAD is detached at `checkout`\n    when it names the baseline commit, or at the source's HEAD for a fixed-code tree id.\n    `checkout` is read into the index and the working tree, leaving a baseline clean against\n    its own commit. The source's refs, index and worktree are read here, never\n    written (spec, criteria 1 and 6).\n    \"\"\"\n    # Snapshot before copying objects: later source refs may name objects the clone never saw.\n    refs = _ref_targets(root)\n    head = refs.pop(\"HEAD\").split(\" \", 1)[0]\n    _git_output(root, \"clone\", \"--quiet\", \"--no-hardlinks\", str(root), str(destination))\n    # An alternates file makes the clone depend on another object store. Refuse rather than\n    # silently discarding that dependency and assuming all required objects were copied.\n    alternates = destination / \".git\" / \"objects\" / \"info\" / \"alternates\"\n    if alternates.exists() or alternates.is_symlink():\n        raise Refused(\"the private repository contains objects/info/alternates\")\n    _git_output(destination, \"remote\", \"remove\", \"origin\")\n    if _git_output(destination, \"cat-file\", \"-t\", checkout).strip() == \"commit\":\n        head = checkout\n    # Detach HEAD in its own transaction before updating its former referent. Git\n    # otherwise refuses both names in one transaction, even with --no-deref.\n    _git_output(\n        destination,\n        \"update-ref\",\n        \"--no-deref\",\n        \"--stdin\",\n        stdin=(\n            f\"start\\nupdate HEAD {head}\\nprepare\\ncommit\\nstart\\n\"\n            + \"\".join(f\"update {name} {target}\\n\" for name, target in refs.items() if \" \" not in target)\n            + \"prepare\\ncommit\\n\"\n        ),\n    )\n    # Measurements retain both the resolved object and symbolic target. Restore\n    # symbolic refs by kind, using symbolic-ref for Git versions without symref-update.\n    for name, target in refs.items():\n        _, _, symbolic = target.partition(\" \")\n        if symbolic:\n            _git_output(destination, \"symbolic-ref\", name, symbolic)\n    _git_output(destination, \"read-tree\", \"--reset\", \"-u\", checkout)\n",

          "excerpt": "def tool_state(root: Path) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The digest of the worktree's `.venv/` tree, taken before the model runs (R-21).\n\n    `.venv/` is ignored by git: a file there is invisible to `changed_paths` and survives\n    `restore_baseline`, so this digest is the only thing that shows an overwritten tool, a planted\n    `*.pth` file or a replaced package. Every file maps to the SHA-256 of its bytes and every symlink\n    to its target; the runner's steps run with the interpreter, ruff and packages of this tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    state: dict[str, str] = {}\n    venv = root / \".venv\"\n    try:\n        info = venv.lstat()\n        if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode):\n            # Record the root link AND digest its tools: an unchanged link must not hide\n            # overwritten target bytes. os.walk traverses its root even with followlinks=False;\n            # nested directory links remain opaque, and _unlink_cache still rejects this root.\n            state[\".venv\"] = \"link:\" + str(venv.readlink())\n    except FileNotFoundError:\n        return state\n    except OSError:\n        return {\".venv\": UNREADABLE}\n\n    def unreadable_directory(error: OSError) -> None:\n        # os.walk otherwise silently skips failed scandir calls, hiding newly planted caches.\n        path = Path(error.filename) if error.filename is not None else venv\n        state[path.relative_to(root).as_posix()] = UNREADABLE\n\n    for directory, names, files in os.walk(venv, onerror=unreadable_directory):\n        for name in sorted([*names, *files]):\n            path = Path(directory) / name\n            relative = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()\n            try:\n                if path.is_symlink():\n                    state[relative] = \"link:\" + str(path.readlink())\n                elif path.is_file():\n                    state[relative] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()\n            except OSError:\n                state[relative] = UNREADABLE\n    return state\n",

          "excerpt": "def restore_baseline(\n    root: Path,\n    baseline: str,\n    keep: set[Path],\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None = None,\n    planned: tuple[list[str], list[Path]] | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"After a failed model call, put every path but `keep` back at the baseline; say what was undone.\n\n    The runner refused pre-existing changes outside `keep` before the first call, so what differs\n    from the baseline outside it is the run's own - including a half-finished edit of a dead process.\n    Gitignored paths the attempt created are removed too: `changed_paths` cannot see them and\n    `git clean` without `-x` keeps them, so the run's earlier snapshot of the ignored files tells them\n    apart from the ones that stood before (phase 6, F-5). This implementation/repair rollback's\n    tracked destinations and newly created ignored cleanup paths are checked for an unsafe parent\n    before its first `git restore`, `git clean`, `unlink`, `rmtree` or parent removal; a refusal\n    leaves this recovery batch unwritten and ends the run.\n    \"\"\"\n    if planned is None:\n        planned = plan_baseline_restore(root, keep, ignored_before, baseline)\n    touched, created = planned\n    if not touched and not created:\n        return \"the worktree needed no restore.\"\n    spec = [f\":(exclude){path.as_posix()}\" for path in sorted(keep, key=lambda path: path.as_posix())]\n    try:\n        _git_output(root, \"restore\", f\"--source={baseline}\", \"--staged\", \"--worktree\", \"--\", \".\", *spec)\n        _git_output(root, \"clean\", \"-fdq\", \"--\", \".\", *spec)\n    except Refused as error:\n        listing = \", \".join([*touched, *(path.as_posix() for path in created)])\n        return f\"restoring the worktree to {baseline[:12]} failed ({error}); discard {listing} by hand.\"\n    removed = []\n    for relative in created:\n        path = root / relative\n        try:\n            if path.is_dir() and not path.is_symlink():\n                shutil.rmtree(path)\n            else:\n                path.unlink()\n        except OSError:\n            continue\n        removed.append(relative.as_posix())\n        parent = path.parent\n        while parent not in (root, parent.parent):\n            try:\n                parent.rmdir()\n            except OSError:\n                break\n            parent = parent.parent\n    undone = f\"undone: {', '.join(touched)}\" if touched else \"\"\n    ignored = f\"ignored paths removed: {', '.join(removed)}\" if removed else \"\"\n    inner = \"; \".join(part for part in (undone, ignored) if part)\n    return f\"the runner restored the worktree to {baseline[:12]} ({inner}); rerun the verb or add --stage2-off.\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb. A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2). Before the failure is decided, findings.md is restored outright: every post-run check, cheap\n    or full, reads the runner's file, an edit alone fails nothing, and a completed attempt that edited\n    it carries a quoted restore notice under its audit line (spec, criteria 8 and 9).\n\n    A verb that passes `retain_answer` keeps every attempt's full answer: right at the model-return\n    boundary, before any HEAD check, verification or answer check can stop the run, the protected\n    answer is saved as local evidence and its location joins the attempt's diagnostics - the parser's\n    rejections, the call and verify failures included - and is printed on success (bead\n    coding-harness-hgvp). A failed call keeps the output it returned.\n\n    A verb that passes `protect_lifecycle` snapshots the change's lifecycle fields (`status`,\n    `implementation_status`) in spec, optional design and plan right before every call. Once the\n    attempt's changed-file measurement stands, changed effective values restore the trusted whole\n    frontmatter block, preserving body edits and YAML anchors - before verification, the\n    derived preparation or the checkpoint reads the documents. The same per-attempt snapshot serves\n    the early exits: a failed call and a retry recover whole snapshotted inputs, a moved HEAD keeps\n    its commit while the safe working-tree fields go back, a refused checkpoint puts the fields back\n    before the run stops, and every attempt's bookkeeping names what was restored or says the fields\n    stayed unchanged (status-fields-restore).           "excerpt": "def worktree_digests(root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The 8-character record digests of every worktree `git worktree list` names for this root.\n\n    The listing is this repository's, including worktrees whose directories are missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        listing = _git_output(root, \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\")\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"worktree discovery failed: {error}\") from error\n    digests: list[str] = []\n    for line in listing.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(\"worktree \"):\n            continue\n        path = Path(line[len(\"worktree \") :]).resolve()\n        digest = record_key(\"\", path).rsplit(\"@\", 1)[1]\n        if digest not in digests:\n            digests.append(digest)\n    return digests\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "worktree_digests",
          "start_line": 3482,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::record_key",
          "end_line": 4059,
          "excerpt": "def record_key(change: str, root: Path) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The record's name: the change and a digest of the resolved repository root.\n\n    Two worktrees may hold the same change folder, and one `release-loop` must not delete the\n    other's record or hand it another's state (R-2 of the review-swarm review).\n    \"\"\"\n    return f\"{change}@{hashlib.sha256(str(root.resolve()).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:8]}\"\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "record_key",
          "start_line": 4053,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::run_work_model",
          "end_line": 6255,
          "excerpt": "def run_work_model(\n    ctx: Context,\n    prompt: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    writable: bool,\n    key: str | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = None,\n    limit: str | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"One non-interactive Claude Code work call with file tools only.\"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        prompt_file = Path(tmp) / \"work-prompt.md\"\n        prompt_file.write_text(prompt, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        command = [\n            \"claude\",\n            \"-p\",\n            f\"Run the phase for {ctx.change} exactly as the appended instructions say.\",\n            \"--append-system-prompt-file\",\n            str(prompt_file),\n            \"--model\",\n            endpoint[1],\n        ]\n        if endpoint[2]:\n            command += [\"--effort\", endpoint[2]]\n        command += [\n            \"--tools\",\n            WORK_WRITE_TOOLS if writable else WORK_READ_TOOLS,\n            \"--restricted\",\n            \"--safe-mode\",\n            \"--strict-mcp-config\",\n            \"--permission-mode\",\n            \"acceptEdits\" if writable else \"dontAsk\",\n            \"--permission-prompts\",\n            \"none\",\n            \"--no-session-persistence\",\n            \"--output-format\",\n            \"text\",\n        ]\n        if key is None:\n            env = foreign_env({})\n        else:\n            config_dir = Path(tmp) / \"claude-config\"\n            config_dir.mkdir()\n            env = glm_env(key, config_dir, endpoint[1])\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, env, key, timeout=timeout, limit=limit)\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        error = fail(\"claude\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\", key)\n        # A failed call's printed answer travels along for the repair evidence; nothing else changes.\n        error.partial_answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n        raise error\n    answer = scrub(done.stdout or \"\", key)\n    if not answer.strip():\n        raise fail(\"claude\", done, \"the answer is empty\", key)\n    return answer\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "run_work_model",

          "truncated": false

A worktree still listed by git remains eligible even if its directory is gone.\n\n",

Then add current\n    contents without forcing ignored, untracked children of a replaced path into the tree.\n    The real index is only read; it, the stash and the refs are never\n    changed (spec, criterion 10).\n    \"\"\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        temporary_index = Path(tmp) / \"index\"\n        tracked = _git_bytes(root, \"ls-files\", \"-s\", \"-z\")\n        env = {**os.environ, \"GIT_INDEX_FILE\": str(temporary_index)}\n        _git_output(root, \"read-tree\", \"--empty\", env=env)\n        if tracked:\n            _git_bytes(\n                root,\n                \"update-index\",\n                \"-z\",\n                \"--index-info\",\n                env=env,\n                stdin=tracked,\n            )\n        _git_output(root, \"add\", \"-A\", env=env)\n        return _git_output(root, \"write-tree\", env=env).strip()\n",

          "excerpt": "def tool_state(root: Path) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The digest of the worktree's `.venv/` tree, taken before the model runs (R-21).\n\n    `.venv/` is ignored by git: a file there is invisible to `changed_paths` and survives\n    `restore_baseline`, so this digest is the only thing that shows an overwritten tool, a planted\n    `*.pth` file or a replaced package. Every file maps to the SHA-256 of its bytes and every symlink\n    to its target; the runner's steps run with the interpreter, ruff and packages of this tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    state: dict[str, str] = {}\n    venv = root / \".venv\"\n    try:\n        info = venv.lstat()\n        if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode):\n            # Record the root link AND digest its tools: an unchanged link must not hide\n            # overwritten target bytes. os.walk traverses its root even with followlinks=False;\n            # nested directory links remain opaque, and _unlink_cache still rejects this root.\n            state[\".venv\"] = \"link:\" + str(venv.readlink())\n    except FileNotFoundError:\n        return state\n    except OSError:\n        return {\".venv\": UNREADABLE}\n\n    def unreadable_directory(error: OSError) -> None:\n        # os.walk otherwise silently skips failed scandir calls, hiding newly planted caches.\n        path = Path(error.filename) if error.filename is not None else venv\n        state[path.relative_to(root).as_posix()] = UNREADABLE\n\n    for directory, names, files in os.walk(venv, onerror=unreadable_directory):\n        for name in sorted([*names, *files]):\n            path = Path(directory) / name\n            relative = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()\n            try:\n                if path.is_symlink():\n                    state[relative] = \"link:\" + str(path.readlink())\n                elif path.is_file():\n                    state[relative] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()\n            except OSError:\n                state[relative] = UNREADABLE\n    return state\n",

Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry.           "end_line": 11036,
          "excerpt": "def run_attempts(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    routes: list[tuple[tuple[str, str, str | None], str | None, str, str | None]],\n    build_prompt,  # (diagnostics, endpoint, inputs) -> prompt\n    baseline: str,\n    key: str | None,\n    ignored_before: dict[Path, tuple[int, int]] | None,\n    commit_message: str,\n    closing: str,\n    answer_check=None,  # answer -> problems, only when `verify_attempt` returned none\n    before_commit=None,  # a write between the checks and the checkpoint commit\n    after_commit=None,  # a write after the checkpoint commit\n    snapshot_findings=None,  # () -> the findings text as it stands right before the model call\n    restore_findings=None,  # (text) -> None, put findings.md back after a failed attempt\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,  # the `.venv/` digest the verb took before this call, else taken here\n    retain_answer: bool = False,  # repair: every attempt's protected answer is saved before any check can stop the run\n    verify_mode: str = \"full\",  # implement and repair: \"targeted\" (bead coding-harness-0swp); draft keeps its own path\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,  # implement: new production code without a reachable test refuses the attempt\n    protect_lifecycle: bool = False,  # repair: the change's lifecycle fields go back before any check reads them\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The attempt loop the work verbs share: call, measure, check, commit - or leave the diagnostics.\n\n    A failed attempt leaves its diagnostics and the files its model changed, quoted, below its audit\n    line in `findings.md`; the route block on `stage-1` names the verb. A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2). Before the failure is decided, findings.md is restored outright: every post-run check, cheap\n    or full, reads the runner's file, an edit alone fails nothing, and a completed attempt that edited\n    it carries a quoted restore notice under its audit line (spec, criteria 8 and 9).\n\n    A verb that passes `retain_answer` keeps every attempt's full answer: right at the model-return\n    boundary, before any HEAD check, verification or answer check can stop the run, the protected\n    answer is saved as local evidence and its location joins the attempt's diagnostics - the parser's\n    rejections, the call and verify failures included - and is printed on success (bead\n    coding-harness-hgvp). A failed call keeps the output it returned.\n\n    A verb that passes `protect_lifecycle` snapshots the change's lifecycle fields (`status`,\n    `implementation_status`) in spec, optional design and plan right before every call.           "excerpt": "def run_codex(\n    ctx: Context, prompt: str, resume: str | None = None, writable: bool = False, *, verb: str\n) -> tuple[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"One Codex call, first or resumed, pinned the same way. Returns (answer, thread id).\n\n    A review reads in the CLI's `read-only` sandbox; a draft writes in\n    `workspace-write`, and the runner puts back what lands outside the change\n    folder. No call takes a bypass flag (spec, criterion 1). The reasoning\n    effort is the caller verb's entry of `CODEX_EFFORTS`, passed explicitly on\n    every argv, a resumed call included; that a resumed thread actually runs at\n    that effort inside Codex is not asserted (bead coding-harness-yzk, Q-6).\n    Only the verbs `CODEX_EFFORTS` names (draft, repair, review) may carry a\n    Codex route; any other verb stops with a `KeyError` before the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    _, model, _ = CODEX\n    effort = CODEX_EFFORTS[verb]\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-\") as tmp:\n        answer_file = Path(tmp) / \"answer.md\"\n        command = [\"codex\", \"exec\"]\n        if resume:\n            command += [\"resume\", resume]\n        command += [\n            \"--json\",\n            \"-m\",\n            model,\n            \"-c\",\n            f'model_reasoning_effort=\"{effort}\"',\n            \"-c\",\n            f'sandbox_mode=\"{\"workspace-write\" if writable else \"read-only\"}\"',\n            \"--disable\",\n            \"hooks\",\n            \"--disable\",\n            \"memories\",\n            \"-o\",\n            str(answer_file),\n            prompt,\n        ]\n        done = launch(command, ctx.root, foreign_env({}))\n        thread = thread_id(done.stdout or \"\")\n        if done.returncode != 0:\n            raise failed_with_answer_file(fail(\"codex\", done, f\"exit {done.returncode}\"), answer_file)\n        if thread is None:\n            raise failed_with_answer_file(fail(\"codex\", done, \"no thread.started event\"), answer_file)\n        try:\n            answer = answer_file.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as error:\n            raise fail(\"codex\", done, \"no answer file\") from error\n    return answer, thread\n",

          "end_line": 8341,
          "excerpt": "def verify_attempt(\n    root: Path,\n    plan: Path,\n    key: str | None = None,\n    formatted: list[str] | None = None,\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None = None,\n    accepted_plan: bytes | None = None,\n    previous_failures: Sequence[str] = (),\n    mode: str = \"full\",\n    against: str = \"HEAD\",\n    scope: list[str] | None = None,\n    new_file_guard: bool = False,\n    clearing: ClearingEvidence | None = None,\n    verb: str = \"implement\",\n    evidence: list[str] | None = None,\n) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Format, run the cheap checks, clear derivable ledger markers, stamp documents, render, `make verify`.\n\n    Preparation writes to the tree and executes its registry renderer. Before `make verify` the\n    runner applies ruff's safe fixes and its formatter to the changed Python files under `scripts/`\n    and `tests/`; when `formatted` is given, the step's line lands there. The cheap checks follow:\n    read-only ruff lint and format checks, then pytest over the selected tests, with the first red,\n    launch error or timeout ending the attempt before the ledger clearing, the derived preparation\n    and `make verify` (spec, criteria 1, 2 and 10). Cheap green never replaces full verification.\n    Return bounded diagnostics for failed preparation or postconditions, naming the gates that\n    blocked. The time section must still be readable; the entry itself is the runner's\n    (`run_attempts`), so the model adds none and nothing is compared with the pre-call plan.\n    When `clearing` carries a container, the ledger clearing's exact rewrites are captured in it\n    for the work check's discount; without one, clearing stands unchanged for direct callers.\n\n    `mode=\"targeted\"` is the implement and repair post-run check (bead coding-harness-0swp): the same\n    format, cheap checks, ledger clearing and derived preparation run outside the verify admission,\n    and the attempt's delta against `against` selects the whole touched and import-linked test files,\n    ruff over the touched Python files and the existing local gates its file kinds need\n    (`targeted_selection`). A coverage that cannot be determined safely runs the admitted full\n    `make verify` instead, and a targeted red, launch failure or timeout fails the attempt - it never\n    falls back to the full check to override it. `new_file_guard` adds the implement-only refusal of\n    new production code without a reachable test. `scope` receives the runner-owned evidence line\n    that names the mode, the selected checks and the result. Draft keeps its own document-only path\n    (`verify_draft`). `verb` names the attempt type for the ledger classification - implement owes\n    every ledger test, repair only the written entries - and `evidence` collects the missing ledger\n    tests the attempt does not owe, one line each, for the attempt's record (spec, criteria 2, 5-7).\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n    tampered = tool_problem(root, tools)\n    if tampered:\n        # The attempt overwrote a program the runner starts: it fails here, before the renderer or\n        # ruff runs, and the diagnostic names the path (R-21, acceptance criterion).\n        return [tampered]\n    try:\n        # The marker of a test the attempt wrote is derivable, so it is not the attempt's to forget\n        # (bead coding-harness-7g6h); the stamp below then sees the plan as changed. The plan is an\n        # attempt-writable path: an alias (a symlink in it or its parents, a hard link) would carry the\n        # write outside the worktree, so it is refused first (runner review R-1, 2026-10-25).\n        relative = plan.relative_to(root)\n        if plan.is_symlink() or plan.resolve() != root.resolve() / relative:\n            return [f\"refusing an aliased plan before clearing its ledger: {relative.as_posix()}\"]\n   ",

          "excerpt": "def committed_runner_held(root: Path, code: str = \"HEAD\") -> tuple[str, ...]:\n    \"\"\"`RUNNER_HELD` as the selected trusted commit declares it (read, never executed).\"\"\"\n    source = git_out(root, \"show\", f\"{code}:scripts/stage2.py\")\n    try:\n        module = ast.parse(source)\n    except SyntaxError as error:\n        raise Failed(f\"committed scripts/stage2.py cannot be read as Python ({error})\") from error\n    for node in module.body:\n        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and any(\n            isinstance(target, ast.Name) and target.id == \"RUNNER_HELD\" for target in node.targets\n        ):\n            if not isinstance(node.value, ast.Tuple | ast.List) or not node.value.elts:\n                raise Failed(\"committed scripts/stage2.py declares no readable RUNNER_HELD tuple\")\n            parts = []\n            for element in node.value.elts:\n                if not isinstance(element, ast.Constant) or not isinstance(element.value, str):\n                    raise Failed(\"committed scripts/stage2.py declares a non-string RUNNER_HELD entry\")\n                parts.append(element.value)\n            return tuple(parts)\n    raise Failed(\"committed scripts/stage2.py declares no RUNNER_HELD\")\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_targeted_mode_is_repair_only(world: World, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 10 (repair-targeted-check).           "excerpt": "def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        description=__doc__,\n        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,\n        allow_abbrev=False,\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\"verb\", choices=sorted([*VERBS, \"session\", \"prepare-explore\"]))\n    parser.add_argument(\"change\", nargs=\"?\", default=\"\", help=\"folder name under plans/changes/\")\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"row_status\",\n        nargs=\"?\",\n        default=None,\n        metavar=\"ROW=STATUS\",\n        help=(\n            \"triage only: the loop row and its new status, e.g. 'L1-1=taken — not a test';           "excerpt": "def run(root: Path, change: str, model: str, handover: str | None, runner) -> None:\n    \"\"\"One checked session: worktree, declaration, handover, two scans, policy, dispatch, audit.\"\"\"\n    root = Path(root)\n    if not on_macos():\n        raise runner.Refused(\"session dispatches to macOS Terminal; this platform is not supported.\")\n    canonical_worktree(root, change, runner)\n    endpoint, transport, selection = resolve_endpoint(root, model, runner)\n    ctx = runner.preflight(root, change, endpoint)\n    prompt, source = handover_prompt(ctx, handover, runner)\n    if \"\\x00\" in prompt:\n        raise runner.Refused(\"the handover text holds a NUL byte; the launch transport cannot carry it.\")\n    if len(prompt.encode(\"utf-8\")) > PROMPT_LIMIT:\n        raise runner.Refused(\n            f\"the prompt is {len(prompt.encode('utf-8'))} UTF-8 bytes; a session takes at most {PROMPT_LIMIT}.\"\n        )\n    cli, terminal = executables(transport, runner)\n    if transport == \"pi\":\n        if prompt.startswith(\"@\"):\n            raise runner.Refused(\n                \"the handover text starts with `@`; Pi would read the rest as a file name, so no session starts.\"\n            )\n        runner.require_pi()\n    runner.checked_prompt(ctx, endpoint, prompt)\n    private = prepare(root, transport, cli, runner)\n    producer = \"codex\" if transport == \"codex\" else \"pi\"\n    try:\n        destination = None\n        address_notice = None\n        if transport == \"pi\":\n            # The initial model binds offline, before anything dispatches: the\n            # checked definition goes into the private launch directory as the\n            # sidecar the policy copy reads, and the installed Pi must resolve\n            # it - otherwise the preparation refuses and no session starts.\n            binding, verdict = checked_session_model(root, endpoint[1], runner)\n            address_notice = verdict.notice\n            try:\n                # The extension's binding record: the provider and the checked\n                # definition it registers - the flat effective definition itself\n                # stays the dispatch destination.\n                (private / MODEL_SIDECAR).write_text(\n                    json.dumps({\"provider\": stage2_go.PROVIDER, \"model\": binding}), encoding=\"utf-8\"\n                )\n            except OSError as error:\n                raise runner.Refused(\n                    f\"the checked model could not be written into the private launch directory: {error}\"\n                ) from error\n            confirm_binding(root, cli, private / POLICY_FILE, endpoint[1], runner)\n            destination = binding\n        result = runner.checked_prompt(ctx, endpoint, prompt)\n        command = terminal_command(\n            root,\n            runner.foreign_env({}),\n            cli_argv(transport, root, cli, selection, prompt, private / POLICY_FILE),\n        )\n        if len(command.encode(\"utf-8\")) > COMMAND_LIMIT:\n            raise runner.Refused(\n                f\"the dispatch command is {len(command.encode('utf-8'))} bytes; the launch transport takes at most {COMMAND_LIMIT}.\"\n            )\n        attempt = uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]\n\n        def send():\n            line = audit_line(runner, attempt, selection, endpoint, source, result)\n            if address_notice:\n                line = f\"Address notice: {address_notice}\\n\\n{line}\"\n            write_pending(ctx, runner, line, producer)\n            return dispatch(terminal, private / SCRIPT_NAME, command)\n\n        if endpoint[0] == \"opencode-go\":\n            accepted, detail = runner.dispatch_go(\n                root, endpoint[1], send, destination=destination, configuration=private / MODEL_SIDECAR\n            )\n        else:\n            accepted, detail = send()\n    except BaseException:  # any failure before the dispatch, Ctrl-C included, leaves no private directory\n        shutil.rmtree(private, ignore_errors=True)\n        raise\n    if not accepted:\n        shutil.rmtree(private, ignore_errors=True)\n     ",

          "excerpt": "def worktree_field(run: RunCommand, worktree: Path | None) -> str:\n    \"\"\"How many non-bare worktrees are registered with this repository - stale ones included, never pruned.\"\"\"\n    if worktree is None:\n        return f\"{NOT_READ} (worktree: not identified)\"\n    try:\n        raw = run([\"git\", \"-C\", str(worktree), \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\", \"-z\"])\n        records = worktree_records(raw)\n    except run_report.SourceError as error:\n        return str(error)\n    count = sum(1 for record in records if \"bare\" not in record)\n    return f\"{count} (git worktree list; non-bare entries, stale registrations included)\"\n",

          "excerpt": "def save_attempt(root: Path, baseline: str, change: str, label: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Save the worktree as it stands after a failed call on a local ref; say where, or why not.\n\n    A failed call is not a worthless one: a run that hits a spent budget after hours of edits still\n    holds them (bead coding-harness-znc). The snapshot goes through a temporary index, so the real\n    index and the files stay untouched; tracked and untracked files go in, gitignored ones do not.\n    The temporary index is seeded with the baseline, as in `worktree_tree`, so a file tracked although\n    ignored stays in the snapshot. The commit's parent is the baseline, so `git diff <baseline> <ref>`\n    shows everything the run left in the tree: this attempt, any earlier attempt of the run whose tree\n    it started on, and the runner's own writes. The ref lives under `refs/stage2/attempts/`, which no\n    branch push carries. A save that fails is named and never blocks the restore that follows.\n    The commit carries the runner's own identity, so a machine without a configured git user (a CI\n    runner) saves as well, and the ref says who wrote it.\n    \"\"\"\n    stamp = utc_now().strftime(\"%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ\")\n    ref = f\"refs/stage2/attempts/{change}/{label}-{stamp}\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-save-\") as scratch:\n        env = {**os.environ, \"GIT_INDEX_FILE\": str(Path(scratch) / \"index\"), **SAVE_IDENTITY}\n        try:\n            _git_output(root, \"read-tree\", baseline, env=env)\n            _git_output(root, \"add\", \"-A\", \"--\", \".\", env=env)\n            tree = _git_output(root, \"write-tree\", env=env).strip()\n            commit = _git_output(\n                root, \"commit-tree\", tree, \"-p\", baseline, \"-m\", f\"stage2: saved {label} of {change}\", env=env\n            ).strip()\n            _git_output(root, \"update-ref\", ref, commit)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            return f\"saving the attempt failed ({error})\"\n    return f\"the attempt is saved at {ref} ({commit[:12]}); `git diff {baseline[:12]} {ref}` shows it\"\n",

          "end_line": 1535,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",

Amends ADR 0021\n  decision 6; supersedes no ADR. Amends no D- or O-number.\n* Review: the maintainer decided on 2026-11-08, in the conversation, that\n  ADR 0021 decision 6 changes together with the runner change that makes a\n  repair pass on a targeted check (pull request #343, bead\n  coding-harness-gxwg), and that the amendment travels in a decision pull\n  request of its own (answer \"Fertig machen + ADR-PR\"), and answered its\n  interview the same day (`plans/changes/adr-repair-check/decisions.md`,\n  Q-1 to Q-5).           "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names.           "excerpt": "## Decision Drivers\n\n* No Z.ai budget is spent on repairs.\n* Every taken finding still carries the existing evidence and checkpoint guards.\n* A re-check receives no repair-session history.\n* An unavailable Codex call does not silently switch the repair budget.\n* The earlier routing decision remains readable as superseded history.\n\n",

        {
          "citation": "docs/adr/0017-codex-repairs-taken-findings.md::Considered Options",
          "end_line": 70,
          "excerpt": "## Considered Options\n\n* **Codex repairs both kinds, with a fresh Codex re-check** — chosen (Q-1, Q-2).\n* **Keep GLM 5.3 repairs** — preserves model separation but spends the budget\n  the maintainer wants to reserve.\n* **Codex repairs only one kind of finding** — retains two repair routes and\n  some GLM repair spend; rejected in Q-2.\n* **Another phase-6 model or an extra loop round** — adds independent model\n  review or another pass, but moves its budget or changes the round count;\n  rejected in Q-1.\n* **GLM as last attempt, or no last attempt** — respectively spends Z.ai\n  budget or abandons a repair after two post-check failures; Q-3 chose Sonnet.\n* **Automatic fallback on Codex call failure** — avoids an explicit restart\n  but hides an availability-driven budget switch; rejected in Q-4.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",

        {
          "citation": "docs/adr/0017-codex-repairs-taken-findings.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 120,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"Codex repairs both kinds, with a fresh Codex re-check\",\nbecause it implements the maintainer's model choice without weakening the\nrepair evidence contract.\n\n1. **Codex repairs all taken findings in one batch** through `python3\n   scripts/stage2.py repair <change>`: loop-record rows, released loop rows\n   and phase-6 findings. Each Codex attempt starts `gpt-6.1-sol` at effort\n   `max` in a fresh session, with the existing `workspace-write` configuration,\n   hooks and memories off, and no added directory, automatic approval or\n   bypass. Repair reads no GLM key and never routes to `glm-coding-plan`.\n2. **Only post-run failures advance the chain:** Codex; a fresh Codex attempt\n   with the first attempt's diagnostics; Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` on\n   Stage 1 with both diagnostics. A model call failure stops; with unchanged\n   HEAD, the existing restoration returns the worktree to baseline. When\n   Codex is unavailable, the orchestrator deliberately starts\n   `--stage2-off <reason>`, which uses Sonnet alone and records why. A\n   declaration refusal or leak-check BLOCK stops without fallback.\n3. **The orchestrator decides, the verb repairs, the reviewer re-checks.**\n   The orchestrator writes `taken — <reason>` or `rejected — <reason>`, or\n   takes a finding no test can show as `taken — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Repair keeps those inputs, requests one fixed line per row and a measured\n   time entry, and starts no review. The runner checks each exact prompt,\n   prepares and formats the result, runs `make verify`, checks the time and\n   evidence, writes statuses and makes one clean descendant checkpoint.\n   A Codex call that moves HEAD stops before restoration or a runner commit.\n4. **The existing proof and statuses stand.** A code finding requires a\n   defined test the runner demonstrates red against baseline code; a finding\n   taken as `not a test` is proven by the separate re-check. Fixed rows read\n   `fixed — tests/<path>::<function>` or `fixed — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Failed attempts retain their audit, quoted diagnostics and changed-file\n   evidence, while their model-written statuses are restored. Private loop\n   rows are marked only after the checkpoint; unreleased rows reach the\n   repair in the prompt rather than a worktree file.\n5. **The same model may repair phase-6 findings; a fresh session re-checks.**\n   A phase-6 verdict after an earlier `## Phase 6` block in `findings.md` — a\n   re-check — runs Codex read-only without resuming the repair, a prior\n   verdict or a historical phase-2a session; the first phase-6 review keeps\n   the resume rule of ADR 0016. Loop marks may\n   resume only that new verdict thread after its verdict. This replaces ADR\n   0015's blanket reviewer/repairer separation; it does not give review calls\n   write tools or move any review to another model.",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Worktrees — one per change",
          "end_line": 911,
          "excerpt": "### Worktrees — one per change\n\nWritten 2026-09-29 from D-5 (worktrees in the repository, through the tool's own\nmechanism), ADR 0006 (parallel work, one worktree per session) and the\nmeasurement of 2026-09-23 (`docs/research/2026-09-23-worktree-tracker-writes.md`).\nThe same rule holds in `lakeswitch-ai`, with the differences its\n`docs/workflow.md` §9 lists.\n\n1. **One change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.** Two sessions\n   never share a worktree, and nobody switches the branch of the main checkout\n   while another session runs.\n2. **In the repository, under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`.** That directory is in\n   `.gitignore` already, and it is where Claude Code puts its own worktrees\n   (`claude --worktree <name>`, and a sub-agent's `isolation: worktree`). By\n   hand: `git fetch origin && git worktree add -b <branch>\n   .claude/worktrees/<name> origin/main`. `bd worktree create` works as well but\n   writes the worktree's path into the tracked `.gitignore`, which is one more\n   change in the diff. Sibling directories beside the repository are retired\n   (D-5); worktrees that still sit there are finished and removed, not moved.\n3. **Always from a freshly fetched `origin/main`.** A worktree on a stale base\n   produces a pull request that is behind before it opens.\n4. **The tracker needs nothing.** `tools/bd` in a worktree finds the main\n   checkout's tracker through the shared git directory — no variable, no\n   redirect file, no copy. Concurrent writers lose nothing and a contested\n   claim has exactly one winner (measured 2026-09-23 with bd 1.3.0). Who may\n   write is house rule 4: the first writing session writes the tracker; every\n   other session claims its one bead with `tools/bd update <id> --claim\n   --actor <session>` and leaves its handover comment on that bead, nothing\n   more.           "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "excerpt": "# isolated-attempts — Decisions\n\nClass: architectural (bead coding-harness-s9r; it changes how every writing verb of the runner runs a model and amends the doctrine sentence in `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3). The interview ran in the conversation on 2026-11-22; the answers are recorded below with the options as they were put. Earlier decisions it builds on: the shared design of 2026-10-16 (beads coding-harness-6ie and coding-harness-s9r), the design of 2026-11-12 that folded coding-harness-c99h, -t3s3, -znc and -6ie into this bead, and the retention answer of 2026-11-03 (coding-harness-c99h Q-1).\n\n## Q-1 · Direction: own worktree per attempt, or the three-way comparison\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — open the lane now on the 2026-11-12 design, without the three-way comparison of 2026-10-23; the orchestrator re-checks it against the alternatives.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: how a writing attempt is isolated.\n  Intention: a failed attempt leaves its changes in the lane worktree and the next step trips over them; on 2026-11-22 this happened three times (u1ha, ttic, i76l).\n  Today: every attempt writes in the lane worktree.\n  Repository change: Options: A open now on the 2026-11-12 design (own git worktree per attempt from the fixed base, failed attempt saved as a side ref, fallback builds on it); B after Monday in a block with the maintainer; C first compare worktree, container (Podman/Docker) and k3s/OpenShift.\n  Architecture change: a new attempt lifecycle for all writing verbs.\n\nIn the context of writing attempts that damage the next one, facing a cheap per-attempt worktree or a heavier container or cluster, we decided to build the per-attempt worktree now, to achieve an end to the hand clean-up at the lowest cost, accepting that network access and foreign file reads are not covered by this change. — 2026-11-22\n\nThe orchestrator's re-check: the worktree covers the damage class (lane and runner inputs) at seconds per attempt; a container adds a network lock and blocks foreign reads but needs a Linux VM on macOS and stalled on 2026-10-15 (branch explore/isolated-attempts); k3s/OpenShift is heavier still. A container can later sit on top of the worktree (bead coding-harness-yw2p).\n\n## Q-2 · Threat model\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — an attempt may damage its own worktree in any way (delete, edit, symlink, replace inputs); the lane and every file the runner reads its next prompt from stay untouched; network access and reading foreign files are out of scope, with their own bead (coding-harness-yw2p).\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: which model behaviour the runner must withstand.\n  Intention: the spec states the threat model (bead).\n  Today: no stated model; each repair closed one case (codex-repairs F-8, F-10..F-14).\n  Repository change: Options: A lane and runner inputs only; B also block foreign file reads without a container; C container from the start.\n  Architecture change: none beyond Q-1.\n\nIn the context of the threat model, facing a narrow or a wide scope, we decided to protect the lane and the runner's inputs only, to achieve a small change that can be built and checked in days, accepting that network and foreign reads wait for the container bead. — 2026-11-22\n\n## Q-3 · Environment in the attempt worktree\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — the attempt worktree links the lane's .venv and installed Pi; a lane without them is refused before the model call with the remedy (make venv, tools/pi/install.sh); the runner checksums the shared environment before and after each attempt and rejects the attempt on a difference.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: where an attempt worktree gets its Python environment and Pi.\n  Intention: without the pinned Pi about 110 tests fail and an attempt goes red for an environment reason (0zhf attempts 2 and 3, 2026-11-22).\n  Today: the lane worktree carries both.\n  Repository change: Options: A link the lane's environme",

          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",

When\n   Codex is unavailable, the orchestrator deliberately starts\n   `--stage2-off <reason>`, which uses Sonnet alone and records why. A\n   declaration refusal or leak-check BLOCK stops without fallback.\n3. **The orchestrator decides, the verb repairs, the reviewer re-checks.**\n   The orchestrator writes `taken — <reason>` or `rejected — <reason>`, or\n   takes a finding no test can show as `taken — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Repair keeps those inputs, requests one fixed line per row and a measured\n   time entry, and starts no review. The runner checks each exact prompt,\n   prepares and formats the result, runs `make verify`, checks the time and\n   evidence, writes statuses and makes one clean descendant checkpoint.\n   A Codex call that moves HEAD stops before restoration or a runner commit.\n4. **The existing proof and statuses stand.** A code finding requires a\n   defined test the runner demonstrates red against baseline code; a finding\n   taken as `not a test` is proven by the separate re-check. Private loop\n   rows are marked only after the checkpoint; unreleased rows reach the\n   repair in the prompt rather than a worktree file.\n5. **The same model may repair phase-6 findings; a fresh session re-checks.**\n   A phase-6 verdict after an earlier `## Phase 6` block in `findings.md` — a\n   re-check — runs Codex read-only without resuming the repair, a prior\n   verdict or a historical phase-2a session; the first phase-6 review keeps\n   the resume rule of ADR 0016. Loop marks may\n   resume only that new verdict thread after its verdict. This replaces ADR\n   0015's blanket reviewer/repairer separation; it does not give review calls\n   write tools or move any review to another model.\n6. **The loop budget and run count stand.** A fixed row counts as taken;\n   round 3 requires a taken or fixed row in round 2, and the maximum stays\n   three rounds.           "citation": "docs/adr/0014-a-change-claims-its-adr-files.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 147,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen: option (1), with the inference removed, the reverse direction held,\nand the whole gate carried by the kit with a day per repository — because an\nattribution per edit needs the claim where the edit is made, one rule is\neasier to hold than an explicit rule beside a guess, and a workflow rule that\nholds in one repository alone is not a rule of the workflow (Q-1 to Q-5).\n\n**What is decided**, in five points:\n\n1. A change claims, in the header of its own spec, every file under\n   `docs/adr/` it creates, changes or removes. A later change that amends an\n   ADR claims that amendment itself.\n2. An ADR edit belongs to the change of the measured work that claims it. A\n   change that does not claim the file is no owner of it, whatever else the\n   work touches. The owner owes five interview answers of the maintainer,\n   whatever its class and its date.\n3. An ADR edit that no change of the work claims is a finding that names the\n   remedy. Nothing infers an owner from the paths a diff touches or from an\n   ADR's text.\n4. For a feature begun after its repository adopted the gate, the answer \"yes\"\n   comes with at least one claimed ADR file, and the answer \"no\" with none.\n5. The interview gate travels with the kit as mechanism. Each repository\n   records the day it adopted the gate; a change begun on or before that day\n   is exempt from the class minimums and from point 4, never from points 2 and\n   3. Moving that day is a decision pull request.\n\n**How it holds from this change on:**\n\n* The claim is the spec header field `adr_files`; the gate\n  `interview-minimums` (`scripts/check_interview_minimums.py`) holds points 2\n  to 4.\n* The day stands in `decisions/adoption.yaml`, a file that stays in its\n  repository; this repository's day is 2026-10-08, the day it adopted the\n  gate, so no change here moves between stock and subject. The gate reads the\n  day through `scripts/adoption.py`, which any other gate can call with its\n  own id (bead coding-harness-wpv); without the record the gate does not\n  measure (exit 3).\n* The gate script, its test, the reader and the reader's test travel as\n  mechanism (`scripts/kit/manifest.yaml`); the record stays as stock. An\n  instance such as LakeSwitch receives them with its next pinned Coding\n  Harness release (bead coding-harness-dj9).\n\n**What this record does not fix.** The field's name, the record's name and\nform, the reader and the gate's messages are the change's design: they change\nin an ordinary change as long as the five points hold.\n\nThis record amends no D- or O-number. It replaces the attribution of the\narchived change interview-minimums — the change folders a diff touches — and\nthe interim rule of pull request #126; ADR 0013 is unchanged.\n\n",

          "citation": "plans/changes/isolated-attempts/decisions.md::Q-1 · Direction: own worktree per attempt, or the three-way comparison",
          "end_line": 40,
          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · Direction: own worktree per attempt, or the three-way comparison\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — open the lane now on the 2026-11-12 design, without the three-way comparison of 2026-10-23; the orchestrator re-checks it against the alternatives.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: how a writing attempt is isolated.\n  Intention: a failed attempt leaves its changes in the lane worktree and the next step trips over them; on 2026-11-22 this happened three times (u1ha, ttic, i76l).\n  Today: every attempt writes in the lane worktree.\n  Repository change: Options: A open now on the 2026-11-12 design (own git worktree per attempt from the fixed base, failed attempt saved as a side ref, fallback builds on it); B after Monday in a block with the maintainer; C first compare worktree, container (Podman/Docker) and k3s/OpenShift.\n  Architecture change: a new attempt lifecycle for all writing verbs.\n\nIn the context of writing attempts that damage the next one, facing a cheap per-attempt worktree or a heavier container or cluster, we decided to build the per-attempt worktree now, to achieve an end to the hand clean-up at the lowest cost, accepting that network access and foreign file reads are not covered by this change. — 2",
          "kind": "local",

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::Sessions across checkouts",
          "end_line": 186,
          "excerpt": "## Sessions across checkouts\n\n- **Another session in the same checkout:** say so before changing a file,\n  committing or switching the branch, and offer a worktree. House rule 4 holds\n  for the tracker meanwhile.\n- **Worktrees: one change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.**\n  A worktree lives under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`, is branched from a freshly fetched `origin/main`,\n  and is removed after the merge; tracker access, claims and sibling directories: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3.\n  Each new checkout or worktree runs `make venv` and `bash tools/pi/install.sh` once before `make verify`\n  (`PYTHON=` picks a 3.12+ interpreter; one that does not match the lock fails the suite, bead\n  coding-harness-ei0; the Pi tests and the swarms need the pinned Pi, bead coding-harness-hs0o).\n- **A text-only change (Markdown outside `scripts/`, `tests/`, `prompts/`,\n  `decisions/`) skips the local `make verify`;** CI is its gate.\n- **Omnigent starts inside the worktree** (ADR 0006). Its default policy (`tools/omnigent/`) is a second layer;\n  nothing depends on it alone. Which tools are denied or asked, and why: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3, \"Worktrees\".\n- **What could not be read is \"not read\", never \"none\"** — an unopened file\n  and an empty query say different things.\n- **A standing rule belongs in the repository's `AGENTS.md`** — every harness\n  reads it; chat, memory and a user file do not reach the next one. Where an\n  agent may not write it (lakeswitch: `human-decided`), propose the text.\n- **Research about this repository lives in `docs/research/`.** A vault note,\n  chat or rendered page is a view of it: it names the source path and commit,\n  and a finding is never first written there. Personal reasons to care stay\n  outside the repository.\n- **The maintainer's Claude Code display** (status line, session entry, handover safety net, `/handover`) lives\n  in `tools/claude-code/`; change it there and reinstall with `tools/claude-code/install.sh`, never only in `~/.claude`.\n- **Sub-agents survive a budget pause** (maintainer, 2026-10-06). Each commits\n  and pushes after every green step and ends its report with a `Resume:` line;\n  the orchestrator keeps a list (agent id, branch, last pushed commit, next\n  step) and resumes or restarts there. One change at a time, with few agents\n  and a visible queue. A long runner job starts in the harness's background mode, one job per call — never with `&` or `nohup` inside a command, which ends without a notice and leaves a lane idle unseen (maintainer, 2026-11-04). Every night run arms a recurring 30-minute wake, keeps the machine awake, and checks and logs its lanes as described in `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, ‘Night runs’.\n- **Pu",

Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry.           "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",
