          "excerpt": "## Sessions across checkouts\n\n- **Another session in the same checkout:** say so before changing a file,\n  committing or switching the branch, and offer a worktree. House rule 4 holds\n  for the tracker meanwhile.\n- **Worktrees: one change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.**\n  A worktree lives under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`, is branched from a freshly fetched `origin/main`,\n  and is removed after the merge; tracker access, claims and sibling directories: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3.\n  Each new checkout or worktree runs `make venv` and `bash tools/pi/install.sh` once before `make verify`\n  (`PYTHON=` picks a 3.12+ interpreter; one that does not match the lock fails the suite, bead\n  coding-harness-ei0; the Pi tests and the swarms need the pinned Pi, bead coding-harness-hs0o).\n- **A text-only change (Markdown outside `scripts/`, `tests/`, `prompts/`,\n  `decisions/`) skips the local `make verify`;** CI is its gate.\n- **Omnigent starts inside the worktree** (ADR 0006). Its default policy (`tools/omnigent/`) is a second layer;\n  nothing depends on it alone. Which tools are denied or asked, and why: `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3, \"Worktrees\".\n- **What could not be read is \"not read\", never \"none\"** — an unopened file\n  and an empty query say different things.\n- **A standing rule belongs in the repository's `AGENTS.md`** — every harness\n  reads it; chat, memory and a user file do not reach the next one. Where an\n  agent may not write it (lakeswitch: `human-decided`), propose the text.\n- **Research about this repository lives in `docs/research/`.** A vault note,\n  chat or rendered page is a view of it: it names the source path and commit,\n  and a finding is never first written there. Personal reasons to care stay\n  outside the repository.\n- **The maintainer's Claude Code display** (status line, session entry, handover safety net, `/handover`) lives\n  in `tools/claude-code/`; change it there and reinstall with `tools/claude-code/install.sh`, never only in `~/.claude`.\n- **Sub-agents survive a budget pause** (maintainer, 2026-10-06). Each commits\n  and pushes after every green step and ends its report with a `Resume:` line;\n  the orchestrator keeps a list (agent id, branch, last pushed commit, next\n  step) and resumes or restarts there. One change at a time, with few agents\n  and a visible queue. A long runner job starts in the harness's background mode, one job per call — never with `&` or `nohup` inside a command, which ends without a notice and leaves a lane idle unseen (maintainer, 2026-11-04). Every night run arms a recurring 30-minute wake, keeps the machine awake, and checks and logs its lanes as described in `docs/WORKFLOW.md`, ‘Night runs’.\n- **Pull requests stay mergeable:** synced daily, asked about after five working\n  days, three per hot file, sliced over ~800 lines, merged through the merge queue at their exact head (without it: one at a time against the new head once every check completed); questions in one 15:00 block (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n- **Findings returned as text** (when the harness refuses a reviewer's write)\n  are committed unchanged by the orchestrator, which says so in the commit.\n  MINOR rows on tests, security or false statements are repaired without asking; style rows\n  are accepted limits named in the PR. A second finding of one mechanism ends case repair; a mechanism no choke point closes gets a `Boundary` in its spec; a hand repair marks the loop row `fixed`, regenerates the index after a header edit and stamps after local midnight (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4).\n- **An exhausted review ladder goes to phase 6** (maintainer, 2026-11-20): when\n  `review-loop` refuses because every stage of its run is consumed and the last\n  round was not clean, and every taken row of that round is repaired, the lane\n  goes to the phase-6 review instead of a new loop run; phase 6 checks that last\n  repair. Reason: a run's history cannot be reset, and asking each time stopped\n  lanes overnight.\n\n",

Any\n  other cross-folder edit breaks that rule again.\n* **Nothing states an owner.** `owner:` in an ADR header names a role, never\n  a change (`provenance.yaml`, the roles block). An answer file binds a change\n  to its answer, never an ADR to a change, and its format (`schema_version:\n  1`) is shared with LakeSwitch and frozen \"not now\"\n  (`docs/research/2026-10-11-adr-answer-pin-plan.md`).\n* **A \"yes\" is not followed up.** `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §2 said: \"Nothing checks\n  … that a 'yes' is followed by an ADR.\"\n* **The gate does not travel.** The gate list that runs it travels with the\n  kit, the script does not, and its cut-off is a constant holding this\n  repository's day, 2026-10-08 (`scripts/kit/manifest.yaml`, read at\n  `2d6a1c6`). Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry.           "end_line": 1535,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",

      "statement": "Framework, kit and instance responsibility is drawn by prefix in `scripts/kit/manifest.yaml`: `mechanismus` 'runs unchanged in a foreign repository', `bestand` 'stays here', and `scripts/` is a catch-all `bestand` (with `docs/WORKFLOW.md` and `prompts/` explicitly `mechanismus`). `scripts/kit/probe.py::rolle` resolves by longest matching prefix and treats an unmatched path as BLOCK.           "excerpt": "def worktree_digests(root: Path) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The 8-character record digests of every worktree `git worktree list` names for this root.\n\n    The listing is this repository's, including worktrees whose directories are missing.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        listing = _git_output(root, \"worktree\", \"list\", \"--porcelain\")\n    except Refused as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"worktree discovery failed: {error}\") from error\n    digests: list[str] = []\n    for line in listing.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(\"worktree \"):\n            continue\n        path = Path(line[len(\"worktree \") :]).resolve()\n        digest = record_key(\"\", path).rsplit(\"@\", 1)[1]\n        if digest not in digests:\n            digests.append(digest)\n    return digests\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::record_key",
          "end_line": 4059,
          "excerpt": "def record_key(change: str, root: Path) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The record's name: the change and a digest of the resolved repository root.\n\n    Two worktrees may hold the same change folder, and one `release-loop` must not delete the\n    other's record or hand it another's state (R-2 of the review-swarm review).\n    \"\"\"\n    return f\"{change}@{hashlib.sha256(str(root.resolve()).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()[:8]}\"\n",

          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell.           "excerpt": "## The workflow in one screen\n\n| # | Phase | Artifact | Gate |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Explore | `plans/changes/<name>/research.md` | — |\n| 1a | Interview | `decisions.md` | the class minimums met — feature ≥ 3 · ADR change ≥ 5 (feature with ADR: 5 total) · spike 3 topics or reasoned skip · bounded 1 or reasoned skip — gate `interview-minimums` |\n| 2 | Spec | `spec.md` | validator green, no open `[DECISION]` |\n| 2a | Spec-Review *(optional)* | lines for `findings.md`, dimension SPEC | no open `[AMBIGUITY]` |\n| 2b | Design *(by class)* | `design.md` | validator green; an ADR draft when `architectural` |\n| 3 | Plan | `plan.md` | validator green |\n| 4 | Implement | code + tests | `make verify` green |\n| 4b | Review loop *(stage 2)* | loop rows, into `findings.md` after the phase-6 verdict | rounds until a clean round — the free swarm, the Flash swarm, then the paid ladder (ADR 0021); a targeted check after each runner repair and each orchestrator hand repair, the full `make verify` before phase 6 |\n| 5 | Verify | test output as evidence | stop-hook blocks on a red tree |\n| 6 | Review | `findings.md` | no open BLOCKER — `[DIVERGENT]` counts as BLOCKER |\n| 7 | Commit | pull request | CI green |\n\n**Stage 2** (framework content, ADR 0007 as amended by ADR 0011 and ADR 0016): a foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py`, which runs the leak check before every call. Codex drafts spec, design and plan (`draft <change>`; GLM 5.3 after two failed attempts) and reviews 6; Opus 5.5 reviews 2a (`spec-review <change>`); the review loop (4b) runs on OpenCode Go through Pi until a clean round (ADR 0021): round 1 is the free swarm, the models the `free_stage` rule selects from a forced live catalog refresh, on the implementation diff alone with no tools; round 2 is the Flash swarm, up to three cheapest reachable admitted paid models in parallel; then one id of the `opencode-go` entry's `modelle` set per round, cheapest first: the runner orders it by the declared `anfragen_5h` (requests per 5 hours, more is cheaper); a failed Flash member is replaced by the cheapest unconsumed one. Of its decision, a worker's claim of its own bead stays\n  in force, and a worker's creating follow-up work and closing its bead\n  pass to the first session, as D-60 has it.\n* **ADR 0002 is superseded in part** as well: its pilot store, its W1\n  activation condition and its M0 validation lapse with the pilot. Until it does, the\n  bounds are stated and not enforced; the maintainer's display warns of a\n  second session in the same checkout (`tools/claude-code/`). It is to be re-scoped to the D-60 guard and the\n  events-journal check; this ADR does not write the tracker.\n* **Worktrees are not a security boundary.** Without an Omnigent sandbox, a\n  worktree keeps sessions from colliding; it does not confine what an agent\n  can reach. Planted fault: a runner time/date read sits outside the clock boundary.\n\n    The guard reads the runner module as source, so it sees what an alias\n    hides; the boundary exemption is proven necessary, not vacuous, by\n    running the same guard once without it.\n    \"\"\"\n    source = (REPO_ROOT / \"scripts\" / \"stage2.py\").read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    assert re.search(r\"(?m)^def clock_now\\(\", source), \"the module defines no clock boundary\"\n    assert clock_guard_violations(source) == [], \"a raw clock read bypasses stage2.clock_now\"\n    boundary = [\n        node for node in ast.parse(source).body if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name == \"clock_now\"\n    ]\n    assert len(boundary) == 1, \"the module must define exactly one clock boundary\"\n    body_lines = range(boundary[0].lineno, (boundary[0].end_lineno or boundary[0].lineno) + 1)\n    without_boundary = clock_guard_violations(source, boundary=\"\")\n    assert without_boundary, \"the exemption is vacuous: the boundary body reads no clock\"\n    lines = [int(re.search(r\"at line (\\d+)$\", finding).group(1)) for finding in without_boundary]\n    assert all(line in body_lines for line in lines), without_boundary\n",

A verb that passes\n    `snapshot_findings` and `restore_findings` puts findings.md back as it stood right before the model\n    call whenever an attempt fails: the audit line above the snapshot stays, the model's own edits to\n    the file - a Status it wrote itself included - go, so no failed run leaves them behind (phase 6,\n    F-2). Before the failure is decided, findings.md is restored outright: every post-run check, cheap\n    or full, reads the runner's file, an edit alone fails nothing, and a completed attempt that edited\n    it carries a quoted restore notice under its audit line (spec, criteria 8 and 9).\n\n    A verb that passes `retain_answer` keeps every attempt's full answer: right at the model-return\n    boundary, before any HEAD check, verification or answer check can stop the run, the protected\n    answer is saved as local evidence and its location joins the attempt's diagnostics - the parser's\n    rejections, the call and verify failures included - and is printed on success (bead\n    coding-harness-hgvp).           "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::The runner is the only way",
          "end_line": 1535,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",

          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`.           "end_line": 5963,
          "excerpt": "def save_attempt(root: Path, baseline: str, change: str, label: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Save the worktree as it stands after a failed call on a local ref; say where, or why not.\n\n    A failed call is not a worthless one: a run that hits a spent budget after hours of edits still\n    holds them (bead coding-harness-znc). The snapshot goes through a temporary index, so the real\n    index and the files stay untouched; tracked and untracked files go in, gitignored ones do not.\n    The temporary index is seeded with the baseline, as in `worktree_tree`, so a file tracked although\n    ignored stays in the snapshot. The commit's parent is the baseline, so `git diff <baseline> <ref>`\n    shows everything the run left in the tree: this attempt, any earlier attempt of the run whose tree\n    it started on, and the runner's own writes. The ref lives under `refs/stage2/attempts/`, which no\n    branch push carries. A save that fails is named and never blocks the restore that follows.\n    The commit carries the runner's own identity, so a machine without a configured git user (a CI\n    runner) saves as well, and the ref says who wrote it.\n    \"\"\"\n    stamp = utc_now().strftime(\"%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ\")\n    ref = f\"refs/stage2/attempts/{change}/{label}-{stamp}\"\n    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix=\"stage2-save-\") as scratch:\n        env = {**os.environ, \"GIT_INDEX_FILE\": str(Path(scratch) / \"index\"), **SAVE_IDENTITY}\n        try:\n            _git_output(root, \"read-tree\", baseline, env=env)\n            _git_output(root, \"add\", \"-A\", \"--\", \".\", env=env)\n            tree = _git_output(root, \"write-tree\", env=env).strip()\n            commit = _git_output(\n                root, \"commit-tree\", tree, \"-p\", baseline, \"-m\", f\"stage2: saved {label} of {change}\", env=env\n            ).strip()\n            _git_output(root, \"update-ref\", ref, commit)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            return f\"saving the attempt failed ({error})\"\n    return f\"the attempt is saved at {ref} ({commit[:12]}); `git diff {baseline[:12]} {ref}` shows it\"\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "end_line": 5630,
          "excerpt": "def tool_state(root: Path) -> dict[str, str]:\n    \"\"\"The digest of the worktree's `.venv/` tree, taken before the model runs (R-21).\n\n    `.venv/` is ignored by git: a file there is invisible to `changed_paths` and survives\n    `restore_baseline`, so this digest is the only thing that shows an overwritten tool, a planted\n    `*.pth` file or a replaced package. Every file maps to the SHA-256 of its bytes and every symlink\n    to its target; the runner's steps run with the interpreter, ruff and packages of this tree.\n    \"\"\"\n    state: dict[str, str] = {}\n    venv = root / \".venv\"\n    try:\n        info = venv.lstat()\n        if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode):\n            # Record the root link AND digest its tools: an unchanged link must not hide\n            # overwritten target bytes. os.walk traverses its root even with followlinks=False;\n            # nested directory links remain opaque, and _unlink_cache still rejects this root.\n            state[\".venv\"] = \"link:\" + str(venv.readlink())\n    except FileNotFoundError:\n        return state\n    except OSError:\n        return {\".venv\": UNREADABLE}\n\n    def unreadable_directory(error: OSError) -> None:\n        # os.walk otherwise silently skips failed scandir calls, hiding newly planted caches.\n        path = Path(error.filename) if error.filename is not None else venv\n        state[path.relative_to(root).as_posix()] = UNREADABLE\n\n    for directory, names, files in os.walk(venv, onerror=unreadable_directory):\n        for name in sorted([*names, *files]):\n            path = Path(directory) / name\n            relative = path.relative_to(root).as_posix()\n            try:\n                if path.is_symlink():\n                    state[relative] = \"link:\" + str(path.readlink())\n                elif path.is_file():\n                    state[relative] = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()\n            except OSError:\n                state[relative] = UNREADABLE\n    return state\n",

          "excerpt": "def tool_problem(root: Path, before: dict[str, str] | None) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"The first path of `.venv/` that is not what the runner saw before the call, named; `None` when none is.\n\n    A new or content-changed regular file below an exact `__pycache__` component inside `.venv/` is\n    deleted before any runner-owned step: pytest's assertion rewriting writes bytecode there during\n    an attempt, and a deleted cache is rebuilt, so that write is normalized instead of refused (bead\n    coding-harness-q94b). Every other difference keeps the refusal with the first path named. The\n    baseline bookkeeping stays narrow: each successful unlink immediately removes that path's old\n    entry from the shared `before` dictionary, even if a later check fails. This records only the\n    runner's own deletions. Nothing that survives is rebaselined; recreated caches are deleted again.\n    \"\"\"\n    if before is None:\n        return None\n\n    def differences(now: dict[str, str]) -> list[str]:\n        return sorted(path for path in before.keys() | now.keys() if before.get(path) != now.get(path))\n\n    now = tool_state(root)\n    cleaned = False\n    for path in sorted(before.keys() | now.keys()):\n        if UNREADABLE in (before.get(path), now.get(path)):\n            return f\"`{path}` cannot be inspected, and a tool the attempt wrote is not run\"\n        if not _is_cache_path(path):\n            continue  # retain the difference, but still clean eligible caches that sort later\n        if before.get(path) == now.get(path):\n            continue\n        if before.get(path, \"\").startswith(\"link:\"):\n            continue  # removing a baseline symlink is never a cache-byte change\n        deleted = _unlink_cache(root, path)\n        if deleted is None:\n            continue  # a linked or non-regular cache-looking path stays a difference\n        if not deleted:\n            return f\"`{path}` cannot be deleted, and a tool the attempt wrote is not run\"\n        before.pop(path, None)  # record each runner-owned deletion even if a later check ",

          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "excerpt": "### Worktrees — one per change\n\nWritten 2026-09-29 from D-5 (worktrees in the repository, through the tool's own\nmechanism), ADR 0006 (parallel work, one worktree per session) and the\nmeasurement of 2026-09-23 (`docs/research/2026-09-23-worktree-tracker-writes.md`).\nThe same rule holds in `lakeswitch-ai`, with the differences its\n`docs/workflow.md` §9 lists.\n\n1. **One change, one bead, one branch, one worktree, one session.** Two sessions\n   never share a worktree, and nobody switches the branch of the main checkout\n   while another session runs.\n2. **In the repository, under `.claude/worktrees/<name>`.** That directory is in\n   `.gitignore` already, and it is where Claude Code puts its own worktrees\n   (`claude --worktree <name>`, and a sub-agent's `isolation: worktree`). By\n   hand: `git fetch origin && git worktree add -b <branch>\n   .claude/worktrees/<name> origin/main`. `bd worktree create` works as well but\n   writes the worktree's path into the tracked `.gitignore`, which is one more\n   change in the diff. Sibling directories beside the repository are retired\n   (D-5); worktrees that still sit there are finished and removed, not moved.\n3. **Always from a freshly fetched `origin/main`.** A worktree on a stale base\n   produces a pull request that is behind before it opens.\n4. **The tracker needs nothing.** `tools/bd` in a worktree finds the main\n   checkout's tracker through the shared git directory — no variable, no\n   redirect file, no copy. Concurrent writers lose nothing and a contested\n   claim has exactly one winner (measured 2026-09-23 with bd 1.3.0). Who may\n   write is house rule 4: the first writing session writes the tracker; every\n   other session claims its one bead with `tools/bd update <id> --claim\n   --actor <session>` and leaves its handover comment on that bead, nothing\n   more. After tracker writes: `tools/bd dolt push` first, `git push` second.\n5. **Omnigent starts inside the worktree.** Omnigent runs Claude Code as its\n   authors intend (`omnigent claude --use-native-config`, ADR 0006); the session\n   is started from the worktree's directory, so its hooks, its\n   `.claude/settings.json` and `tools/bd` all resolve there. Omnigent's own\n   tools reach the session as `mcp__omnigent__<tool>`, and neither Claude\n   Code's path rules, the hooks on its file tools nor Omnigent's own Claude Code\n   hook see what they do. Each one that writes, runs, spawns or changes state is\n   therefore denied by name in `.claude/settings.json`; the read-only ones stay\n   usable, except one that may send the task text to a routing judge\n   (`sys_advise_models`), which the user is asked about each time\n   (`permissions.ask`; decision of 2026-09-29). The one list, with a reason per\n   tool, is `scripts/omnigent_policy.py`. Read-only tools stay usable.\n   The default policy in `tools/omnigent/` is the second layer, rendered from\n   that same list. It refuses the denied ones and asks about the asked one\n   server-side for every Omnigent session on the machine. The\n   maintainer installs it, and nothing here depends on it alone (ADR 0006); as of\n   2026-09-29 it is built but not installed. Omnigent's bridge runs its own\n   `sys_os_*` tools without any policy while its relay does not advertise them,\n   and there only the rule in `.claude/settings.json` holds. Not yet measured: whether `omnigent claude`\n   started inside a worktree keeps that directory as the session's working\n   directory in every case.\n6. **After the merge, the worktree goes.** `git worktree remove\n   .claude/worktrees/<name>` and the branch with it. A worktree nobody works in\n   is a place where a later session finds an old state and takes it for the\n   current one.\n\nIsolation between sessions is a working agreement, not a wall: worktrees share\ngit's refs, hooks and configuration (`docs/architecture/2026-09-17-gap-analysis.md`).\nWhat really does not happen is simultaneous writing *to the same change* — that\nis not a tool question but a division of work.\n\n**What i",

          "excerpt": "## Q-3 · Any linked directory on a restored path refuses recovery\n\ncontext: |\n  Topic: recovery through a directory that is a symbolic link.\n  Intention: the phase-6 re-check found two more link chains (F6-5, F6-6)\n  after the Q-2 rule, the fourth and fifth of the same mechanism.\n  Today: only a link the attempt created or changed refuses the batch.\n  Repository change: the parent-chain check refuses any directory on a\n  restored path that is a symbolic link at the baseline or now; leaf aliases\n  stay as they are; spec terms, criteria 1 and 6 and a non-goal.\n  Architecture change: none; the structural fix is bead coding-harness-s9r.\nasked: 2026-10-27, conversation 2026-10-27\nanswer: \"Strenge Regel (Empfohlen)\"\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\n\nThe option chosen, as put to the maintainer (translated): Codex rebuilds the\ncheck so that any directory on the path that is a symbolic link refuses\nbefore anything is written; F6-5 and F6-6 close with it.           "excerpt": "## Terms\n\n- **Recovery operation:** restoration of an implementation or repair\n  attempt's snapshotted inputs or findings, recovery for time persistence,\n  or failed-call baseline rollback, including ignored-path cleanup.\n- **Unsafe parent:** an ancestor below the worktree root whose resolved\n  location is outside the canonical worktree root.           "end_line": 96,
          "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When any destination in a recovery batch has an unsafe parent, a\n   changed alias ancestor or a parent link, the operation refuses before its first\n   filesystem mutation.\n   *Refuted by:* a preceding safe destination, the alias itself, an external\n   sentinel or a cleanup target is created, rewritten, removed or stamped\n   before the unsafe destination stops the batch.\n\n2. If unsafe-parent recovery is refused, the runner terminates as a refusal\n   without another attempt, a fallback model or a checkpoint.\n   *Refuted by:* the command succeeds, returns an ordinary repairable\n   failure, starts another model, or advances HEAD with a runner checkpoint.\n\n3. When the runner refuses unsafe-parent recovery, its standard-error\n   diagnostic identifies the affected worktree-relative destination and\n   says that restoration was refused because its parent escapes the worktree.\n   *Refuted by:* standard error omits the path or reason, or reports only a\n   generic time-write or model-call failure.\n\n4. If a destination's parent chain cannot be resolved, recovery refuses\n   without mutation and ends the run with a diagnostic naming that path.\n   *Refuted by:* a resolution error or symlink loop permits recovery,\n   another model or a checkpoint, or escapes as an unnamed traceback.\n\n5. While a restoration safety refusal propagates, enclosing recovery,\n   diagnostic persistence and time finalization perform no filesystem writes.\n   *Refuted by:* a handler replaces the alias, restores findings, appends a\n   time entry, saves an attempt or runs further cleanup after the refusal.\n\n6. When parent chains are resolvable, remain inside the worktree and hold\n   no parent link, recovery retains the existing behavior for ordinary files, missing\n   directories, leaf aliases and hard links.\n   *Refuted by:* a safe retry loses trusted input bytes or measured time,\n   ordinary failed-call rollback stops working, or detaching a leaf alias or\n   hard link changes its external target.\n\n",

          "citation": "plans/changes/loop-record-other-worktree/decisions.md::Q-1 · What the runner does when a change continues in a new worktree",
          "end_line": 50,
          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · What the runner does when a change continues in a new worktree\n\nasked: 2026-11-18\nanswer: \"A: Ablösen per Befehl\" — in English: option A, supersede by command. The refusal names records of the same change found under other keys. A new form `release-loop <change> --restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>` lets the runner itself write one accounting line into findings.md (the superseded record's key, its rounds and the audit calls it accounts for) and move the old record into an archive beside the state directory; the next `review-loop` starts a fresh run. Accepted downside as shown with the option: exactly one command may read another worktree's key of the same change and mark it superseded; everywhere else each worktree's record stays private (R-2).\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: the review-loop record of a change that continues in a new worktree (bead coding-harness-e82i).\n  Intention: lane L4 (bead coding-harness-xul8, change pi-neutral-paths) is blocked: its second attempt runs in worktree pi-neutral-paths-v2, while the first attempt's loop record (rounds 1 to 3, never released) sits under the key of the old worktree pi-neutral-paths. Every re-sliced lane (L1, L2 of the same night) can hit the same trap.\n  Today: the record key is the change name plus the first eight hex digits of the sha256 of the worktree path (record_key in scripts/stage2.py), so each worktree's record is private (R-2 of the 2026-10-20 runner review). No verb looks across keys. findings.md of the new worktree carries the old attempt's seven review-loop audit lines but none of its rounds, so review-loop, release-loop and `release-loop --restart` refuse, and the refusal only says the record may sit \"under another state directory\". docs/WORKFLOW.md asks the maintainer to reconcile by hand but names no form; every line the runner accepts is runner output and would state something false here.\n  Repository change: scripts/stage2.py (the refusal names other keys of the same change; release-loop gains the supersede form), tests, docs/WORKFLOW.md §4 (loop record).\n  Architecture change: one command may read another worktree's record key of the same change and mark it superseded; the privacy of each worktree's record stays otherwise.\n  Options shown: A supersede by command (recommended); B only name the other records in the refusal (L4 stays blocked); C key by change and branch instead of worktree path (changes R-2 isolation and the key in three places); D like A but the old record stays in place, only marked (the old worktree could later continue its loop by mistake).\n\nIn the context of a change whose review loop continues in a new worktree\nwhile the old worktree's record stays under its own key, facing a refusal\nthat no honest hand line can pass and a doctrine that names no form for the\nmaintainer's reconciliation, we decided that the runner names records of the\nsame change under other keys and supersedes one through\n`release-loop --restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`, writing the\naccounting line itself and archiving the old record, to achieve a restart\nthat the runner records truthfully and that no other worktree can continue by\nmistake, accepting that exactly one command reads across worktree keys of the\nsame change. — 2026-11-18\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When `python3 scripts/stage2.py session <change> --model <id>` runs in the\n   change's dedicated worktree, it accepts the declared supported model.\n   *Refuted by:* no session parser, or dispatch from the main checkout,\n   detached HEAD or a different root than the validated change.\n2. If the endpoint/model declaration is absent, ambiguous, unreadable or\n   disallows framework content, the command refuses before terminal dispatch.\n   *Refuted by:* an unknown model, unapproved transport, missing residency\n   or malformed declaration reaching the terminal stand-in.\n3. When the handover is supplied, its actual text becomes the first prompt;\n   otherwise the change-local `handover.md` is used.\n   *Refuted by:* an empty/missing/unreadable/nonregular file being accepted,\n   only a pathname being sent, or an unrelated handover silently selected.\n   Prompts over 32 KiB UTF-8 or containing NUL refuse before dispatch; the\n   complete dispatch command is bounded to 64 KiB to fit the launch transport.\n4. If a handover path resolves outside the validated worktree, it is refused.\n   *Refuted by:* traversal or a symlink sending outside-file text to a model.\n5. When dispatch succeeds, a findings audit names date, requested model,\n   endpoint, handover source and the measured file/commit/rule counts.\n   *Refuted by:* missing or invented counts, wrong model, lost prior findings\n   or an audit indistinguishable from a completed review verdict.\n8. If dispatch fails after clean preflight, the command returns failure and\n   records a failed dispatch rather than claiming an interactive model ran.\n   *Refuted by:* denied automation or terminal dispatch failure\n   returning success or leaving a success-only audit.\n   A missing CLI/terminal executable is a prerequisite refusal (exit 2).\n   Successful Terminal acceptance is exit 0, not a CLI-start acknowledgment;\n   a subsequent CLI/login/model failure is reported in the new window.\n9. When a supported model is launched, the terminal runs the official CLI\n   interactively with that model and the checked worktree as its directory.\n   *Refuted by:* a non-interactive Pi mode (`--print`, `--mode`),\n   `codex exec`, any `opencode` call, wrong cwd, automatic fallback, or a\n   runner waiting for the interactive session to terminate.\n10.           "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When an implement or repair attempt's cheap ruff lint or format check\n   returns non-zero, that attempt fails before `make verify` starts.\n   *Refuted by:* a recorded full verification for that red attempt, or an\n   accepted attempt with remaining lint or format violations.\n\n2. When an implement or repair attempt's selected pytest run returns\n   non-zero, that attempt fails before `make verify` starts.\n   *Refuted by:* full verification or acceptance after an assertion,\n   collection or other pytest error in the selected run.\n\n3. When an implement or repair attempt reaches cheap pytest, its explicit\n   targets equal the selected tests defined above.\n   *Refuted by:* omitting a new or modified test function, a ledger test\n   (including one marked not yet written) or, on a retry, a test the\n   previous attempt reported as failed; selecting a whole changed file that\n   is not new, an importer, a deleted test file or unrelated discovery also\n   refutes it. (Amended 2026-10-28, `decisions.md#Q-3`.)\n\n4. If a cheap command's target set is empty, that command is skipped.\n   *Refuted by:* invoking ruff or pytest without explicit targets, or\n   refusing an otherwise valid text-only attempt merely for having none.\n\n5. When an attempt passes its applicable cheap checks, full `make verify`\n   remains required for acceptance.\n   *Refuted by:* a checkpoint after cheap green without full verification,\n   or acceptance despite red full verification or existing answer checks.\n\n6. When a cheap check rejects an attempt, its identified command, exit or\n   timeout and actual failure output enter the existing protected diagnostic\n   path for that attempt's findings block and any next attempt's prompt.\n   *Refuted by:* losing a short planted failure message, substituting a\n   generic failure summary, exposing a planted credential, recording a\n   successful verdict, or using a new retry route or extra model call.\n\n7. When an implement or repair prompt is built, it identifies the accepted\n   ledger's test references and requires them and ruff before handback for\n   command-capable models, with execution explicitly delegated to the runner\n   for file-only models.\n   *Refuted by:* a missing test reference, absent must-run instruction, a\n   command instruction without a file-only delegation, or extra model tools.\n\n8. When an implement or repair attempt edits its findings file, the findings\n   snapshot is restored before checks assess the remaining work, without\n   the edit alone causing rejection.\n   *Refuted by:* a retry solely for that edit despite valid code and answer,\n   forged findings reaching checks, loss of earlier evidence, or loss of\n   unrelated valid code during restoration.\n\n9. When findings restoration occurs, the attempt's quoted bookkeeping\n   records that restoration with the actual accepted or rejected outcome.\n   *Refuted by:* an invisible restore, a passing restored attempt labelled\n   failed, a fabricated review row, or the notice erasing an audit or an\n   earlier attempt's evidence.\n\n10. When a cheap check cannot start or exceeds its bounded execution time,\n    the attempt cannot be accepted as cheap-green.\n    *Refuted by:* reaching full verification or a checkpoint as though the\n    command passed, or a command running without the runner's time bound.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When any destination in a recovery batch has an unsafe parent, a\n   changed alias ancestor or a parent link, the operation refuses before its first\n   filesystem mutation.\n   *Refuted by:* a preceding safe destination, the alias itself, an external\n   sentinel or a cleanup target is created, rewritten, removed or stamped\n   before the unsafe destination stops the batch.\n\n2. If unsafe-parent recovery is refused, the runner terminates as a refusal\n   without another attempt, a fallback model or a checkpoint.\n   *Refuted by:* the command succeeds, returns an ordinary repairable\n   failure, starts another model, or advances HEAD with a runner checkpoint.\n\n3. When the runner refuses unsafe-parent recovery, its standard-error\n   diagnostic identifies the affected worktree-relative destination and\n   says that restoration was refused because its parent escapes the worktree.\n   *Refuted by:* standard error omits the path or reason, or reports only a\n   generic time-write or model-call failure.\n\n4. If a destination's parent chain cannot be resolved, recovery refuses\n   without mutation and ends the run with a diagnostic naming that path.\n   *Refuted by:* a resolution error or symlink loop permits recovery,\n   another model or a checkpoint, or escapes as an unnamed traceback.\n\n5. While a restoration safety refusal propagates, enclosing recovery,\n   diagnostic persistence and time finalization perform no filesystem writes.\n   *Refuted by:* a handler replaces the alias, restores findings, appends a\n   time entry, saves an attempt or runs further cleanup after the refusal.\n\n6. When parent chains are resolvable, remain inside the worktree and hold\n   no parent link, recovery retains the existing behavior for ordinary files, missing\n   directories, leaf aliases and hard links.\n   *Refuted by:* a safe retry loses trusted input bytes or measured time,\n   ordinary failed-call rollback stops working, or detaching a leaf alias or\n   hard link changes its external target.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Terms\n\n- **Recovery operation:** restoration of an implementation or repair\n  attempt's snapshotted inputs or findings, recovery for time persistence,\n  or failed-call baseline rollback, including ignored-path cleanup.\n- **Unsafe parent:** an ancestor below the worktree root whose resolved\n  location is outside the canonical worktree root. Relative links, links at\n  any ancestor depth and links to missing external targets count too.\n- **Recovery batch:** every destination a recovery operation can mutate;\n  checking a safe prefix of the batch does not authorize partial recovery.\n- **Changed alias ancestor:** an ancestor below the worktree root of a\n  recovery destination that is a symbolic link the attempt created or\n  changed, or that was a symbolic link at the attempt's baseline and is no\n  longer the same link. The attempt's own links in a parent chain are never\n  simulated: their presence alone makes the batch unsafe (Q-2, 2026-10-24).\n- **Parent link:** an ancestor below the worktree root of a recovery\n  destination that is a symbolic link now or was one at the attempt's\n  baseline, changed or not. Since Q-3 (2026-10-27) a parent link alone makes\n  the batch unsafe, whatever it resolves to; leaf aliases are not parent\n  links.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When any no-record refusal for the loop, restart, stage retirement, preparation or triage finds active loop records for the same change under other worktree keys in the current state directory, it names each such key.\n   *Refuted by:* a matching key is omitted, or another change's key or an archive is named.\n2. When the maintainer runs `release-loop <change> --restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>` for eligible other-worktree records, repeating `--supersedes <key>` for every active other key, the runner writes one `Loop restarted: <date> after round <N> — ...` accounting line to the current findings naming each key, each record’s round-number range and archive subdirectory expressed as `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/coding-harness/stage2-superseded/<change>@<superseding-digest>@<UTC timestamp>/<key>`, the count of all pending review-loop audit calls since the last release or restart, and the reason; N is the highest round ever assigned, including superseded rounds, released rounds, the current round count and the previous restart floor.\n   *Refuted by:* the line is absent, duplicated, or misstates any of those facts.\n3. When supersession succeeds, all selected records and the other non-research entries that release would delete, including `availability.json`, are preserved unchanged in one unique archive directory under `<state>/coding-harness/stage2-superseded/`, and are no longer active at their old keys.\n   *Refuted by:* its contents are lost or altered, or the old key can continue that record.\n4. When supersession succeeds, the next review loop starts fresh and each subsequent round, including after release, is numbered N plus the number of rounds run since the restart plus one.\n   *Refuted by:* the old snapshot or consumed stages are reused, or a round is misnumbered or a prior round number recurs.\n5. If the requested key is invalid, belongs to another change or the current worktree, is missing without an unfinished archived supersession or unreadable, the complete active and unfinished key set is not named, the current worktree has an active record, the reason is blank, or the flags are incompatible, supersession refuses without changing findings or any record.\n   *Refuted by:* an invalid request succeeds or changes findings or record state.\n6. While either worktree's loop record is in use, supersession does not alter it or its findings.\n   *Refuted by:* a competing run and supersession can both change either protected record or findings.\n7. If supersession is interrupted or an archive or write fails and its key set and readability remain unchanged, retry safely completes without losing records or duplicating accounting, using a staged archive with a manifest of the complete key set and the superseding worktree key, finalized before accounting; retry completes only the same key set started by that worktree.\n   *Refuted by:* a fault leaves the record irretrievable, a restart line while its record remains active at the old key, duplicate accounting on retry, an omitted key after a partial move, or one worktree completing another worktree’s archive.\n8. When a loop record is superseded, research state, research receipts and probe audits beside it remain at their original key unchanged.\n   *Refuted by:* any such item moves, disappears or changes.\n9.           "excerpt": "## Alternatives\n\n- Launch the TUI in the runner's terminal: fewer parts, but takes the\n  maintainer out of the orchestrating session and keeps the runner attached.\n- Dispatch a safely quoted command to macOS Terminal: the runner returns\n  after acceptance, the maintainer works independently, and the audit says\n  exactly that. Later startup errors stay visible in the new window.\n\nChosen: Terminal dispatch, as requested. No program-start handshake is added:\nthe maintainer accepted that boundary in F-2. A helper handles mechanics while\n`stage2.py` remains the sole public model-launch entry.\n\n",

          "end_line": 79,
          "excerpt": "## Interfaces\n\n- Public CLI: `stage2.py session <change> --model <id> [--handover <path>]`.\n  No stage-2-off bypass. Canonical worktree/cwd checked against git's common\n  directory; attached branch required. Unsupported platforms refuse.\n- Declaration: `openai-codex` uses its exact listed model via Codex;\n  `opencode-go/<model>` requires endpoint `opencode-go` to list the bare\n  `<model>` in `modelle` (as ADR 0011 declares it) and selects Pi (Q-5); Pi\n  gets the full ID. No aliases, suffix guessing or reviewer ordering.\n- Shared preflight: the helper receives the invoking runner module explicitly\n  and uses its `preflight`, `checked_prompt`, `foreign_env`, findings helpers\n  and exception types, avoiding duplicated classes under `__main__`.\n- Pi: `require_pi` first (exactly 1.1.0, else refuse before dispatch). The\n  runner writes one policy extension into a fresh private directory under\n  `.stage2-sessions/` and starts Pi with `--no-extensions` and `-e <that\n  file>` (discovery off, exactly one extension), `--offline`, `--no-approve`\n  and `--model <full id>`. The extension's `tool_call` handler blocks `read`,\n  `grep`, `find`, `ls`, `edit` and `write` on a path outside the worktree\n  and blocks writes to its own file, `.stage2-sessions/` and `.pi/` (Q-3);\n  it asks through the UI before a `bash` call that matches a dangerous\n  pattern (Q-2, as Pi's shipped `permission-gate.ts` does) and blocks that\n  call when no UI exists; a failing handler blocks the call. Pi has no\n  sub-agent and no web-fetch tool, so there is nothing to deny for them.\n- Read-back: the runner confirms that the extension *loaded* (its flag shows\n  in `pi --help` with discovery off; Q-1). Behaviour is held by handler tests\n  run without Pi and without a model. Whether the handlers act inside a live\n  Pi is not checked at launch; this is the weaker guarantee the maintainer\n  chose knowingly. A second prompt scan precedes GUI dispatch.\n- Sign-in: Pi reads `<agent dir>/auth.json`, default `~/.pi/agent`, which the\n  maintainer fills with `/login` (Q-6). The runner reads nothing from it,\n  hands over no key and sets no `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`; the environment\n  allow-list must carry what Pi needs to find that directory, which package 7\n  measures on the Mac.\n- Terminal: fixed AppleScript source receives the shell command as argv data;\n  `cd`, `env -i` variables and CLI arguments are separately shell-quoted.\n  No caller tokens/model overrides. Codex uses workspace-write, on-request\n  approval and `--no-daemon`; Pi takes the full handover text as its\n  positional prompt after the options, Codex after `--`. Bound prompt/command\n  arguments.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · What the runner does when a restore path resolves outside the worktree\n\ncontext: |\n  Topic: the runner's restore of a failed attempt's inputs, when a parent\n  directory inside the worktree was replaced by a symbolic link.\n  Intention: a runner audit reproduced a write outside the worktree through\n  such a link (bead coding-harness-10w).\n  Today: the restore replaces the link with a directory and continues.\n  Repository change: the restore refuses before writing; a test proves no\n  outside write.\n  Architecture change: none.\nasked: 2026-10-22, conversation 2026-10-22 (joint window)\nanswer: \"refuse and stop: write nothing, name the path, end the run without a fallback model, like a leak-check BLOCK\"\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\n\nIn the context of the runner's restore of a failed attempt, facing a parent\ndirectory replaced by a symbolic link that resolves outside the worktree, we\ndecided that the runner refuses and stops without writing, names the path\nand starts no fallback model, to achieve that no attempt can make the runner\nwrite outside its worktree, accepting that such a run ends and needs the\nmaintainer. — 2026-10-22\n\n",

          "excerpt": "# Spec — loop-record-other-worktree\n\nA maintainer can explicitly supersede a review-loop record left in another worktree and start a fresh run without losing its history (bead coding-harness-e82i). Research: `research.md`. Decision: `decisions.md#Q-1`.\n\n## Problem\n\nOn 2026-11-18 research found that a record is keyed by the resolved worktree path, so continuing a change in another worktree leaves its prior record invisible; the missing-record refusal names another state directory but not another worktree. The 2026-11-17-a night run parked a lane on this refusal; its findings held audit calls but no released rounds, so the existing restart could not account for them (`research.md`, incident and recovery paths).\n\n## Terms\n\n**Record key:** the change name and digest identifying one worktree's state directory. **Supersede:** archive the selected old loop record and account for it before a fresh run. **Other worktree keys:** keys derived from the currently listed worktrees of this repository; worktrees no longer listed by git and other repositories are excluded. A worktree still listed by git remains eligible even if its directory is gone.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When any no-record refusal for the loop, restart, stage retirement, preparation or triage finds active loop records for the same change under other worktree keys in the current state directory, it names each such key.\n   *Refuted by:* a matching key is omitted, or another change's key or an archive is named.\n2. When the maintainer runs `release-loop <change> --restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>` for eligible other-worktree records, repeating `--supersedes <key>` for every active other key, the runner writes one `Loop restarted: <date> after round <N> — ...` accounting line to the current findings naming each key, each record’s round-number range and archive subdirectory expressed as `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/coding-harness/stage2-superseded/<change>@<superseding-digest>@<UTC timestamp>/<key>`, the count of all pending re",

          "excerpt": "## Terms\n\n- **Recovery operation:** restoration of an implementation or repair\n  attempt's snapshotted inputs or findings, recovery for time persistence,\n  or failed-call baseline rollback, including ignored-path cleanup.\n- **Unsafe parent:** an ancestor below the worktree root whose resolved\n  location is outside the canonical worktree root.           "excerpt": "## Non-goals\n\n- Changing routing, attempt limits, verification or checkpoint policy for\n  runs without a restoration safety refusal.\n- Rejecting a leaf-file alias solely because its target is external when\n  its parents are contained and existing recovery safely detaches the leaf.\n- Recovering a batch whose parent chains hold a parent link, changed or\n  unchanged, even when every link in it would resolve inside the worktree:\n  such a run is refused, accepting that a linked directory in the worktree\n  blocks every recovery through it (Q-2, Q-3).\n- OS-level isolation or race-proofing against concurrent filesystem mutation.\n- Extending this fix to draft, review or unrelated runner verbs.\n- A design document or ADR: phase 2b does not run for this bounded change.\n\n",

          "reference": "Non-goals",
          "start_line": 97,

        {
          "citation": "plans/changes/isolated-attempts/decisions.md::Q-3 · Environment in the attempt worktree",
          "end_line": 70,
          "excerpt": "## Q-3 · Environment in the attempt worktree\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — the attempt worktree links the lane's .venv and installed Pi; a lane without them is refused before the model call with the remedy (make venv, tools/pi/install.sh); the runner checksums the shared environment before and after each attempt and rejects the attempt on a difference.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: where an attempt worktree gets its Python environment and Pi.\n  Intention: without the pinned Pi about 110 tests fail and an attempt goes red for an environment reason (0zhf attempts 2 and 3, 2026-11-22).\n  Today: the lane worktree carries both.\n  Repository change: Options: A link the lane's environment; B fresh install per attempt; C copy per attempt.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of the attempt environment, facing links, fresh installs or copies, we decided to link the lane's environment with a before-and-after checksum, to achieve seconds per attempt and the same environment for every attempt, accepting that a changed environment rejects the attempt instead of being repaired. — 2026-11-22\n\n",
          "kind": "local",

When the maintainer runs `release-loop <change> --restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>` for eligible other-worktree records, repeating `--supersedes <key>` for every active other key, the runner writes one `Loop restarted: <date> after round <N> — ...` accounting line to the current findings naming each key, each record’s round-number range and archive subdirectory expressed as `${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/coding-harness/stage2-superseded/<change>@<superseding-digest>@<UTC timestamp>/<key>`, the count of all pending review-loop audit calls since the last release or restart, and the reason; N is the highest round ever assigned, including superseded rounds, released rounds, the current round count and the previous restart floor.\n   *Refuted by:* the line is absent, duplicated, or misstates any of those facts.\n3. When supersession succeeds, all selected records and the other non-research entries that release would delete, including `availability.json`, are preserved unchanged in one unique archive directory under `<state>/coding-harness/stage2-superseded/`, and are no longer active at their old keys.\n   *Refuted by:* its contents are lost or altered, or the old key can continue that record.\n4. When supersession succeeds, the next review loop starts fresh and each subsequent round, including after release, is numbered N plus the number of rounds run since the restart plus one.\n   *Refuted by:* the old snapshot or consumed stages are reused, or a round is misnumbered or a prior round number recurs.\n5. If the requested key is invalid, belongs to another change or the current worktree, is missing without an unfinished archived supersession or unreadable, the complete active and unfinished key set is not named, the current worktree has an active record, the reason is blank, or the flags are incompatible, supersession refuses without changing findings or any record.\n   *Refuted by:* an invalid request succeeds or changes findings or record state.\n6. While either worktree's loop record is in use, supersession does not alter it or its findings.\n   *Refuted by:* a competing run and supersession can both change either protected record or findings.\n7. If supersession is interrupted or an archive or write fails and its key set and readability remain unchanged, retry safely completes without losing records or duplicating accounting, using a staged archive with a manifest of the complete key set and the superseding worktree key, finalized before accounting; retry completes only the same key set started by that worktree.\n   *Refuted by:* a fault leaves the record irretrievable, a restart line while its record remains active at the old key, duplicate accounting on retry, an omitted key after a partial move, or one worktree completing another worktree’s archive.\n8. When a loop record is superseded, research state, research receipts and probe audits beside it remain at their original key unchanged.\n   *Refuted by:* any such item moves, disappears or changes.\n9.           "excerpt": "## Q-5 · A failed model call\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — implement the 2026-10-16 decision: a failed model call (error, time or usage limit) counts as a failed attempt and falls through to the next route, building on its saved state; the switch and its reason stand visibly in findings.md; the doctrine sentence in docs/WORKFLOW.md §3 is amended with an ADR addendum. A leak refusal still never falls back.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: what follows a model call that ends without an answer.\n  Intention: on 2026-11-22 two u1ha repairs stopped at the Codex usage limit and Sonnet had to be started by hand.\n  Today: the call stops; docs/WORKFLOW.md §3 says a failed model process stops instead of silently changing route.\n  Repository change: Options: A fall through on every failed call except a leak refusal; B only for known causes; C keep stopping.\n  Architecture change: the §3 doctrine sentence, with an ADR addendum.\n\nIn the context of failed model calls, facing a stop or a visible fall-through, we decided to fall through to the next route with the reason recorded, to achieve night runs that do not stall, accepting that an unknown failure is answered by the next route instead of a stop. — 2026-11-22\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "plans/changes/isolated-attempts/decisions.md",
          "reference": "Q-5 · A failed model call",
          "start_line": 86,
          "supported": true,

        {
          "citation": "plans/changes/isolated-attempts/decisions.md::isolated-attempts — Decisions",
          "end_line": 129,
          "excerpt": "# isolated-attempts — Decisions\n\nClass: architectural (bead coding-harness-s9r; it changes how every writing verb of the runner runs a model and amends the doctrine sentence in `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3). The interview ran in the conversation on 2026-11-22; the answers are recorded below with the options as they were put. Earlier decisions it builds on: the shared design of 2026-10-16 (beads coding-harness-6ie and coding-harness-s9r), the design of 2026-11-12 that folded coding-harness-c99h, -t3s3, -znc and -6ie into this bead, and the retention answer of 2026-11-03 (coding-harness-c99h Q-1).\n\n## Q-1 · Direction: own worktree per attempt, or the three-way comparison\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — open the lane now on the 2026-11-12 design, without the three-way comparison of 2026-10-23; the orchestrator re-checks it against the alternatives.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: how a writing attempt is isolated.\n  Intention: a failed attempt leaves its changes in the lane worktree and the next step trips over them; on 2026-11-22 this happened three times (u1ha, ttic, i76l).\n  Today: every attempt writes in the lane worktree.\n  Repository change: Options: A open now on the 2026-11-12 design (own git worktree per attempt from the fixed base, failed attempt saved as a side ref, fallback builds on it); B after Monday in a block with the maintainer; C first compare worktree, container (Podman/Docker) and k3s/OpenShift.\n  Architecture change: a new attempt lifecycle for all writing verbs.\n\nIn the context of writing attempts that damage the next one, facing a cheap per-attempt worktree or a heavier container or cluster, we decided to build the per-attempt worktree now, to achieve an end to the hand clean-up at the lowest cost, accepting that network access and foreign file reads are not covered by this change. — 2026-11-22\n\nThe orchestrator's re-check: the worktree covers the damage class (lane and runner inputs) at seconds per attempt; a container adds a network lock and blocks foreign reads but needs a Linux VM on macOS and stalled on 2026-10-15 (branch explore/isolated-attempts); k3s/OpenShift is heavier still. A container can later sit on top of the worktree (bead coding-harness-yw2p).\n\n## Q-2 · Threat model\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — an attempt may damage its own worktree in any way (delete, edit, symlink, replace inputs); the lane and every file the runner reads its next prompt from stay untouched; network access and reading foreign files are out of scope, with their own bead (coding-harness-yw2p).\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: which model behaviour the runner must withstand.\n  Intention: the spec states the threat model (bead).\n  Today: no stated mod",

          "excerpt": "## Decision Drivers\n\n* No Z.ai budget is spent on repairs.\n* Every taken finding still carries the existing evidence and checkpoint guards.\n* A re-check receives no repair-session history.\n* An unavailable Codex call does not silently switch the repair budget.\n* The earlier routing decision remains readable as superseded history.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "docs/adr/0017-codex-repairs-taken-findings.md",
          "reference": "Decision Drivers",
          "start_line": 48,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "docs/adr/0017-codex-repairs-taken-findings.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 120,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"Codex repairs both kinds, with a fresh Codex re-check\",\nbecause it implements the maintainer's model choice without weakening the\nrepair evidence contract.\n\n1. **Codex repairs all taken findings in one batch** through `python3\n   scripts/stage2.py repair <change>`: loop-record rows, released loop rows\n   and phase-6 findings. Each Codex attempt starts `gpt-6.1-sol` at effort\n   `max` in a fresh session, with the existing `workspace-write` configuration,\n   hooks and memories off, and no added directory, automatic approval or\n   bypass. Repair reads no GLM key and never routes to `glm-coding-plan`.\n2. **Only post-run failures advance the chain:** Codex; a fresh Codex attempt\n   with the first attempt's diagnostics; Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` on\n   Stage 1 with both diagnostics. A model call failure stops; with unchanged\n   HEAD, the existing restoration returns the worktree to baseline. When\n   Codex is unavailable, the orchestrator deliberately starts\n   `--stage2-off <reason>`, which uses Sonnet alone and records why. A\n   declaration refusal or leak-check BLOCK stops without fallback.\n3. **The orchestrator decides, the verb repairs, the reviewer re-checks.**\n   The orchestrator writes `taken — <reason>` or `rejected — <reason>`, or\n   takes a finding no test can show as `taken — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Repair keeps those inputs, requests one fixed line per row and a measured\n   time entry, and starts no review. The runner checks each exact prompt,\n   prepares and formats the result, runs `make verify`, checks the time and\n   evidence, writes statuses and makes one clean descendant checkpoint.\n   A Codex call that moves HEAD stops before restoration or a runner commit.\n4. **The existing proof and statuses stand.** A code finding requires a\n   defined test the runner demonstrates red against baseline code; a finding\n   taken as `not a test` is proven by the separate re-check. Fixed rows read\n   `fixed — tests/<path>::<function>` or `fixed — not a test — <reason>`.\n   Failed attempts retain their audit, quoted diagnostics and changed-file\n   evidence, while their model-written statuses are restored. Private loop\n   rows are marked only after the checkpoint; unreleased rows reach the\n   repair in the prompt rather than a worktree file.\n5. **The same model may repair phase-6 findings; a fresh session re-checks.**\n   A phase-6 verdict after an earlier `## Phase 6` block in `findings.md` — a\n   re-check — runs Codex read-only without resuming the repair, a prior\n   verdict or a historical phase-2a session; the first phase-6 review keeps\n   the resume rule of ADR 0016. Loop marks may\n   resume only that new verdict thread after its verdict. This replaces ADR\n   0015's blanket reviewer/repairer separation; it does not give review calls\n   write tools or move any review to another model.\n6. **The loop budget and run count stand.** A fixed row counts as taken;\n   round 3 requires a taken or fixed row in round 2, and the maximum stays\n   three rounds. The orchestrator writes `Broke a test` from the repair\n   evidence before the next round or release. Audit lines and historical GLM\n   counts retain their format. Initial implementation, Explore and draft's\n   GLM fallback retain their models.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30.
